Terms used in this page (open once)
field-line style, axisymmetric style
The two vacuum methods, vac%style 1 and 2. Style 1 (VMEC) is the 3-D boundary-element method on the points of the field lines; style 2 (HELENA) integrates over ζ analytically with toroidal functions and over θ numerically.
BC_style
Boundary conditions. Its first value is the inner end and has to be 1; its second value is the plasma edge: 1 fixed, 2 free through the variational surface energy. Until #36 (D) the edge could also be 4, free through an explicit natural-boundary-condition row.
norm_disc_prec_sol, p
The order p of the radial finite differences of the eigenvalue problem, 3 by default. The derivative at a radial point is a left difference: it uses that point and the p points on the axis side of it. Until #36 (D) the input norm_disc_style_sol could choose central differences over 2p + 1 points instead.
end weights
The weights, in units of the radial step h, of the last points of a free edge in the sum that replaces the radial integral of the energy: 6/11, 108/121, 1.0143, … for p = 3, and 1 further inside (cba0762, D). Your edge note calls them the consistent weights.
vac_diag_style
How the diagonals of the vacuum matrices G and H are computed: 1 indirect (from identities), 2 direct (corner term and cell integral). New input.
X, p
X = ξ·∇ψ, PB3D's normal displacement; p the parallel angle along a field line (θ for poloidal flux). A mode: X ∝ ei(nα + (nq−m)p).
EP, res
EP: the normal data of the vacuum potential for each mode at the boundary points (in calc_vac_res). res = vac%res, the nmod × nmod vacuum response that enters the edge block of A; res(m, m) its diagonal element for poloidal mode m.
lines × points
A field-line vacuum grid: number of field lines × points per line, e.g. 128 × 121 on W7-X.
the circular cases
HELENA circular-cross-section equilibria with q from 1.04 (fixtures circ_eps005_q104, circ_eps033_q104, inverse aspect ratio 0.05 and 0.33); the n = 10 external kink is the free-boundary benchmark.
VMEC twin, rippled twin
The VMEC equilibrium made from the ε = 0.33 HELENA case (same plasma, VMEC++), and copies of it with a 5-fold ripple of amplitude δ (0.01 to 0.04): the 3-D tests of the field-line style.
cbm18a, cut cbm18a
The HELENA pedestal equilibrium of the regression decks (n = 10, edge at ψ = 0.75 in the free-boundary deck), and a version of it cut at the pedestal foot for the comparison with TERPSICHORE.
MISHKA-1, TERPSICHORE
The axisymmetric code you used in your PhD (rebuilt from Simulations/MISHKA/Sources), and the open-source 3-D stability code of EPFL (since 2025), run on Snellius.
check_vac, CHECKVAC
New input that makes PB3D test its vacuum operators with exact potentials on the real boundary; the results are log lines starting with CHECKVAC.
anchor, fixture
An eigenvalue recorded in a regression test, and an equilibrium file committed for the tests (tests/fixtures).
eigenvalue
ω²/ωA² in PB3D's MISHKA normalisation (norm_style 1), negative when unstable.
Snellius
The SURF cluster; the runs of 27 October on were made there.

How to use this page

  • Each section has a status (to do, in progress, done, question) and a notes box. They are saved with the page, so they survive reloads and other devices, and Claude can read your notes back in a later session. When the HTML is opened as a local file they are kept in that browser only.
  • Every code change is in the page, in the section that explains it, and always as one diff from 2.47 to 9e9aba5: each section lists its commits as cards (subject, message, what the commit's own diff holds), then shows each file those commits changed once, with only the blocks of changed lines (hunks) they touched. The vacuum modules are shown routine by routine in stage 5. The intermediate states are not shown; each commit's own diff is one click away on GitHub. Under each block are the commits that changed its lines; the ten blocks that commits of two sections changed appear in both.
  • Blocks of the non-vacuum modules carry a badge from a mechanical classifier: use-list, ldebug-guard, moved and the like mean the block only moves or renames lines and was checked by script; read means it changes what the code does.
  • Line numbers are those of 2.47 (left) and of 9e9aba5 (right). A click on a number opens that line on GitHub at that version. In VS Code, Cmd+P and vac_ops.f90:1537 opens the line in your checkout.
  • Two switches in the index: "hide comment-only diff lines" (a quarter of the changed lines in vac_ops are comments) and "hide mechanical hunks", which leaves only what the classifier could not decide. Right above the code of each section, one button opens the files that have a block to read and jumps to the first of them; "close all files" closes them again. The index marks the section you are reading.
  • Numbers: a number without a named source comes from the commit message of the commit the section is about. Other sources are named. Numbers from the demos and tools are produced by this page. Where I derived something for this page, the text says so.
  • demo blocks are small scripts in review/demos/. Each prints numbers and draws one figure; output and figure are in the page, so running them is optional.
  • Tiers: skim the change is checked by a tool or is trivial; read read the diff with the explanation; study work through the reasoning before reading the code.
  • Two appendices. A, optional: the first eigenvalue of nine decks at every commit, to look up which commit moved which number. L, the ledger: every commit that touched a Fortran module and where its change appears here; the build script stops with an error if any change is missing.

M1

PETSc/SLEPc 3.9 to 3.25 port

files SLEPC_ops, SLEPC_utilitiescommits 775219a, d4812f7, 1862df0time 15 minread

2.47 used the PETSc 3.9 Fortran interface and no longer builds against a current PETSc. The port changes calls, not what is computed: PetscBool optional arguments become logical, InsertMode gets its own type, MatSetValuesBlocked takes index arrays and a flattened block, PetscViewerSetFormat becomes push/pop, VecGetArrayF90 becomes VecGetArray, and MatInfo and PETSC_NULL_SCALAR_ARRAY are switched on PETSC_VERSION_GE(3,22,0).

Two hunks are more than renames:

  • An implicit SAVE, fixed. In the routine that removes faulty eigenvalues, 2.47 declared PetscBool :: remove_next_loc = .false.. An initialisation in a declaration gives the variable the SAVE attribute, so after one call with remove_next = .true. every later call without the argument also removed all following eigenvalues. The port sets it to .false. at the start of each call. The demo shows the Fortran rule. (Effect by reading of the code: it only matters in runs where PB3D discards eigenvalues; I did not construct such a case.)
  • MatCopy flag. 2.47 passed MAT_SHARE_NONZERO_PATTERN (a MatDuplicateOption) where a MatStructure is expected; the port passes SAME_NONZERO_PATTERN. In petscmat.h of PETSc 3.25.3 both names are the third entry of their enumeration (value 2), so this corrects the type, not the behaviour.
How to check it
  1. Read the code below the three cards; in their own diffs the classifier marks three hunks as mechanical (two renames of PetscBool, one debug guard); the rest are API changes to read once.
  2. The build at the tip and the regression anchors (S0) show that the ported calls work; 2.47 cannot be built with PETSc 3.25, so there is no before/after run of the port itself.

script
! Area 0a: the PETSc port fixed an implicit SAVE in SLEPC_ops (remove_next_loc).
!
! At 2.47 the local variable was declared as
!     PetscBool :: remove_next_loc = .false.
! An initialisation in a declaration gives the variable the SAVE attribute: it
! is initialised once, at program start, and keeps its value between calls.
! After one call with remove_next = .true., every later call without the
! argument still sees .true.. The port declares it without initialisation and
! sets it to .false. at the start of every call.
!
! Build and run:  gfortran implicit_save.f90 -o implicit_save && ./implicit_save
program implicit_save
    implicit none
    call as_247(.true.)
    call as_247()
    call as_247()
    print *
    call as_now(.true.)
    call as_now()
    call as_now()
contains
    subroutine as_247(remove_next)
        logical, intent(in), optional :: remove_next
        logical :: remove_next_loc = .false.        ! implies SAVE
        if (present(remove_next)) remove_next_loc = remove_next
        print '(a,l1,a,l1)', '2.47: argument present = ', present(remove_next), &
            &', remove_next_loc = ', remove_next_loc
    end subroutine as_247
    subroutine as_now(remove_next)
        logical, intent(in), optional :: remove_next
        logical :: remove_next_loc
        remove_next_loc = .false.
        if (present(remove_next)) remove_next_loc = remove_next
        print '(a,l1,a,l1)', 'now:  argument present = ', present(remove_next), &
            &', remove_next_loc = ', remove_next_loc
    end subroutine as_now
end program implicit_save

commit message
The 2018-era PETSc 3.9.2 is no longer buildable on current platforms
(python2-era configure, predates Apple Silicon) and is no longer carried
by Spack, so the port forward is the only viable route.

Changes, all confined to the two SLEPc-facing modules:
* SLEPC_utilities: InsertMode is now a typed enum, not PetscInt;
  MatSetValuesBlocked requires rank-1 index arrays under the generated
  strict interfaces ([v] casts); PB3D-internal optional flags changed
  from PetscBool to plain logical (PetscBool is 1-byte logical(C_BOOL)
  since PETSc 3.24 and no longer matches default-kind literals).
* SLEPC_ops: MatInfo is a derived type instead of a real array
  (MAT_INFO_* index constants are gone); PETSC_NULL_SCALAR_ARRAY where
  an omitted array is passed (VecCreateMPIWithArray); MatCopy called
  with a proper MatStructure (SAME_NONZERO_PATTERN) instead of the
  MatDuplicateOption that the permissive old interface tolerated;
  VecGetArrayF90/VecRestoreArrayF90 replaced by VecGetArray/
  VecRestoreArray (F90-suffixed accessors removed in 3.25); fixed a
  latent implicit-SAVE bug on remove_EV's remove_next_loc default.
* spack.yaml: modern stack (petsc@3.25 +complex, slepc@3.25), gcc
  preference and openmpi requirement; validated on macOS arm64.

Both executables build and run: 5/5 ctest (unit + smoke) passing.

commit message
The 2.48 port targeted PETSc/SLEPc 3.25; this makes the same code build
and pass tests against distro PETSc/SLEPc 3.19 (e.g. Ubuntu 24.04):

* MatSetValuesBlocked: pass values as 1-D (row-major-flattened) array,
  which all versions accept; the 2-D form only exists from 3.20 on.
* MatInfo: version guard between pre-3.22 array indexing and the
  derived type of the 3.22 Fortran overhaul.
* PETSC_NULL_SCALAR_ARRAY: version guard, introduced in 3.22.
* tests: when OpenMPI still ships the pt2pt osc component, use it for
  tests that run the executables; sandboxed containers break the
  default shared-memory/CMA one-sided path (MPI_Win_create fails even
  single-process).

Verified: full stack (apt PETSc/SLEPc 3.19-complex + PSPLINE +
minimal LIBSTELL + STRUMPACK-Dense 1.1.1) builds and all 5 ctest
tests pass on Linux.

Compiler-warning cleanup

files 16 modulescommit 6ce5029time 15 minskim

The warning count of a full build went from 321 to 124 (commit message). Most hunks move a declaration that only debug builds use under #if ldebug, or trim a use list. The classifier marks those. The hunks left to read:

  • MPI_utilities, the lock logic: if (lock%blocking .or. wl_empty(...)) calls an impure function inside .or.. Fortran does not say whether the second operand is evaluated, so gfortran warns. The call now goes first into no_NB_running. Same result if the compiler evaluated both operands before; defined behaviour now.
  • Declarations split so that only the debug-only counters go under the guard (eq_ops, sol_ops), an unused rout_name removed (num_utilities), an error message shortened (input_ops).

The vacuum-module part of this commit is inside the vacuum routine diffs of stage 5.

How to check it: the card below gives the verdict for each hunk of the commit's own diff; read its blocks marked read below the card. A block can be marked read because another commit changed lines in it too: the commits under the block say which.
6ce50292026-07-10 quality: burn the compiler-warning baseline down from 321 to 124.
its own diff: 26 hunks: 7 to read, mechanical 8 ldebug-guard, 8 use-list, 3 whitespace in 14 files
its lines, 2.47 against 9e9aba5, below: HDF5_ops.f90:1566 HDF5_utilities.f90:106 HELENA_ops.f90:84 MPI_utilities.f90:912 MPI_utilities.f90:939 driver_POST.f90:1191 driver_POST.f90:1213 driver_eq.f90:52 driver_sol.f90:287 eq_ops.f90:455 eq_ops.f90:3357 eq_ops.f90:4294 eq_ops.f90:4526 eq_ops.f90:4578 eq_ops.f90:5304 eq_ops.f90:5338 eq_ops.f90:5850 files_ops.f90:180 input_ops.f90:885 messages.f90:275 num_utilities.f90:978 sol_ops.f90:151 sol_ops.f90:177 sol_ops.f90:1213 sol_utilities.f90:817

Its change to the vacuum modules is in the routine diffs of stage 5.

commit message
Investigation first: 157 of the 321 counted warnings were not ours - they
come from the vendored Libraries/dfft.f, which the CI counter's
grep -v Libraries/ can never exclude because gfortran prints the file
location on a separate line from the 'Warning:' line. The vendored
dfftpack target now compiles with -w (like foul already did), consistent
with the policy that vendored code is not ours to lint.

The genuinely-ours fixes, verified against both the Release and the
Debug + PB3D_ENABLE_DEBUG builds:

 - unused variables/imports that are used only inside #if ldebug blocks
   (the dominant pattern): their declarations and imports move into the
   guard, in HDF5_ops, HDF5_utilities, HELENA_ops, driver_POST, driver_eq,
   driver_sol, eq_ops, files_ops, messages, sol_ops, sol_utilities and
   vac_ops. eq_ops's ldebug-only helpers test_S_HEL and
   calc_derived_S_from_sigma_HEL are now compiled only under ldebug.
 - genuinely dead rout_name parameters (routines without CHCKERR) removed
   in num_utilities and vac_utilities.
 - MPI_utilities::lock_return_acc evaluated the impure function wl_empty
   inside an .or. expression, which Fortran allows the compiler to
   short-circuit away (-Wfunction-elimination); it is now evaluated into
   an explicit local first.
 - an overlong error message in input_ops (character truncation) and a
   real equality comparison in test_dtorh rewritten.

Bonus find: the Debug+ldebug build of the new multi-rank rows flagged an
out-of-bounds in solve_Phi_BEM's ldebug Phi-plot block - the angle array
was allocated per block-cyclic subrow but filled and sliced with global
indices, which only ever worked single-process where the whole matrix is
one block. The global angle array is now built once, spanning the full
boundary.

The baseline is now 124: 113 -Wmaybe-uninitialized (mostly -O3 false
positives, case-by-case review pending) and 11 interface-constrained
-Wunused-dummy-argument.

Verified: primary build 18/18 tests, Debug+ldebug 15/15 (incl. the
multi-rank rows that caught the plot bug), ScaLAPACK-fallback 9/9.

Lint: specific intrinsics

files dtorh, num_varscommit 17716c4time 5 minskim

The Fortran linter (fortitude, category OB, obsolescent features, now a CI gate) rejects the specific double-precision intrinsics. DSQRT, DABS, DLOG and datan became the generic sqrt, abs, log and atan. For real(dp) arguments the generic and the specific function are the same function. Every hunk of the commit's own diff is classified intrinsic: after replacing each specific name by its generic one, the removed and added lines are identical. Nothing to read unless you want to. The unit test unit_dtorh checks dtorh against reference values (also at n = 20 to 80, to 1.4e-11).

17716c42026-07-10 lint: clean the fortitude OB (obsolescent features) category and gate it.
its own diff: 10 hunks: 0 to read, mechanical 10 intrinsic in 2 files
its lines, 2.47 against 9e9aba5, below: dtorh.f90:118 dtorh.f90:140 dtorh.f90:198 dtorh.f90:256 dtorh.f90:329 dtorh.f90:339 dtorh.f90:367 dtorh.f90:545 dtorh.f90:564 num_vars.f90:83
commit message
The 16 findings were all type-specific intrinsics: DSQRT/DLOG/DABS in
dtorh.f90 and datan in num_vars.f90, replaced by their generic forms.
For double-precision arguments these are semantically identical; the
dtorh values are pinned by the unit tests against 30-digit mpmath
references (1e-11 relative), which still pass.

The lint CI job gains a blocking step for the cleaned category
(fortitude check --select=OB); the full report stays non-blocking. This
is the staged-adoption ratchet from Documentation/quality-and-ci.md:
one rule category at a time reaches zero, then may not regress.

Module splits for unit testing

files num_utilities → spline_utilities, HDF5_vars → var_1D_vars, and the use lines of 14 modulescommits 8ac37d7, 17b712c; var_1D_vars renamed flat_vars in 18f87e8time 10 minskim

The unit-test layer compiles parts of PB3D without PSPLINE and HDF5. For that, the PSPLINE wrapper spline moved out of num_utilities into a new module spline_utilities, and var_1D_type with dealloc_var_1D moved out of HDF5_vars into var_1D_vars (which HDF5_vars re-exports). Every caller's use num_utilities, only: spline became use spline_utilities, only: spline.

The checker below compares the removed lines with the new module line by line. Result: 339 of the 340 lines removed from num_utilities are in spline_utilities unchanged (the 340th is the public list, which lost spline), and 52 of 54 for var_1D_vars (the other two: the public list and a doc line that now says "1-D"). What is new in each module is boilerplate (header, module, use, private, public).

How to check it: read the checker's output below; the 37 use-list hunks of 8ac37d7 are the callers' use lines; read the remaining blocks below the cards (the public lists and the re-export in HDF5_vars).
tool review/tools/pure_move_check.py

script
"""Area M4: prove that the two module splits moved code without changing it.

Commit 8ac37d7 moved the PSPLINE wrapper `spline` out of num_utilities into
the new spline_utilities; commit 17b712c moved var_1D_type and
dealloc_var_1D out of HDF5_vars into the new var_1D_vars. For each split this
compares, after normalising whitespace, every non-blank line removed from the
old module with the lines of the new module, and lists what is NOT a pure
move in either direction (module boilerplate is expected there).

Run from the repository root:  python3 review/tools/pure_move_check.py
"""
import re
import os
import subprocess
from collections import Counter


os.chdir(subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], capture_output=True, text=True,
                      check=True, cwd=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))).stdout.strip())


def git(*a):
    return subprocess.run(["git", *a], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout


def lines(diff, sign):
    return [l[1:] for l in diff.splitlines() if l.startswith(sign) and not l.startswith(sign * 3)]


def norm(L):
    return [re.sub(r"\s+", " ", x).strip() for x in L if x.strip()]


for sha, old, new in (("8ac37d7", "Modules/num_utilities.f90", "Modules/spline_utilities.f90"),
                      ("17b712c", "Modules/HDF5_vars.f90", "Modules/var_1D_vars.f90")):
    d_old = git("show", "--format=", sha, "--", old)
    d_new = git("show", "--format=", sha, "--", new)
    rem, add_old = Counter(norm(lines(d_old, "-"))), Counter(norm(lines(d_old, "+")))
    add = Counter(norm(lines(d_new, "+")))
    not_moved = rem - add                       # removed but not found in the new module
    only_new = add - rem                        # in the new module but not removed from the old one
    print(f"== {sha}: {old} -> {new}")
    print(f"   {sum(rem.values())} non-blank lines removed from the old module, "
          f"{sum(add.values())} lines in the new module, {sum((rem & add).values())} identical")
    print("   removed but not in the new module:")
    for k, v in not_moved.items():
        print(f"      {k}" + (f"   (x{v})" if v > 1 else ""))
    print("   new lines (not moved):")
    for k, v in only_new.items():
        print(f"      {k}")
    print("   lines added to the old module:")
    for k in add_old:
        print(f"      {k}")

commit message
The spline wrappers (the only PSPLINE dependency of num_utilities) move
to a new module spline_utilities (34 use-sites updated), and num_ops's
output_ops (HDF5) dependency is confined to ldebug. This lets
num_utilities and num_ops join the dependency-light pb3d_core - with
LAPACK as a new optional core dependency for the 0-D determinant/
inverse/extrapolation - and be unit-tested without any scientific
stack.

New test-drive suites (tests/unit):
* num_utilities: trapezoidal integration vs analytic, finite-difference
  weights vs classical values, Bjorck-Pereyra Vandermonde solver,
  symmetric-storage indexing c/is_sym, bubble sort with pivots, LAPACK
  determinant/inverse on a known matrix, polynomial extrapolation
  (value and derivative), GCD/LCM/factorial.
* num_ops: Householder zero finder (orders 1-3) on x^2-2, Zhang
  bracketing finder on cos.

Both are skipped cleanly when LAPACK is absent (and num_ops also under
PB3D_ENABLE_DEBUG, where it needs HDF5 for debug plotting).

commit message
Second-stage expansion of the dependency-light core (roadmap item 5 of
Documentation/quality-and-ci.md):

 - var_1D_type (+ dealloc_var_1D, max_dim_var_1D) moves from HDF5_vars to
   the new light module var_1D_vars; HDF5_vars re-exports the names, so
   none of the users change. This removes PB3D_utilities' only HDF5
   dependency.
 - grid_vars, X_vars, var_1D_vars and PB3D_utilities join pb3d_core
   unconditionally; X_utilities joins when LAPACK is available (it uses
   num_utilities' index helper c).

New suites:

 - X_utilities: sec_ind_loc2tot (vectorial + tensorial), is_necessary_X
   (asymmetric always; symmetric on/below the diagonal in total indices,
   full range and subrange), get_sec_X_range pinning the worked example
   from its own documentation (subrange [2:3,2:5] of [1:5,1:5], both
   asymmetric and symmetric incl. the empty columns), and trim_modes.
 - PB3D_utilities: setup_par_id checked against its docstring formulas -
   most importantly the partition property: the per-level index sets of an
   interlaced Richardson parallel grid tile the grid exactly once; also
   par_lim windows (windowed indices = full-range points inside the
   window), per-level par_id_mem memory indices, setup_rich_id, and the
   conv_1D2ND column-major bounds/values roundtrip.

All green: light+sanitizer build 7/7 unit suites, primary 21/21,
ScaLAPACK-fallback 17/17, Debug+ldebug 18/18.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01H8BZacVBuLNqVN7fSsaw1V

Version number

file num_varscommit a8c07b6time 2 minskim

prog_version went from 2.47 to 2.48 in July. The README's newest changelog entry is 2.49 (October and November), but prog_version still says 2.48. POST refuses output written before the Nyquist change by the size of misc_in_V (R1), not by the version number, so nothing breaks; the number is just behind.

Decided. Set prog_version to 2.49 before the merge. Done in 18f87e8, together with min_PB3D_version 2.49.

commit message
* Added CTest-driven test suite in tests/, unit tests written in the
  vendored fortran-lang test-drive framework (v0.5.0, MIT/Apache-2.0).
* New CMake option PB3D_BUILD_EXECUTABLES (default ON): with OFF, only a
  dependency-light core library (num_vars, str_utilities, messages,
  files_utilities, dtorh) and its unit tests are built, requiring no
  external libraries beyond a Fortran compiler.
* First unit tests: dtorh toroidal harmonics validated against 30-digit
  mpmath references (54 points incl. the near-singular regime relevant
  for the vacuum BEM), degree recurrence, and error handling;
  str_utilities output formats pinned down.
* Added GitHub Actions workflow running the unit layer on every push.
* Committed the previously missing spack.yaml (was excluded by the
  *.yaml gitignore rule) with pinned known-good PETSc/SLEPc versions.
* Registered PB3D/POST usage smoke tests; verification awaits a full
  dependency-stack build.
* See Documentation/testing.md.

"Line as at 2.47 since": the commit in which the faulty line took the form it had at 2.47 (found with git log -S); an earlier form may have had the same error. The tag Weyens2017PB3D (v1.29, June 2016) contains none of these lines; the tag Weyens2018expressions (v2.37, 18 June 2018) contains all six. The implicit SAVE of M1 dates from v0.74 (April 2015) and is in both tags.

Verified on 16 November 2026: commit 1839ea0 "Stage 2 verified by toon" on dev/vacuum-fixes, pushed. What changed during this stage:
  • F3: the comments of redistribute_var and of the margin in redistribute_output_grid say what the code does, without its history. The margin is no longer a local ghost_interp = 20: num_vars holds the order of the radial interpolation, interp_V_ord = 3, and the margin computed from it, size_ghost_interp_V: 0 points for linear, 2 for Akima, ⌈ln ε / ln(2 − √3)⌉ = 28 for the cubic spline, whose end effect shrinks by 2 − √3 per equal interval. interp_V_spline takes as order the lower of interp_V_ord and what the points allow: 0 for one point (a copy), 1 for two or three, 3 for four or more, because PSPLINE's Akima and cubic splines both need four points. With the setting at 3 that is what the code did before. untrim_grid (grid_utilities) and get_ghost_arr with its four versions (MPI_utilities) were never called and are removed.
  • F4: read_VMEC takes B0 from the first Nyquist mode, after checking that it is (0,0), instead of searching all modes for it. The comment and the description of B_0_V say what B0 is, and the README gives the factors by which VMEC eigenvalues changed: 0.9839 for the circular twin, 1.064 for W7-X.

Checked before the commit: the full build on the Mac and ctest without the regression decks, 16 of 20, the four that fail being the _np2/_np4 full-stack rows that crash at start-up in the Mac's MPI launcher; interp_V_spline on its own for 1, 2, 3, 4 and 10 points (order, ivs_stat, exact on linear and cubic data). On Snellius, 18f87e8 against the stage-2 code: 27 of 27 tests in both, the regression decks and the _np2/_np4 rows included. With one process every eigenvalue is the same in all 16 digits (cbm18a fixed, cbm18a free with styles 2 and 4, the circular deck, the twin fixed and free, the last after the change of B0). With 2 and 4 processes cbm18a fixed moves by 3.7e−13 and 6.1e−13, from the margin of 28 instead of 20. Not checked: interp_V_ord set to 1 or 2. Left as they are: the header of set_BC_4 (F6) still cites "issue #4, step 4" and the 0.7 % gap from before F5.

F1

HELENA shear: the end condition of an odd spline

file eq_ops (calc_derived_q)commit 28f8dabtime 20 minstudy

For a HELENA equilibrium PB3D computes the magnetic shear as \(S = -\frac{1}{\mathcal{J}}\,\partial_\chi\!\left(h^{\alpha\psi}/h^{\psi\psi}\right)\) by fitting a cubic spline in χ and differentiating it (calc_derived_S_from_deriv_HEL). An up-down symmetric equilibrium (ias = 0) is stored on χ ∈ [0, π], so the spline needs a condition at both ends. The ratio \(h^{\alpha\psi}/h^{\psi\psi}\) is odd in χ: its slope is not zero at χ = 0 and π, its second derivative is. 2.47 passed bcs(:,1), the zero-slope condition of even quantities. The fix passes bcs(:,2), zero second derivative. One line; the other three hunks correct the comment "zero first derivative" next to bcs(:,2) = [2,2] in three places.

Effect. The zero-slope condition forced S to zero at both midplanes, χ = 0 and π. The cbm18a n = 10 fixed-boundary eigenvalue moved from −4.074e-2 to −4.357e-2, 6.5 % more unstable, and POST's energy balance closes to 0.08 %. The faulty argument dates from 18 June 2018 (b8c07f7, v2.36) and is in the code of the tag Weyens2018expressions. The demo shows that the error at the ends does not shrink with the number of poloidal points.

How to check it
  1. Read the change: bcs(:,1) → bcs(:,2) in the call for eq_2%S (below the card).
  2. Look at the demo: with the even condition the derivative error stays 0.86 at the ends for 33 to 257 points; with the odd one it falls as 1/N⁴.
  3. Independent evidence: the VMEC path does not use this spline, and the HELENA and VMEC versions of the circular ε = 0.33 case agree to 1e-4 in their fixed-boundary eigenvalue (test regression_circ_eps033_vmec_twin, TWIN_RTOL).
  4. Guard: regression_cbm18a_shear_HEL compares the shear S in the output file with the direct formula from the stored metric derivatives: deviation 0.79 with the even condition, 1.5e-5 with the odd one.

The wrong end condition forces the slope to 0 at chi = 0 and pi, where the
odd function has its largest slope: an O(1) error that does not shrink with
nchi at the ends and decays over a few intervals inward.
script
"""Area 2a: the HELENA shear and the end condition of an odd spline.

PB3D computes the magnetic shear of a HELENA equilibrium in
eq_ops.calc_derived_S_from_deriv_HEL as

    S = -(1/J) d/dchi (h^{alpha psi} / h^{psi psi}),

by fitting a cubic spline to h12/h22 over the poloidal grid chi_H and
differentiating it. For an up-down symmetric equilibrium (ias = 0) the grid
covers only the half period [0, pi], so the spline needs end conditions at
chi = 0 and chi = pi. h12/h22 is odd in chi. An odd function has a non-zero
slope at 0 and pi and a zero second derivative there.

At 2.47 the call passed bcs(:,1) = [1,1] (PSPLINE code 1: prescribed first
derivative, value 0), the condition for EVEN quantities. Commit 28f8dab passes
bcs(:,2) = [2,2] (code 2: prescribed second derivative, value 0).

This script repeats that with scipy's CubicSpline on a model odd function
and shows the error of the spline derivative with both end conditions.
"""
import numpy as np
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline

from _common import BLUE, ORANGE, plt, save


def model(chi):
    """An odd model of h12/h22 with a few harmonics (shape is not important)."""
    return 0.6 * np.sin(chi) + 0.25 * np.sin(2 * chi) - 0.08 * np.sin(3 * chi)


def dmodel(chi):
    return 0.6 * np.cos(chi) + 0.5 * np.cos(2 * chi) - 0.24 * np.cos(3 * chi)


fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.6))
print(f"{'nchi':>6} {'max err, even BC (2.47)':>26} {'max err, odd BC (now)':>24}")
for nchi in (33, 65, 129, 257):
    chi = np.linspace(0, np.pi, nchi)
    f = model(chi)
    wrong = CubicSpline(chi, f, bc_type=((1, 0.0), (1, 0.0)))   # PSPLINE bcs code 1, value 0
    right = CubicSpline(chi, f, bc_type=((2, 0.0), (2, 0.0)))   # PSPLINE bcs code 2, value 0
    fine = np.linspace(0, np.pi, 2001)
    ew = np.max(np.abs(wrong(fine, 1) - dmodel(fine)))
    er = np.max(np.abs(right(fine, 1) - dmodel(fine)))
    print(f"{nchi:6d} {ew:26.3e} {er:24.3e}")
    if nchi == 65:
        axes[0].plot(fine, dmodel(fine), color="k", lw=1, label="exact d/dchi")
        axes[0].plot(fine, wrong(fine, 1), color=ORANGE, label="spline, zero 1st derivative (2.47)")
        axes[0].plot(fine, right(fine, 1), color=BLUE, ls="--", label="spline, zero 2nd derivative (now)")
        axes[1].semilogy(chi, np.abs(wrong(chi, 1) - dmodel(chi)) + 1e-16, color=ORANGE, label="2.47")
        axes[1].semilogy(chi, np.abs(right(chi, 1) - dmodel(chi)) + 1e-16, color=BLUE, label="now")

axes[0].set_xlabel("chi"); axes[0].set_title("derivative of an odd function on [0, pi], 65 points")
axes[0].legend(fontsize=8)
axes[1].set_xlabel("chi"); axes[1].set_title("|error| of the derivative at the grid points")
axes[1].legend(fontsize=8)
for ax in axes:
    ax.set_xticks([0, np.pi / 2, np.pi]); ax.set_xticklabels(["0", "pi/2", "pi"])
save(fig, "shear_odd_spline.png")
print("The wrong end condition forces the slope to 0 at chi = 0 and pi, where the")
print("odd function has its largest slope: an O(1) error that does not shrink with")
print("nchi at the ends and decays over a few intervals inward.")

shear S. Theta^alpha is odd in theta, so on a top-bottom symmetric
equilibrium the spline needs the odd condition bcs(:,2) = [2,2] (zero

setup_modes: table slot from the mode number

file X_ops (setup_modes)commit e4e3fddtime 20 minread

With the fast mode window (X_style 2) the window of n_mod_X poloidal modes follows nq across the radius, and modes end and start where the window moves. PB3D keeps two tables that must agree: nm_X (mode number per radial point and slot) and ind_tot (per mode: number, radial range, slot). 2.47 computed the slot of a new mode from the slot of the mode created last, which agrees with nm_X only while the window moves up. When it moves down (nq < 0), reverses (reversed shear) or jitters (a flat q), two active modes shared a slot and their couplings were mixed without a message. That formula dates from 27 March 2018 (63ce0f4, v2.14). The fix takes the slot from the mode number with the formula nm_X uses, modulo(m - nm_X(1,1), n_mod_X) + 1, and adds a check that every mode finds its own number in its slot at every point of its range (a new runtime error if not).

The script tests/reference/setup_modes_sim.py copies the index formulas of 2.47, of an unmerged 2020 rewrite (afc9d17 on origin/issue_vac_not_used_VMEC), of a corrected version of that rewrite, and of the fix, and counts wrong (point, mode) entries for eight window histories. It runs in ctest as unit_setup_modes_sim.

script
"""Simulate the mode bookkeeping of PB3D's `setup_modes` (Modules/X_ops.f90).

With X_style = 2 ("fast", the default) the window of n_mod_X poloidal modes
follows nq across the radius. At each radial point kd the lowest mode number of
the window is nint(min_nm_X(kd)). When it changes by delta, |delta| modes end
and |delta| new modes start. PB3D stores the modes in n_mod_X table slots:

* the nm_X table puts the mode of rank ld (1 = lowest) in slot
  modulo(ld + ld_shift - 1, n_mod_X) + 1, where ld_shift is the running sum of
  delta (X_ops.f90, "set n or m at local normal position");
* the ind_tot / mds%sec table records, for every mode, its number, its radial
  range and the slot it is stored in (column 4).

Both tables must agree. This script copies the index formulas of

* the CURRENT code (since 63ce0f4, 2018-03-27; X_ops.f90:1169-1200 on
  dev/ci-quality): the slot of a new mode is computed from the slot of the
  mode that was created last;
* the 2020 rewrite afc9d17 (branch origin/issue_vac_not_used_VMEC, never
  merged): at every sub-step it searches the active modes for the lowest and
  highest mode number, ends one of them, gives the new mode the freed slot and
  the number (extreme +/- jd);
* a CORRECTED version: as afc9d17, but the new number is extreme +/- 1,
  because the extreme is searched again at every sub-step;
* the FIXED code (issue #4, step 5): as the current code, but the slot of a
  new mode is modulo(m_new - nm_X(1,1), n_mod_X) + 1, the formula the nm_X
  table uses, so the two tables agree by construction.

It reports, for a set of min_nm_X sequences, how many (radial point, mode)
pairs end up with a wrong slot or a wrong set of mode numbers, and exits
with status 1 if the fixed code has any (so that CTest can run it).

Run: python3 setup_modes_sim.py
"""
import sys

N = 5  # n_mod_X


def check(kd, active, tot, minseq, ld_shift, errors):
    """Compare the active modes with what the nm_X table holds at kd."""
    want = list(range(minseq[kd], minseq[kd] + N))
    got = sorted(tot[i][0] for i in active)
    if got != want:
        errors.append((kd, "mode numbers", got, want))
        return
    for i in active:
        rank = tot[i][0] - minseq[kd] + 1
        true_slot = (rank + ld_shift - 1) % N + 1
        if tot[i][3] != true_slot:
            errors.append((kd, "slot", tot[i][0], tot[i][3], true_slot))


def current(minseq):
    ld_shift = 0
    tot = [[minseq[0] + ld - 1, 1, 0, ld] for ld in range(1, N + 1)]  # [m, start, end, slot]
    cur = list(range(N))   # ind_cur: indices into tot, kept sorted from low to high m
    ind_id = N             # number of entries created so far
    errors = []
    for kd in range(1, len(minseq)):
        d = minseq[kd] - minseq[kd - 1]
        ld_shift += d
        for ld in range(1, abs(d) + 1):
            last_slot = tot[ind_id - 1][3]   # ind_tot(ind_id,4): slot of the last created mode
            if d > 0:
                tot[cur[0]][2] = kd
                tot.append([tot[cur[-1]][0] + 1, kd + 1, 0, (last_slot + ld - 1) % N + 1])
                cur = cur[1:] + [len(tot) - 1]
            else:
                tot[cur[-1]][2] = kd
                tot.append([tot[cur[0]][0] - 1, kd + 1, 0, (last_slot - ld) % N + 1])
                cur = [len(tot) - 1] + cur[:-1]
        ind_id = len(tot)
        check(kd, cur, tot, minseq, ld_shift, errors)
    return errors


def fixed(minseq):
    """The current code with the slot computed from the mode number."""
    ld_shift = 0
    m0 = minseq[0]        # nm_X(1,1)
    tot = [[minseq[0] + ld - 1, 1, 0, ld] for ld in range(1, N + 1)]
    cur = list(range(N))
    errors = []
    for kd in range(1, len(minseq)):
        d = minseq[kd] - minseq[kd - 1]
        ld_shift += d
        for ld in range(1, abs(d) + 1):
            if d > 0:
                tot[cur[0]][2] = kd
                m_new = tot[cur[-1]][0] + 1
                tot.append([m_new, kd + 1, 0, (m_new - m0) % N + 1])
                cur = cur[1:] + [len(tot) - 1]
            else:
                tot[cur[-1]][2] = kd
                m_new = tot[cur[0]][0] - 1
                tot.append([m_new, kd + 1, 0, (m_new - m0) % N + 1])
                cur = [len(tot) - 1] + cur[:-1]
        check(kd, cur, tot, minseq, ld_shift, errors)
    return errors


def searched(minseq, step_is_jd):
    ld_shift = 0
    tot = [[minseq[0] + ld - 1, 1, 0, ld] for ld in range(1, N + 1)]
    active = list(range(N))
    errors = []
    for kd in range(1, len(minseq)):
        d = minseq[kd] - minseq[kd - 1]
        ld_shift += d
        for jd in range(1, abs(d) + 1):
            step = jd if step_is_jd else 1
            imin = min(active, key=lambda i: tot[i][0])
            imax = max(active, key=lambda i: tot[i][0])
            if d > 0:
                tot[imin][2] = kd
                tot.append([tot[imax][0] + step, kd + 1, 0, tot[imin][3]])
                active[active.index(imin)] = len(tot) - 1
            else:
                tot[imax][2] = kd
                tot.append([tot[imin][0] - step, kd + 1, 0, tot[imax][3]])
                active[active.index(imax)] = len(tot) - 1
        check(kd, active, tot, minseq, ld_shift, errors)
    return errors


CASES = {
    "monotonic up (q rising, m > 0)": [10, 10, 11, 11, 12, 13, 13, 14],
    "monotonic down (nq < 0, e.g. VMEC)": [14, 13, 13, 12, 11, 11, 10],
    "up then down (q has a maximum)": [10, 11, 12, 12, 11, 10],
    "down then up (reversed shear)": [12, 11, 10, 10, 11, 12, 13],
    "jitter in flat q": [10, 10, 11, 10, 11, 11, 12],
    "jumps of 2 up": [10, 12, 14, 16],
    "jumps of 2 down": [16, 14, 12, 10],
    "jumps of 3 up": [10, 13, 16],
}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"{'case':38s} {'current':>8s} {'afc9d17':>8s} {'corrected':>10s} {'fixed':>6s}")
    n_bad = 0
    for name, seq in CASES.items():
        a = len(current(seq))
        b = len(searched(seq, step_is_jd=True))
        c = len(searched(seq, step_is_jd=False))
        d = len(fixed(seq))
        n_bad += d
        print(f"{name:38s} {a:8d} {b:8d} {c:10d} {d:6d}")
    print("\n(numbers are counts of wrong (radial point, mode) entries; 0 = correct)")
    print("PASS" if n_bad == 0 else "FAIL")
    sys.exit(0 if n_bad == 0 else 1)
How to check it
  1. Read the two changed formulas against nm_X's own rule, modulo(m - nm_X(1,1), n_mod_X) + 1.
  2. Read the new check loop after the main loop.
  3. Run or read the sim: the column "current" (the code as at 2.47; the script was written before the fix) has wrong entries for five of the eight window histories, the column "fixed" none.
Gap. None of the fixtures moves the window down, so no eigenvalue changed and no regression test covers the case. The sim tests a Python copy of the formulas, not the Fortran; the Fortran's own check is the new loop, which stops a run whose tables disagree.

mode m in slot modulo(m - nm_X(1,1), n_mod_X) + 1; ind_tot computed a new
mode's slot from the slot of the mode created last, which agrees only while

MPI: every point from its owner

files MPI_utilities (redistribute_var), grid_opscommit 798fe50; margin from num_vars and unused routines removed in 1839ea0time 25 minstudy

With 2 or 4 MPI processes every eigenvalue differed from the 1-process one by about 2e-5 relative. Cause: every process hands its whole local range to redistribute_var, ghost points included, so the source ranges overlap. 2.47 filled each destination point from the sources in rank order, which in an overlap takes the lower rank's ghost region, where derivatives are one-sided and splines end. A and B differed from the 1-process matrices in the 12 to 16 rows after each interface, by 6e-6 and 2e-5 of their largest entry. The fix splits each overlap in the middle (the convention of trim_grid) and takes every point from its owner. On Snellius the cbm18a fixed deck then gives the same eigenvalue with 1, 2, 3 and 4 processes to 1.5e-8, the circular deck to 2e-12. The rank-order loop dates from 22 March 2017 (2bc8bbc, v1.61).

A second, smaller part: grid_ops widens the equilibrium range by 20 points (ghost_interp), because interp_V fits a cubic spline over exactly the local range and a spline's end effect reaches inward, falling by about 2 − √3 ≈ 0.27 per interval. Its contribution to the eigenvalue was 1e-6. The right panel of the demo shows the decay.

How to check it
  1. Run or read the demo: it copies both versions of the index arithmetic and marks the eight points (of 60, with 3 processes and 4 ghost points) that 2.47 took from a ghost region.
  2. Read the new loop against the demo: lims_eff_tot is the owned range, id_start and n_vars the intersection of destination and owned range, and id_rec/id_sen the offsets into the local arrays.
  3. Guard: regression_cbm18a_fixed_bnd_np2 and _np4 (tolerance 1e-6 against one process). They are opt-in (-DPB3D_TEST_MPI_REGRESSION=ON, needs MUMPS in PETSc); they ran on Snellius, and CI does not run them.

script
"""Area 2c: who fills which point in MPI_utilities.redistribute_var (commit 798fe50).

Every process hands in its whole local range, ghost points included, so the
source ranges overlap. The destination ranges do not overlap. The routine
decides, for every destination point, which process sends it.

2.47: for each destination, walk the sources in rank order and take from the
first one whose range still covers the next point. In an overlap the point
comes from the LOWER rank, i.e. from that rank's ghost region, where radial
derivatives and interpolations are one-sided and less accurate.

Now: split every overlap in the middle (the convention of trim_grid) and take
each point from its owner.

The two loops below are copied from the Fortran (old and new) with 1-based
inclusive limits. The ranges are an example with 3 processes, 60 points and
a ghost region of 4 points on each side.

Second panel: grid_ops now widens the range of the spline that interp_V fits
by 20 points (ghost_interp). A cubic not-a-knot spline fitted on a window
differs from the spline on the full range near the window ends; the
difference falls by about 2 - sqrt(3) = 0.27 per interval inward.
"""
import math

import numpy as np
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline

from _common import BLUE, GREY, ORANGE, plt, save

n_pts, n_procs, ghost = 60, 3, 4
own = [(1, 20), (21, 40), (41, 60)]
lims_tot = [(max(a - ghost, 1), min(b + ghost, n_pts)) for a, b in own]   # source ranges, overlapping
lims_dis_tot = own                                                         # destination ranges


def old_rule():
    src = np.zeros(n_pts + 1, int)
    for jd in range(n_procs):
        max_loc = lims_dis_tot[jd][0]
        for id_ in range(n_procs):
            if lims_tot[id_][1] >= max_loc:
                n = min(lims_tot[id_][1], lims_dis_tot[jd][1]) - max_loc + 1
                if n > 0:
                    src[max_loc:max_loc + n] = id_
                max_loc += max(n, 0)
    return src[1:]


def new_rule():
    eff = [list(r) for r in lims_tot]
    for id_ in range(1, n_procs):
        if lims_tot[id_][0] <= lims_tot[id_ - 1][1]:
            eff[id_][0] = lims_tot[id_][0] + math.ceil((lims_tot[id_ - 1][1] - lims_tot[id_][0] + 1.0) / 2)
            eff[id_ - 1][1] = eff[id_][0] - 1
    src = np.zeros(n_pts + 1, int)
    for jd in range(n_procs):
        for id_ in range(n_procs):
            start = max(lims_dis_tot[jd][0], eff[id_][0])
            n = max(0, min(lims_dis_tot[jd][1], eff[id_][1]) - start + 1)
            src[start:start + n] = id_
    return src[1:], eff


old = old_rule()
new, eff = new_rule()
in_ghost_old = [i + 1 for i in range(n_pts) if not (own[old[i]][0] <= i + 1 <= own[old[i]][1])]
print("source ranges incl. ghosts:", lims_tot)
print("owned ranges after the split:", [tuple(e) for e in eff])
print("points the 2.47 rule took from another process' ghost region:", in_ghost_old)
print("points the new rule takes from a non-owner:",
      [i + 1 for i in range(n_pts) if not (own[new[i]][0] <= i + 1 <= own[new[i]][1])])

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.4), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.4, 1]})
ax = axes[0]
cols = [BLUE, ORANGE, "#3a9a5b"]
for p in range(n_procs):
    a, b = lims_tot[p]
    ax.barh(3 - p * 0.5, b - a + 1, left=a - 0.5, height=0.35, color=cols[p], alpha=0.25)
    a, b = own[p]
    ax.barh(3 - p * 0.5, b - a + 1, left=a - 0.5, height=0.35, color=cols[p], alpha=0.8)
    ax.text(0, 3 - p * 0.5, f"rank {p}", va="center", ha="right", fontsize=8)
x = np.arange(1, n_pts + 1)
ax.scatter(x, np.full(n_pts, 1.2), c=[cols[s] for s in old], s=14, marker="s")
ax.scatter(x, np.full(n_pts, 0.7), c=[cols[s] for s in new], s=14, marker="s")
for i in in_ghost_old:
    ax.plot(i, 1.2, "kx", ms=6)
ax.text(0, 1.2, "source, 2.47", va="center", ha="right", fontsize=8)
ax.text(0, 0.7, "source, now", va="center", ha="right", fontsize=8)
ax.set_yticks([]); ax.set_xlim(-12, n_pts + 1); ax.set_xlabel("global radial index")
ax.set_title("pale: ghost points handed in; x: taken from a ghost region")
ax.grid(False)

# panel 2: local spline window vs full-range spline
xs = np.linspace(0, 1, 201)
f = np.sin(7 * xs) * np.exp(xs)
full = CubicSpline(xs, f)
i0, i1 = 80, 140
fine_idx = np.arange(i0, i1 + 1)
for margin, c in ((0, ORANGE), (20, BLUE)):
    a, b = i0 - margin, i1 + margin
    loc = CubicSpline(xs[a:b + 1], f[a:b + 1])
    xm = 0.5 * (xs[fine_idx[:-1]] + xs[fine_idx[1:]])               # midpoints, where the splines differ
    d = np.abs(loc(xm) - full(xm))
    lab = f"window widened by {margin}" + (" (round-off everywhere)" if margin else "")
    axes[1].semilogy(fine_idx[:-1] - i0, np.maximum(d, 2e-17), color=c, label=lab)
    if margin == 0:
        d0 = d[0]
axes[1].semilogy(np.arange(0, 30), d0 * (2 - math.sqrt(3)) ** np.arange(0, 30), color=GREY, ls=":", label="0.27 per interval")
axes[1].set_ylim(1e-17, 1e-1)
axes[1].set_xlabel("interval inside the window of one process")
axes[1].set_title("spline on a window vs on the full range")
axes[1].legend(fontsize=8)
save(fig, "redistribute_owner.png")

commit message
The 2e-5 relative shift of every eigenvalue with 2 or 4 MPI processes:
redistribute_var (MPI_utilities) assumed non-overlapping source ranges and
filled each destination from the sources in rank order, so the overlap after
a process interface came from the lower rank's ghost region, whose values near
the end of its range are the less accurate ones (one-sided derivatives, spline
ends). The assembled A and B differed from the one-process matrices in the 12
to 16 rows after every interface, by 6e-6 and 2e-5 of the largest entry. Each
destination point now comes from its owner, the overlap of two neighbours
split in the middle as trim_grid does. On Snellius (PETSc 3.25.3 with MUMPS)
the cbm18a fixed deck gives -4.3572898102e-2, -4.3572897434e-2,
-4.3572897397e-2 and -4.3572898258e-2 with 1, 2, 3 and 4 processes (1.5e-8,
1.6e-8, 3.6e-9), the circular deck 1.4e-12 and 1.8e-12; what remains is the
level at which the eigenvalue itself is reproducible. redistribute_output_grid
adds a 20-point margin for the cubic spline of interp_V (a 1e-6 contribution).

Tests: the opt-in rows regression_cbm18a_fixed_bnd_np2/_np4
(-DPB3D_TEST_MPI_REGRESSION=ON, a distributed LU in PETSc needed) run the deck
with one process and under mpirun and require 1e-6 agreement, which the 1e-3
anchor rows could not see; they pass on Snellius. response_1_vs_2 also asserts
its five style-1 over style-2 ratios at 81 x 80 against recorded values to
0.5 %, so that the field-line spacing of step 6b is caught (the mutation check
of step 7 found that the convergence-order checks alone were not).

VMEC: the Nyquist mode list and B0

file VMEC_ops (read_VMEC)commit 0d49f19; B0 from the first Nyquist mode in 1839ea0time 20 minread

Mode list. A VMEC wout file stores R, Z and λ on the main mode list (xm, xn, mnmax modes) and the Jacobian, |B| and the covariant B components on the Nyquist list (xm_nyq, xn_nyq, mnmax_nyq ≥ mnmax), each ordered by its own limits. 2.47 took gmnc(1:mnmax,:), bmnc(1:mnmax,:) and bsub*(1:mnmax,:) and labelled them with the main list. That is right only when ntor = 0 or mnmax_nyq = mnmax (the STELLOPT W7-X file). For a VMEC++ file of the rippled twin (mpol 12, ntor 6) 143 of 150 labels were wrong, and the fixed-boundary eigenvalue was 37 % off. Commit 0d49f19 matched the modes by (m, n); the Fourier-basis commit 3b99109 (R1) then kept the whole Nyquist list. The line as at 2.47 dates from July 2017 (ca8a070, v1.86).

B0. PB3D normalises with |B| on the axis. 2.47 summed all bmnc modes, which is |B| at θ = ζ = 0 and depends on where the toroidal origin lies; on a rippled axis it varies with the ripple amplitude δ, so the normalised eigenvalues varied linearly in δ while the physics is even in δ. Now B0 is the (0, 0) Nyquist mode, the toroidal average. Even on the axisymmetric twin the old B0 was 0.8 % low: the HELENA and VMEC fixed-boundary eigenvalues of the circular twin were 1.6 % apart and now agree to 2e-6. On the rippled twins the eigenvalues now change as δ² (ratios 4.0 and 3.9 fixed, 4.1 and 4.9 free, for doubling δ); W7-X eigenvalues rescale by 1.064. The sum dates from April 2017 (df0f239, v1.67).

How to check it
  1. Run or read the demo: it builds both mode lists with VMEC's ordering and counts the mislabelled entries, and checks the claim on the committed fixture (ntor 0: no mislabelling).
  2. Read the B0 loop and the Nyquist block of read_VMEC; every 1:mnmax_V on a Nyquist array became 1:mnmax_nyq_V.

script
"""Area 2d: VMEC's two mode lists (VMEC_ops.read_VMEC, commit 0d49f19).

A VMEC wout file stores R, Z and lambda on the main list (xm, xn; mnmax
modes, set by mpol and ntor) and the Jacobian gmn, |B| bmn and the covariant
components bsub*mn on the Nyquist list (xm_nyq, xn_nyq; mnmax_nyq modes, set
by the Nyquist limits of the real-space grid). Both lists are ordered
m = 0: n = 0..ntor; m >= 1: n = -ntor..ntor (xn = n * nfp), each with its
own limits.

At 2.47 read_VMEC took gmnc(1:mnmax,:), bmnc(1:mnmax,:) and bsub*(1:mnmax,:)
and labelled them with the MAIN list. This script builds both lists and
counts how many of the first mnmax Nyquist entries carry a different (m, n)
than the main-list label they were given.

If the fixture wout_circ_eps033_q104.nc.xz can be found, it also checks the
claim on a real file (ntor = 0).
"""
import lzma
import os
import tempfile


def vmec_list(m_max, n_max, nfp):
    """VMEC ordering: m = 0 with n = 0..n_max, then m = 1..m_max with n = -n_max..n_max."""
    out = [(0, n * nfp) for n in range(0, n_max + 1)]
    for m in range(1, m_max + 1):
        out += [(m, n * nfp) for n in range(-n_max, n_max + 1)]
    return out


cases = [
    ("circular twin (ntor 0)", 12, 0, 1, 15, 0),
    ("rippled twin (mpol 12, ntor 6, nfp 5)", 12, 6, 5, 15, 8),
    ("W7-X STELLOPT file (mpol 12, ntor 12, nfp 5)", 12, 12, 5, 11, 12),
]
print(f"{'case':46} {'mnmax':>6} {'mnmax_nyq':>10} {'mislabelled at 2.47':>20}")
for name, mpol, ntor, nfp, mnyq, nnyq in cases:
    main = vmec_list(mpol - 1, ntor, nfp)
    nyq = vmec_list(mnyq, nnyq, nfp)
    k = min(len(main), len(nyq))
    bad = sum(1 for a, b in zip(main[:k], nyq[:k]) if a != b)
    print(f"{name:46} {len(main):6d} {len(nyq):10d} {bad:20d}")
    if ntor == 6:
        print("   first entries:  main", main[7:11], " nyquist", nyq[7:11])
print("(The W7-X row assumes a Nyquist list of the same size as the main list,")
print(" as in that STELLOPT file, mnmax_nyq = mnmax = 288: then nothing is mislabelled.)")

here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
fx = os.path.join(here, "..", "..", "tests", "fixtures", "wout_circ_eps033_q104.nc.xz")
if os.path.exists(fx):
    try:
        import netCDF4
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            p = os.path.join(d, "wout.nc")
            with open(p, "wb") as fo:
                fo.write(lzma.open(fx).read())
            ds = netCDF4.Dataset(p)
            xm, xn = ds["xm"][:], ds["xn"][:]
            xmn, xnn = ds["xm_nyq"][:], ds["xn_nyq"][:]
            same = all(int(xm[i]) == int(xmn[i]) and int(xn[i]) == int(xnn[i]) for i in range(len(xm)))
            print(f"fixture: mnmax {len(xm)}, mnmax_nyq {len(xmn)}; first mnmax Nyquist entries equal the main list: {same}")
            ds.close()
    except ImportError:
        print("netCDF4 not installed: fixture check skipped")
Gap. No committed test has a VMEC file with ntor > 0: the only VMEC fixture, wout_circ_eps033_q104.nc, is axisymmetric, so neither the Nyquist fix, the B0 fix nor the Nyquist path of the Fourier basis (R1) is guarded in CI. The rippled twins and W7-X were run on Snellius.

commit message
read_VMEC copied the Jacobian, |B| and the covariant B components as the first
mnmax entries of arrays that follow VMEC Nyquist mode list, right only when that
list starts with the main one (ntor = 0, or mnmax_nyq = mnmax as in STELLOPT files);
a VMEC++ file with ntor = 6 had 143 of 150 coefficients mislabelled and a 37 %
fixed-boundary error. The modes are now matched by (m, n).

The reference field B_0 summed all |B| modes at the axis, i.e. |B| at theta = zeta
= 0: on a rippled torus the dimensionless eigenvalue then varied linearly with the
ripple amplitude although the physics is even in it, and even the axisymmetric
twin B_0 was 0.8 % low. B_0 is now the (0,0) mode. HELENA and VMEC fixed-boundary
eigenvalues of the circular twin agree to 2e-6 (1.6 % before); the rippled twins
shift as delta^2 (ratios 4.0, 3.9 fixed; 4.1, 4.9 free), so 6f passes. W7-X numbers
rescale by 1.064. The twin regression test anchors follow (VMEC fixed +7.8431e-2,
twins within 1e-4, free -0.51892).

Also in the plan: 6e verified on Snellius, the multi-process shift characterised,
the W7-X ordering pass, the mutation check O3 (3 of 4 mutations caught).

Free edge: the trapezoidal end weight

file SLEPC_ops (fill_mat)commit 4915d4btime 25 minstudy

fill_mat adds the energy integrand of each radial point times the step size. With a fixed boundary the last row is replaced by the boundary condition, so the weight of the last point never enters. With a free boundary (BC_style(2) = 2 or 4) the last point stays in the system and the trapezoidal rule gives it half the weight. 2.47 gave it the full weight, so the free-boundary eigenvalues converged like 1/N in n_r_sol (2.3 % off at the 200 points of the regression decks on the HELENA circular ε = 0.33 kink: −0.44383 before, −0.43380 after, comment of the twin regression test) while fixed-boundary ones converged like 1/N². The fix multiplies the blocks of the last point by w_q = 1/2 for those two styles.

The full end weight dates from November 2017 (5108fb5, v2.01), but it only affected free-boundary runs with style 4, since style 2 never ran before July 2026. The demo is a model, not PB3D's assembly: the 1-D problem −u″ = λu with a surface term κu(1)² at a free end. With the full end weight its eigenvalue error halves per doubling of N; with half the weight it falls by 4; with a fixed end both weights give the same result.

How to check it
  1. Read the change: w_q multiplies all three block types of row kd = n_r-1 (0-based: the last point), for A and B alike.
  2. Guard: regression_circ_eps005_free_bnd runs 200 and 400 radial points and fails if the eigenvalue moves by more than 5e-4 between them (ORDER_RTOL). With the full weight the eigenvalue converges like 1/N and moves by far more.
  3. Numbers after the fix: the circular ε = 0.33 kink agrees with MISHKA-1 without a wall to 0.005 % at n = 10 (the README later calls this a coincidence: the axisymmetric style then still converged like 1/N in the poloidal points, see V6), 0.63 % and 0.89 % at n = 15 and 20; the cbm18a free anchors moved 4.5e-4 (style 2) and 0.9 % (style 4).

script
"""Area 2e: the quadrature weight of the free edge point (SLEPC_ops.fill_mat, w_q).

PB3D assembles the energy integrals over the radial points as sum_k h f_k.
At 2.47 every point had the weight h, also the last one. With a fixed boundary
the last row is replaced by the boundary condition, so its weight never
matters. With a free boundary (BC_style(2) = 2 or 4) the last point stays in
the system and the trapezoidal rule gives it h/2. Commit 4915d4b sets
w_q = 1/2 there.

This is a MODEL of the principle, not PB3D's assembly: the 1-D eigenproblem

    -u'' = lambda u on [0, 1],  u(0) = 0,  u'(1) + kappa u(1) = 0,

which is the stationary point of W/K with
    W = int_0^1 u'^2 dx + kappa u(1)^2   (kappa u(1)^2 plays the vacuum term)
    K = int_0^1 u^2 dx.
Discretized with N intervals: W with differences on the intervals (second
order), K with point values u_k and weights w_k = h, except w_N, which is
either h (2.47) or h/2 (now). The exact lambda solves sqrt(l) cos(sqrt(l)) +
kappa sin(sqrt(l)) = 0.

With u(1) = 0 instead (fixed boundary) the weight of the last point drops out:
both versions give the same result, converging like 1/N^2.
"""
import numpy as np
from scipy.linalg import eigh
from scipy.optimize import brentq

from _common import BLUE, GREY, ORANGE, plt, save

KAPPA = 1.0


def exact_free():
    return brentq(lambda s: s * np.cos(s) + KAPPA * np.sin(s), 1.0, 3.0) ** 2


def discrete(N, w_end, free=True):
    h = 1.0 / N
    n = N if free else N - 1                       # unknowns u_1..u_N (free) or u_1..u_{N-1}
    A = np.zeros((n, n)); B = np.zeros((n, n))
    # stiffness: sum over intervals of ((u_k - u_{k-1})/h)^2 h, u_0 = 0
    for k in range(1, N + 1):
        i, j = k - 1, k - 2                        # indices of u_k and u_{k-1}
        for a, ca in ((i, 1.0), (j, -1.0)):
            for b, cb in ((i, 1.0), (j, -1.0)):
                if 0 <= a < n and 0 <= b < n:
                    A[a, b] += ca * cb / h
    if free:
        A[n - 1, n - 1] += KAPPA                   # the surface ("vacuum") term
    w = np.full(n, h)
    if free:
        w[-1] = w_end
    B[np.arange(n), np.arange(n)] = w
    return eigh(A, B, eigvals_only=True)[0]


lam = exact_free()
lam_fix = np.pi ** 2
Ns = np.array([25, 50, 100, 200, 400, 800])
err_old = np.array([abs(discrete(N, 1.0 / N) - lam) / lam for N in Ns])
err_new = np.array([abs(discrete(N, 0.5 / N) - lam) / lam for N in Ns])
err_fix = np.array([abs(discrete(N, 1.0 / N, free=False) - lam_fix) / lam_fix for N in Ns])

print(f"exact lambda (free, kappa = {KAPPA}) = {lam:.10f}")
print(f"{'N':>5} {'rel err, w_N = h (2.47)':>24} {'rel err, w_N = h/2 (now)':>25} {'fixed bnd':>11}")
for N, a, b, c in zip(Ns, err_old, err_new, err_fix):
    print(f"{N:5d} {a:24.3e} {b:25.3e} {c:11.3e}")
p_old = np.polyfit(np.log(Ns), np.log(err_old), 1)[0]
p_new = np.polyfit(np.log(Ns), np.log(err_new), 1)[0]
print(f"observed order: 2.47 {-p_old:.2f}, now {-p_new:.2f}")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.6, 3.8))
ax.loglog(Ns, err_old, "o-", color=ORANGE, label="free end, weight h (2.47)")
ax.loglog(Ns, err_new, "s-", color=BLUE, label="free end, weight h/2 (now)")
ax.loglog(Ns, err_fix, "^--", color=GREY, label="fixed end (either weight)")
ax.set_xlabel("number of radial intervals N")
ax.set_ylabel("relative error of the lowest eigenvalue")
ax.set_title("model problem: the end weight sets the order")
ax.legend(fontsize=8)
save(fig, "edge_weight_1d.png")

commit message
The free end point carried the full weight h in the radial energy sum
(fill_mat) where the trapezoidal rule gives h/2, so free-boundary
eigenvalues converged only at first order in n_r_sol: 2.3 % at the 200
points of the regression decks on the circular external kink, whose
fixed-boundary eigenvalue converges at second order. One weight w_q
(BC styles 2 and 4) makes them second order. Against MISHKA-1 without a
wall the circular eps = 0.33 case now agrees to 0.005 % at n = 10
(0.63 and 0.89 % at n = 15 and 20), the eps = 0.05 case to 1.2, 0.55
and 0.26 % (falling as 1/n^2); the 2.3 % the plan had taken for the
toroidal correction of the high-n ordering was this quadrature.
Anchors re-recorded (cbm18a free style 2 moved 4.5e-4, style 4 0.9 %;
eps = 0.05 free -0.42168; twin free -0.43914 against HELENA -0.43380);
circ_eps005_free_bnd.sh also runs 400 points and requires a move below
5e-4. Snellius ctest: Release 27/27, Debug 24/24.

MISHKA-1 runs on the extended cbm18a once its mapping has 513 poloidal
points (its FFT needs 2(NCHI-1) a power of two) and a square root of a
slightly negative pressure is clamped. With the plasma to psi_N = 1 in
both codes PB3D is 6 % (n = 10) to 18 % (n = 20) more unstable, not
explained by compressibility (MISHKA-1 is incompressible), harmonics,
radial grids or modes; the pseudo-vacuum's rational surfaces are
suspected. The fast mode window's non-monotonicity is the dropped
coupling at window shifts (0.2 % between 20 and 40 modes, not 2 %).
Mercier (T10) is not usable at the n PB3D runs.

Documentation/benchmarking_prep.md and Documentation/benchmarking/
(three literature surveys, claims tagged by verification) lay out the
benchmarks against other codes: TERPSICHORE (open source since 2025),
DESC's singular integrals for the 3-D vacuum kernels, COBRAVMEC, the
published cbm18 curves and their normalisation, the ELITE and IPP
requests.

Boundary-condition styles 2, 3 and 4

files SLEPC_ops (set_BC), input_opscommits 41b5274, 1d74b8f, 83c02dftime 25 minread

At 2.47 the free-boundary styles 2 and 3 stopped with "Vacuum has not been implemented yet!", and style 4 did run but lost the vacuum. Three commits:

  • Style 3 removed (41b5274). It extended the grid by ndps points and was never more than a stub.
  • Style 2 implemented (1d74b8f): the edge row is assembled by fill_mat like any bulk row (one-sided stencils), so the only boundary term of the energy is XeH res Xe, and set_BC_2 adds vac%res to the edge diagonal block. The natural boundary condition then follows from stationarity of the discrete energy, and A and B stay Hermitian. The code change is small: the stop is removed; the explanation went into the comments.
  • Style 4's edge block assembled once (83c02df; the double insertion dates from March 2018, 108bc9f, v2.12). set_BC_4 wrote the explicit natural-boundary-condition row V1TX + V2X′ + res X = 0 in two insertions at block (0, 0), both with overwrite=.true., so the second (the V2 part) replaced the first (V1T and the vacuum). Now the two are added and inserted once. The default BC_style went to [1, 4] in July and back to [1, 2] here, your choice since 2017.

Style 4 still differs from style 2: on cbm18a by 0.19 % now (anchors −4.5051e-2 and −4.5136e-2), on the circular external kink by 7 %. Your own 2017 comment called it "does not work well yet"; its header now says "Not validated" and quotes 0.7 % on cbm18a, a number from before the edge weight of F5. You decided on 6 November to keep the style.

How to check it
  1. Read set_BC_2: one insertion of vac%res at the edge diagonal block, no step size (a surface term).
  2. Read set_BC_4 against the 2.47 version: the two former insertions at (0, 0) are summed before one insertion, and the V2 loop now stops at jd = −1.
  3. Read the removal of style 3 and of the grid extension in setup_mats and fill_mat.

How the vacuum enters A and the POST energy (the factor 2π and the sign) is part of V8.

commit message
BC styles 2 and 3 were identical three-line stubs behind a 'vacuum not
implemented' guard: they added the raw (unweighted) vacuum response to
the edge diagonal of A and nothing else - no V1/V2 couplings, no B-side
terms, and none of what defines the styles (asymmetric-stencil rework
of the last rows for 2, ghost-point elimination for 3).

* Style 3 is removed, including its grid-extension special cases in
  setup_mats: it offers nothing over style 2 conceptually and over
  style 4 practically.
* Style 2 is kept as a documented placeholder that fails with a clear
  message pointing to style 4: a proper implementation (natural
  boundary condition imposed variationally with one-sided stencils)
  would keep A and B Hermitian, which style 4's overwritten edge row
  does not - worth doing as a separate feature.
* The default BC_style is now [1,4]: the previous default [1,2]
  pointed at the guarded stub, so any default-configured free-boundary
  run would have failed.

1d74b8f2026-07-10 BC: implement style 2, the variational (Hermitian) free-boundary condition.
its own diff: 3 hunks: 2 to read, mechanical 1 comment in 1 file
its lines, 2.47 against 9e9aba5, below: SLEPC_ops.f90:926 SLEPC_ops.f90:1179
commit message
It turns out the infrastructure was already in place: set_bulk_lims
includes the edge row in the bulk assembly for free-boundary styles,
fill_mat assembles that row variationally (V_1 blocks carry their
Hermitian-conjugate mirrors, V_2 the double stencil) with one-sided
stencils near the edge (natively for left differences, through the
ndc_ind shifting for central ones). The natural boundary condition
  (V_1^dagger X + V_2 X' + vac X)|_edge = 0
therefore emerges from the discrete stationarity of the energy once the
vacuum term's Hessian, vac%res, is added to the edge diagonal block of
A - which is exactly what the former stub did behind its 2.44-era
'vacuum not implemented' guard. Removing the guard is the
implementation.

In contrast to style 4 (explicit natural-BC row, overwritten), style 2
keeps A and B Hermitian. On the cbm18a free-boundary benchmark the two
styles agree to 3.5e-8 relative - two structurally different
discretizations of the same condition - while style 2 has a ~180x
smaller spurious imaginary part (1.1e-10 vs 2.0e-8) and a ~180x better
SLEPc residual (3.4e-2 vs 6.3).

The free-boundary regression now runs the deck with both styles and
asserts the anchor for each plus mutual agreement to 1e-5.

its own diff: 4 hunks: 3 to read, mechanical 1 comment in 2 files
its lines, 2.47 against 9e9aba5, below: SLEPC_ops.f90:1179 SLEPC_ops.f90:1259 SLEPC_ops.f90:1287 input_ops.f90:330
commit message
set_BC_4 inserted the (0,0) edge block with V1^T + vac and then let the V2
loop overwrite it at jd = 0, which dropped the vacuum and V1^T. The block
is now assembled once (V1^T + vac together with the jd = 0 part of V2) and
the loop runs from -st_size to -1. The default returns to [1,2], Toon's
choice since 2017.

With the overwrite gone, style 4 still differs from the variational style 2
by 0.7 % on cbm18a at psi = 0.75 and by far more on the circular external
kink, independently of the radial resolution, while style 2 agrees with
MISHKA to 1 %: the explicit natural-boundary-condition row has an
inconsistency of its own ("does not work well yet", 2017). It is marked not
validated in its header; use style 2.

The free-boundary regression deck moves to psi = 0.75 (edge amplitude 0.1),
anchors style 2 at -4.5019e-2 and style 4 at -4.4712e-2 (1e-3), asserts
free <= fixed and runs the response-matrix check.

R1

The Fourier basis of the VMEC path

files VMEC_utilities, VMEC_ops, VMEC_vars, eq_ops, grid_utilities, grid_vars, sol_ops, PB3D_ops, input_opscommits 3b99109, 329b7a4, 1a53f50time 45 minread

calc_trigon_factors stored, at every grid point, cos(mθ − nζ) and sin(mθ − nζ) for every mode of the main list, so the Nyquist modes beyond it could not be evaluated (F4). It now stores the one-angle basis: cos and sin of mθ for m = 0 … mpol_tf−1 and of n Nfp ζ for n = −ntor_tf … ntor_tf, with the grid points first in memory. fourier2real forms the products per mode for any mode list (mn argument, default the main list), so the Jacobian, |B| and Bi are evaluated on the full Nyquist list. The derivative factors are those of 2.47. The angle version fourier2real_2 now builds the basis for its angles and calls the table version (1a53f50, 90 lines fewer).

Results (commit messages): W7-X identical to all digits (its two mode lists coincide); the circular twin to 4.5e-13 (fixed) and 1.4e-11 (free, 64 lines); the rippled twins (ntor 6) to 1.2e-12, 4.5e-9 and 1.5e-6 for δ = 0.01, 0.02 and 0.04, the last because the Nyquist modes beyond the main list are now kept. Appendix A agrees: W7-X bit for bit, the circular twin by at most 4.5e-13. The equilibrium phase of a 150-mode, 64-line run takes half the time and the W7-X decks 22 % less memory; the consolidation changed eigenvalues by at most 6e-13.

Two consequences to check in the diffs: the index order of trigon_factors changed from (mode, θ, ζ, r, cos/sin) to (θ, ζ, r, basis, cos/sin), so every slice and every allocation that copies it changed too (trim_grid, sol_ops, test_B_F); and the output file gained mn_V_nyq and three entries in misc_in_V, so POST refuses output from before this commit ("rerun PB3D").

How to check it
  1. The demo copies the index arithmetic of the new fourier2real_1 line by line (basis indices, derivative factors, the cos/sin swap for an odd number of derivatives, the skip of zero coefficient sets) and compares it with direct evaluation for the W7-X mode extent, all derivative orders up to 2 in each angle and all sym flags: agreement to 3e-14.
  2. Read calc_trigon_factors and fourier2real_1 in the diff of VMEC_utilities below the cards, then the index-order blocks in the other files.

script
"""Area 3: the trigonometric basis of fourier2real (VMEC_utilities, commits 3b99109, 1a53f50).

At 2.47 calc_trigon_factors stored cos(m theta - n zeta) and sin(...) for
every mode of the MAIN list at every grid point, and fourier2real summed
coefficient * derivative factor * stored factor.

Now calc_trigon_factors stores the one-angle basis
    index m+1                       : cos(m theta), sin(m theta),   m = 0..mpol_tf-1
    index mpol_tf+ntor_tf+1+n       : cos(n nfp zeta), sin(n nfp zeta), n = -ntor_tf..ntor_tf
(grid points first) and fourier2real_1 forms, per mode,
    cos(m theta - n zeta) = cos(m theta) cos(n zeta) + sin(m theta) sin(n zeta)
    sin(m theta - n zeta) = sin(m theta) cos(n zeta) - cos(m theta) sin(n zeta)
for any mode list (main or Nyquist) within the basis.

This script copies the index arithmetic of the new fourier2real_1 line by line
(1-based indices kept as in the Fortran, shifted by -1 when used) and checks it
against direct evaluation of the derivatives of
    f = sum_k c_k cos(m_k theta - n_k zeta) + s_k sin(m_k theta - n_k zeta)
for random coefficients, the W7-X-like mode extent, and every combination of
up to two derivatives in each angle and of the sym flags.
It checks the algorithm, not the compiled Fortran: that is what the unchanged
eigenvalues on the three VMEC fixtures check (README, 2.49).
"""
import itertools

import numpy as np

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
nfp, mpol_V, ntor_V = 5, 12, 12
mn_V = [(0, n * nfp) for n in range(0, ntor_V + 1)] + \
       [(m, n * nfp) for m in range(1, mpol_V) for n in range(-ntor_V, ntor_V + 1)]
mn_nyq = [(0, n * nfp) for n in range(0, 16 + 1)] + \
         [(m, n * nfp) for m in range(1, 19) for n in range(-16, 16 + 1)]
mpol_tf = max(mpol_V, max(m for m, _ in mn_nyq) + 1)                 # as read_VMEC
ntor_tf = max(ntor_V, max(abs(n) for _, n in mn_nyq) // nfp)

theta = rng.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi, (7, 3))
zeta = rng.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi, (7, 3))

# calc_trigon_factors: (n1, n2, mpol_tf+2*ntor_tf+1, 2), one normal point
tf = np.zeros(theta.shape + (mpol_tf + 2 * ntor_tf + 1, 2))
for m in range(mpol_tf):
    tf[..., m, 0], tf[..., m, 1] = np.cos(m * theta), np.sin(m * theta)
for n in range(-ntor_tf, ntor_tf + 1):
    tf[..., mpol_tf + ntor_tf + n, 0] = np.cos(n * nfp * zeta)
    tf[..., mpol_tf + ntor_tf + n, 1] = np.sin(n * nfp * zeta)


def fourier2real_1(c, s, mn, deriv, sym):
    """Line-by-line copy of the new Fortran (one normal point)."""
    i_c, i_s = (1, 2) if sum(deriv) % 2 == 0 else (2, 1)
    sym = [sym[0] and np.any(np.abs(c) > 0), sym[1] and np.any(np.abs(s) > 0)]
    need = [(sym[0] and i_c == 1) or (sym[1] and i_s == 1),
            (sym[0] and i_c == 2) or (sym[1] and i_s == 2)]
    varr = np.zeros(theta.shape)
    for k, (m, n) in enumerate(mn):
        i_m = m + 1
        i_n = mpol_tf + ntor_tf + 1 + n // nfp
        fac_c = m ** deriv[0] * (-n) ** deriv[1] * (-1) ** ((sum(deriv) + 1) // 2)
        fac_s = m ** deriv[0] * (-n) ** deriv[1] * (-1) ** (sum(deriv) // 2)
        if abs(c[k]) <= 0 and abs(s[k]) <= 0:
            continue
        cs = [None, None]
        if need[0]:
            cs[0] = tf[..., i_m - 1, 0] * tf[..., i_n - 1, 0] + tf[..., i_m - 1, 1] * tf[..., i_n - 1, 1]
        if need[1]:
            cs[1] = tf[..., i_m - 1, 1] * tf[..., i_n - 1, 0] - tf[..., i_m - 1, 0] * tf[..., i_n - 1, 1]
        if sym[0]:
            varr += c[k] * fac_c * cs[i_c - 1]
        if sym[1]:
            varr += s[k] * fac_s * cs[i_s - 1]
    return varr


def direct(c, s, mn, deriv, sym):
    """d^a/dtheta^a d^b/dzeta^b of the Fourier sum, written out."""
    a, b = deriv
    out = np.zeros(theta.shape)
    for k, (m, n) in enumerate(mn):
        ph = m * theta - n * zeta
        amp = m ** a * (-n) ** b                     # chain rule factor of (m theta - n zeta)
        p = a + b                                    # d^p/dph^p of cos and sin
        dcos = [np.cos(ph), -np.sin(ph), -np.cos(ph), np.sin(ph)][p % 4]
        dsin = [np.sin(ph), np.cos(ph), -np.sin(ph), -np.cos(ph)][p % 4]
        if sym[0]:
            out += c[k] * amp * dcos
        if sym[1]:
            out += s[k] * amp * dsin
    return out


worst = 0.0
for mn, label in ((mn_V, "main list"), (mn_nyq, "Nyquist list")):
    c = rng.normal(size=len(mn)) / (1 + np.arange(len(mn)))
    s = rng.normal(size=len(mn)) / (1 + np.arange(len(mn)))
    for deriv in itertools.product(range(3), range(3)):
        for sym in ((True, True), (True, False), (False, True)):
            new = fourier2real_1(c, s, mn, deriv, sym)
            ref = direct(c, s, mn, deriv, sym)
            err = np.max(np.abs(new - ref)) / max(np.max(np.abs(ref)), 1e-300)
            worst = max(worst, err)
    print(f"{label:13}: {len(mn)} modes, max relative difference over 27 cases so far {worst:.1e}")
print(f"mpol_tf = {mpol_tf}, ntor_tf = {ntor_tf}: basis of {mpol_tf + 2 * ntor_tf + 1} functions "
      f"instead of {len(mn_V)} (main) or {len(mn_nyq)} (Nyquist) per grid point")
assert worst < 1e-10, "basis form disagrees with direct evaluation"
print("PASS")

commit message
calc_trigon_factors stores cos and sin of m theta for m = 0 .. mpol_tf-1 and
of n nfp zeta for n = -ntor_tf .. ntor_tf, with the grid points first:
trigon_factors(n_ang_1, n_ang_2, n_r, mpol_tf+2*ntor_tf+1, 2). mpol_tf and
ntor_tf cover the main and the Nyquist mode list and go into the output file
with the Nyquist list mn_V_nyq (misc_in_V has 10 entries; POST refuses older
files with a message). fourier2real forms cos(m theta - n zeta) and
sin(m theta - n zeta) from the basis per mode for whatever mode list it is
handed (optional mn, default mn_V), normal points outside and modes inside so
that one point's basis stays in cache, zero coefficient sets skipped; the
derivative rules are unchanged. read_VMEC keeps the Jacobian, |B| and the
covariant B components on the full Nyquist list (the (m, n) matching of
0d49f19 is gone) and the three reconstructions in eq_ops pass mn_V_nyq; the
sliced users (sol_ops interpolation, trim_grid, the B_E reconstruction) follow
the new index order.

Measured on Snellius against a7a8f6a: W7-X identical to all digits (its two
mode lists coincide), the circular twin to 4.5e-13 (fixed) and 1.4e-11 (free,
64 lines), the rippled NTOR = 6 twins to 1.2e-12, 4.5e-9 and 1.5e-6 for
delta = 0.01, 0.02, 0.04 (the Nyquist content now kept). The equilibrium
phase of the NTOR = 6 twin takes half the time it did (40 -> 20 s per
equilibrium job, 24 -> 16 s for the fixed run) while reconstructing 264
instead of 150 modes; the first build, with the mode index first as planned,
had tripled it. W7-X decks: 1051 -> 821 MB and 2032 -> 1574 MB peak resident.
Release ctest 25 of 25, Debug 24 of 24.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
329b7a42026-10-30 Step 9 follow-up for #4: no real equality tests in fourier2real, so the CI warning count is back at its baseline.
its own diff: 2 hunks: 2 to read in 1 file
its lines, 2.47 against 9e9aba5, below: VMEC_utilities.f90:109
commit message
gfortran's -Wcompare-reals flagged the four .eq./.ne. tests on the Fourier
coefficients; they now test abs(x) > 0, which is the same question.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
1a53f502026-10-31 Consolidation for #4: the angle version of fourier2real delegates to the table version.
its own diff: 2 hunks: 1 to read, mechanical 1 comment in 1 file
its lines, 2.47 against 9e9aba5, below: VMEC_utilities.f90:109 VMEC_utilities.f90:242
commit message
fourier2real_2 builds the trigonometric basis for its angles with
calc_trigon_factors and calls fourier2real_1, so the Fourier reconstruction has
one code path; 90 lines fewer. Release ctest on Snellius 27 of 27; the twin,
rippled-twin and W7-X eigenvalues move by at most 6e-13 (round-off of the
reordered trigonometric evaluation).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
