Stage 4

Vacuum design review

Decide before verifying. This stage has no diffs: it lays out what the vacuum code does now and where you might want it done differently.

V0

The vacuum now: data flow, convention, structure

modules vac_ops 2503 → 3878 lines, vac_utilities 518 → 1015, vac_vars 388 → 405time 2 hstudy

Data flow

The convention since 5 November (f3ebf11)

Both vacuum styles now use one convention, the vacuum's. The stored normal is \(\boldsymbol{n} = -\mathcal{J}\nabla\psi\): it points into the plasma, which is out of the vacuum region, and its length carries the surface element, \(\mathrm{d}S = |\mathcal{J}\nabla\psi|\,\mathrm{d}\theta\,\mathrm{d}\alpha\). With the normal data \(\phi' = \boldsymbol{n}\cdot\nabla\phi\) the discretised operators are

\[ G_{ij} \approx -\frac{w_j}{|\boldsymbol{x}_i-\boldsymbol{x}_j|}, \qquad H_{ij} \approx w_j\,\frac{\boldsymbol{n}_j\cdot(\boldsymbol{x}_j-\boldsymbol{x}_i)}{|\boldsymbol{x}_j-\boldsymbol{x}_i|^3} \quad (i\neq j), \]

with the quadrature weights \(w_j\) (field lines: Δp Δα / 2 per half interval; the axisymmetric style integrates over ζ analytically with the toroidal functions \(Q_{|n|-1/2}\)). For a point \(\boldsymbol{x}_i\) on the boundary and the diagonal included, the assembled operators satisfy

\[ \sum_j H_{ij}\phi_j - \sum_j G_{ij}\phi'_j = \begin{cases} 0 & \phi \text{ harmonic in the vacuum, decaying,}\\ -4\pi\,\phi_i & \phi \text{ harmonic in the plasma.}\end{cases} \]

The second line with φ = 1 gives \(\sum_j H_{ij} = -4\pi\), the row-sum rule that sets the field-line H diagonal (your design at 2.47). On a smooth surface the diagonal is \(H_{ii} = -2\pi\) plus the integral of the H kernel over the cell; at a corner it is \(-2\beta\) with β the vacuum's internal angle (β = π on a smooth surface), which is what calc_GH_2 adds. The exterior problem is then \(H\Phi = G\,\phi'\), solved without any shift of the diagonal for both styles.

The normal data come from the plasma displacement. With X = ξ·∇ψ and p the parallel angle, continuity of the normal field at the boundary gives \(\nabla\psi\cdot\nabla\phi = \boldsymbol{B}\cdot\nabla X\), and \(\mathcal{J}\boldsymbol{B}\cdot\nabla = \partial/\partial p\) along a field line in PB3D's flux coordinates, so \(\phi' = -\mathcal{J}\nabla\psi\cdot\nabla\phi = -\partial X/\partial p\), which for one mode \(X \propto e^{i(n\alpha + (nq-m)p)}\) gives \(-i(nq-m)X\). That is the factor \(-(nq-m)\) in set_up_data; the imaginary unit sits in the pairing of cos and sin columns. With this sign the vacuum energy \(\delta W_v = \frac{1}{2\mu_0}\oint \phi'^*\phi\,\mathrm{d}S\) is positive, and finish_response multiplies by 2π (the toroidal integral, since A carries 2δW including it) and divides by μ₀.

Derivation status: the identities and their constants follow from Green's second identity with this normal, and the data from the boundary condition above; I derived both for this page, and the toy below checks the identities numerically. The same convention is described in the commit message of f3ebf11. The code's own checks are the full-stack tests greens_identity_3d, exact_exterior_2d and vac_response_cylinder (T).

Between July and 5 November there was an intermediate state: the axisymmetric style kept the plasma-side kernels and solved (H + 4πI)Φ = G·EP, and the field-line response was flipped in sign at the end, which is the "H and G in different signs" you saw. Documentation/vacuum_work_overview.md, section 2, has that history. The step from that state to the one convention, f3ebf11, changes none of the nine eigenvalues of appendix A by more than 1e-13: the two sign choices described the same operators, and the commit re-expressed them.

A toy with the same convention

A boundary-element toy on a circular torus (R₀ = 3, a = 1, plain trapezoidal rule on a (θ, φ) grid) with PB3D's conventions. It shows three things. With the normal into the plasma, the exterior identity and the exterior solve converge. With the normal flipped (the field-line style before e3b4847) the interior identities are unchanged, because the row-sum diagonal adjusts to either sign of the off-diagonal entries. Only the exterior test fails, with a residual of exactly 2, so no test that used only interior potentials could detect the wrong normal. And the third point, for V6: the diagonals from identities make the toy converge like 1/N³, against 1/N for the diagonal from the corner term alone.

script
"""Areas 4b and 4e: the vacuum-side sign convention and the indirect diagonal, on a toy.

A boundary-element toy on a circular torus (R0 = 3, a = 1) with the SAME
conventions as PB3D's vac_ops now (both styles):

  * stored normal  n = x_theta x x_phi = -a (R0 + a cos theta) e_r:
    it points INTO the plasma, i.e. OUT OF the vacuum, and carries the area
    element (PB3D: -J grad psi, which carries |J grad psi| for dS = |J grad psi|
    dtheta dalpha);
  * normal data    dphi_j = n_j . grad phi(x_j);
  * G_ij = -w / |x_i - x_j|,   H_ij = w n_j . (x_j - x_i) / |x_j - x_i|^3,
    w = dtheta dphi (plain trapezoidal rule on a doubly periodic grid);
  * diagonal of G: the integral of -1/r over the singular cell (flat-cell
    closed form, as calc_GH_int_1's half cells);
  * diagonals, three variants:
      "row sum + G lin": H_ii from the row sum H 1 = -4 pi and a correction of
          G_ii from the identities of the linear harmonics x, y, z projected on
          the normal (PB3D's default for the field-line style, vac_diag_style 1);
      "row sum": the row sum for H_ii, G_ii from the flat cell only;
      "-2 pi": the corner term of a smooth surface alone for H_ii (a direct
          diagonal WITHOUT the cell integral of the H kernel that PB3D's
          vac_diag_style 2 adds), G_ii from the flat cell.

Identities that the assembled operators should satisfy on the boundary:
    interior harmonic phi (1, x, z):          H phi - G dphi = -4 pi phi
    exterior decaying phi (point source on
    the magnetic axis):                       H phi - G dphi = 0
and the exterior problem H Phi = G dphi returns phi on the boundary (no shift
of the diagonal: PB3D's solve_Phi_BEM since 5 November 2026).

Then the same with the normal flipped (n -> -n, outward), as store_vac_VMEC
had it until commit e3b4847 while the kernels assumed the inward one.

This is a toy for understanding: plain trapezoidal rule on a (theta, phi)
grid, not PB3D's field-line grid with its near-field rule.
"""
import numpy as np

from _common import BLUE, GREY, ORANGE, RED, plt, save

R0, A = 3.0, 1.0
X0 = np.array([R0, 0.0, 0.0])            # point source on the magnetic axis (inside the plasma)


def F_closed(U, V, s):
    Dp = np.sqrt(U**2 + 2 * s * U * V + V**2)
    Dm = np.sqrt(U**2 - 2 * s * U * V + V**2)
    return U * np.log(abs((V + s * U + Dp) / (-V + s * U + Dm))) + \
        V * np.log(abs((U + s * V + Dp) / (-U + s * V + Dm)))


def surface(nt):
    nphi = 3 * nt                                             # roughly square cells
    th, ph = np.meshgrid(2 * np.pi * np.arange(nt) / nt, 2 * np.pi * np.arange(nphi) / nphi, indexing="ij")
    th, ph = th.ravel(), ph.ravel()
    rho = R0 + A * np.cos(th)
    x = np.stack([rho * np.cos(ph), rho * np.sin(ph), A * np.sin(th)], 1)
    x_t = np.stack([-A * np.sin(th) * np.cos(ph), -A * np.sin(th) * np.sin(ph), A * np.cos(th)], 1)
    x_p = np.stack([-rho * np.sin(ph), rho * np.cos(ph), 0 * th], 1)
    n = np.cross(x_t, x_p)                                    # = -A rho e_r: into the plasma
    dt, dp = 2 * np.pi / nt, 2 * np.pi / nphi
    g_tt, g_pp = A**2 * np.ones_like(th), rho**2
    G_diag = -2 * F_closed(np.sqrt(g_tt) * dt / 2, np.sqrt(g_pp) * dp / 2, 0.0) / np.sqrt(g_tt * g_pp)
    return x, n, dt * dp, G_diag


def operators(x, n, w, G_diag, diag):
    d = x[None, :, :] - x[:, None, :]                         # x_j - x_i
    r = np.sqrt(np.sum(d**2, 2)); np.fill_diagonal(r, 1.0)
    G = -w / r
    H = w * np.einsum("jk,ijk->ij", n, d) / r**3
    np.fill_diagonal(G, G_diag); np.fill_diagonal(H, 0.0)
    if diag.startswith("row sum"):
        np.fill_diagonal(H, -4 * np.pi - H.sum(1))
    else:
        np.fill_diagonal(H, -2 * np.pi)
    if diag == "row sum + G lin":
        # calc_GH_1 (vac_diag_style 1): add to G_ii what makes the identity
        # H x - G n_x = -4 pi x hold for x, y, z, projected on the normal
        lin = np.zeros(len(x))
        for k in range(3):
            lin += n[:, k] * (H @ x[:, k] + 4 * np.pi * x[:, k] - G @ n[:, k])
        G[np.arange(len(x)), np.arange(len(x))] += lin / np.sum(n**2, 1)
    return G, H


def potentials(x, n):
    """(phi, dphi, free term c) for interior 1, x, z and the exterior point source."""
    out = [(np.ones(len(x)), np.zeros(len(x)), -4 * np.pi, "1 (interior)"),
           (x[:, 0], n[:, 0], -4 * np.pi, "x (interior)"),
           (x[:, 2], n[:, 2], -4 * np.pi, "z (interior)")]
    dd = x - X0; r = np.linalg.norm(dd, axis=1)
    out.append((1 / r, np.sum(n * (-dd / r[:, None]**3), 1), 0.0, "1/|x-x0| (exterior)"))
    return out


rows = []
nts = (8, 12, 16, 24, 32)
for nt in nts:
    x, n_in, w, Gd = surface(nt)
    for normal, n in (("inward (now)", n_in), ("outward (VMEC before e3b4847)", -n_in)):
        for diag in ("row sum + G lin", "row sum", "-2 pi"):
            if normal.startswith("outward") and diag != "row sum + G lin":
                continue
            G, H = operators(x, n, w, Gd, diag)
            res = {}
            for phi, dphi, c, name in potentials(x, n):
                res[name] = np.max(np.abs(H @ phi - G @ dphi - c * phi)) / np.max(np.abs(4 * np.pi * phi))
            phi, dphi, _, _ = potentials(x, n)[-1]
            Phi = np.linalg.solve(H, G @ dphi)
            res["exterior solve"] = np.max(np.abs(Phi - phi)) / np.max(np.abs(phi))
            rows.append((nt, len(x), normal, diag, res))

names = ["1 (interior)", "x (interior)", "z (interior)", "1/|x-x0| (exterior)", "exterior solve"]
print("max residual of the identity / max|4 pi phi|, and the error of the exterior solve")
print(f"{'n_theta':>7} {'N':>5} {'normal':30} {'diagonals':16} " + " ".join(f"{s:>20}" for s in names))
for nt, N, normal, diag, res in rows:
    print(f"{nt:7d} {N:5d} {normal:30} {diag:16} " + " ".join(f"{res[s]:20.2e}" for s in names))

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10.5, 3.7))
for (normal, diag, c, mk) in (("inward (now)", "row sum + G lin", BLUE, "o"),
                              ("inward (now)", "row sum", GREY, "d"),
                              ("inward (now)", "-2 pi", ORANGE, "s"),
                              ("outward (VMEC before e3b4847)", "row sum + G lin", RED, "^")):
    sel = [r for r in rows if r[2] == normal and r[3] == diag]
    N = [np.sqrt(r[1] / 3) for r in sel]                       # = n_theta
    axes[0].loglog(N, [r[4]["1/|x-x0| (exterior)"] for r in sel], mk + "-", color=c, label=f"{normal}, H diag {diag}")
    axes[1].loglog(N, [r[4]["exterior solve"] for r in sel], mk + "-", color=c, label=f"{normal}, H diag {diag}")
for ax in axes:
    ax.loglog(nts, 0.5 * (nts[0] / np.array(nts)), ":", color=GREY, label="first order")
    ax.loglog(nts, 0.5 * (nts[0] / np.array(nts))**2, "--", color=GREY, label="second order")
    ax.set_xlabel("points per poloidal turn (toroidal: 3x)")
axes[0].set_title("exterior identity H phi - G dphi = 0: residual")
axes[1].set_title("exterior solve H Phi = G dphi: error of Phi")
axes[1].legend(fontsize=7)
save(fig, "torus_bem_toy.png")

Questions to decide before verifying lines

My observations, each with a recommendation; the decision is yours. Write it in this section's notes, one line per question: "yes" (do what is recommended), "no" (leave the code as it is), "after the review", or another option in your own words. Decide before you check the lines of V3 to V11, because V0-a and V0-e change the code those sections show. Each "yes" becomes one commit on dev/vacuum-fixes, and this page is then rebuilt, so that you read the new code only once. "Cleanup" means that no number changes, which the regression anchors and the tools of this page (review/tools/statement_diff.py, review/tools/pure_move_check.py) can show.

V0-a. One routine for the indirect diagonals.

What it is about. Quadrature cannot give the diagonal entries Hii and Gii, because both kernels are singular at j = i: G behaves like 1/r and H like n·r/r³. "Indirect" means that the code chooses Hii and Gii so that the discrete operators satisfy Green's identity on row i,

\[ \sum_j H_{ij}\phi_j - \sum_j G_{ij}\phi'_j = c\,\phi_i , \]

for potentials φ whose boundary values φ and normal data φ′ = n·∇φ are known exactly. The constant c is −4π for a potential that is harmonic inside the boundary, and 0 for one that is harmonic outside and decays. Two pieces of code do this, written separately.

Field-line style, at the end of calc_GH_1, in two steps. In the first step the code uses the potential φ = 1. It is harmonic inside the boundary, so c = −4π, and its normal data are zero, φ′ = 0. Green's identity on row i then contains only entries of H, and Hii is its only unknown, so the identity fixes Hii exactly:

\[ H_{ii} = -4\pi - \sum_{j\ne i} H_{ij} . \]

This is the row-sum rule you already had at 2.47. In the second step the code uses the three potentials φ = x, y and z, the Cartesian coordinates. Each of them is harmonic inside the boundary (c = −4π), and its normal data are the matching component of the stored normal, φ′ = nx, ny and nz. With Hii known from the first step, each of the three identities is an equation for the one remaining unknown, Gii. The off-diagonal entries carry quadrature errors, so the three equations have no common solution. The code therefore takes the value that minimises the sum of the three squared residuals, the least-squares solution:

\[ G_{ii} = \frac{\sum_k n_{k,i}\big[(Hx_k)_i + 4\pi x_{k,i} - \sum_{j\ne i} G_{ij}\, n_{k,j}\big]}{\sum_k n_{k,i}^2} , \]

where k runs over the components x, y and z, and (Hxk)i includes the Hii of the first step.

Axisymmetric style, in diag_indirect_2, in one step. The code uses three potentials: R|n| and R|n|Z, which are harmonic inside the boundary (c = −4π), and the potential of a ring source placed at the centroid of the boundary points, which is harmonic outside and decays (c = 0). For each row i the three identities are three equations for the two unknowns Hii and Gii, and the code takes their least-squares solution. Before the fit it divides each potential and its normal data by the largest value of that potential on the boundary, which puts the three equations on a comparable scale. The constant cannot be used in this style, because for n ≠ 0 every potential has to vary like einζ; R|n| takes its place.

Both styles therefore do the same thing. For each row i they solve, in the least-squares sense over the potentials k, the equations

\[ h\,\phi_{k,i} - g\,\phi'_{k,i} = c_k\phi_{k,i} - \sum_{j\ne i} H_{ij}\phi_{k,j} + \sum_{j\ne i} G_{ij}\phi'_{k,j} \]

for whichever of h = Hii and g = Gii are still unknown.

Found while writing this out. The field-line code does not evaluate the formula for Gii above directly. It starts from the half-cell value g0 that calc_GH_int_1 puts on the diagonal, and adds the correction

\[ \delta = \frac{\sum_k n_{k,i}\, r_{k,i}}{\sum_k n_{k,i}^2}, \qquad r_{k,i} = (Hx_k)_i - (Gn_k)_i + 4\pi x_{k,i} , \]

which is lin_res / sum(norm**2) in the code. The residual rk,i is computed with the full row of G, so it contains the term −g0 nk,i, and δ therefore contains −g0. In the sum g0 + δ the two cancel, and what is left is the formula above. In the default path the half-cell integral is therefore never used: the identities replace it. It matters only with vac_diag_style 2 and in check_vac. The table above said "plus a correction", and the comment in calc_GH_1 says "the identity absorbs it into the diagonal"; both made it sound like a starting value that the identities correct.

The proposal. A routine fit_diag in vac_utilities, next to dis_matvec and dis_diag, solves the equations above for a given list of potentials and a given choice of unknowns. A caller diag_indirect in vac_ops passes each style's potentials to it. For the field-line style it calls fit_diag twice: first for Hii from the constant, then for Gii from x, y and z with the new Hii. For the axisymmetric style it calls fit_diag once, for both entries from the three potentials, each scaled to unit maximum as now. calc_GH calls diag_indirect once for the boundary rows. The contained set_diag of calc_GH_1 and the routine diag_indirect_2 are removed, and both check_vac styles call diag_indirect.

Effect on the numbers. The axisymmetric style and the field-line Hii keep the same arithmetic, so they stay bit-identical. The field-line Gii is computed in one step instead of as half-cell value plus correction. The two are equal in exact arithmetic but differ in rounding, by about 1e-13 in the eigenvalues, as for f3ebf11. The gate is the regression decks with both values of vac_diag_style, the CHECKVAC lines to their printed digits, and the tests vac_3d and exact_exterior_2d_options.

What it gains. The idea lives in one place with one explanation, and the code shows which value is used. check_vac could then report the H and G diagonals for both styles; today only the axisymmetric style reports G. It does not save lines: there are about 150 now and would be about 145 after.

Recommendation (cleanup to rounding level): yes, but with a lower priority than the other cleanups.
V0-b. Keep vac_diag_style as an input?

What it is about. The input vac_diag_style (in num_vars, default 1) chooses how the diagonals are set, for both styles (V6). The value 1 selects the indirect diagonals of V0-a. The value 2 selects the direct ones, which evaluate the singular integrals themselves. For the field-line style, Hii is then −2π plus the integral of the H kernel over the node's cell (calc_diag_direct) wherever a full cell exists, and the row sum at the ends of the lines, where no full cell exists; Gii is the half-cell integral alone. For the axisymmetric style, both entries come from the analytical integrals over the near-singular intervals, and Hii gets the corner term −2β in addition, as at 2.47.

You decided on 6 November that indirect is the default and direct a diagnostic. The direct diagonals are less accurate. On the exact toroidal harmonics (n = 10, 601 points) their errors are 2.1e-3 to 7.7e-3, against 4.6e-5 to 7.4e-4 with the indirect ones, and they fall by a factor 1.8 per doubling of the points instead of 8. On W7-X the eigenvalue with the direct diagonals still moves by 1.4e-4 at 31 000 points.

The choice. If the input stays, a full eigenvalue run with the direct diagonals stays possible. If it goes, production runs always use the indirect ones; check_vac computes the direct diagonals for its comparison whatever the input says. Removing it saves about 30 lines: the vac_diag_style branches in calc_GH_1 and calc_GH_2, and the input lines in num_vars, input_ops and MPI_ops. calc_diag_direct and the corner term stay, because check_vac uses them. What removing it costs is the full solves with the direct diagonals: they produced the W7-X eigenvalue comparison of Documentation/w7x_check_vac_diag.md and the direct HELENA sequence of #28.

Documentation. The input is described only by its comment in num_vars, which Doxygen shows as its documentation, and in the README changelog. Neither says that it is a diagnostic. The comment would become:

    integer :: vac_diag_style = 1                                               !< diagonal of the vacuum operators: 1 indirect (from identities, the default), 2 direct (corner term and cell integral; a diagnostic to compare with 1, not for production runs)
Recommendation: keep the input and change that one comment.
V0-e. Comments that tell the history.

What it is about. A search for "issue #4" and for dates finds 14 new comments. Twelve of them name issue #4 (vac_ops 3, vac_utilities 2, SLEPC_ops 2, VMEC_ops 2, and MPI_utilities, VMEC_utilities and input_ops 1 each), and two more carry only a date. Some of them tell the old error at length, for example "the response of the circular VMEC twin came out 3 to 4 times too small". Your 2.47 comments say what the code does. For example, the comment on the G diagonal in calc_GH_1 now reads:

            ! G: the identity H x - G norm_x = -4 pi x for the linear interior
            ! harmonics x, y, z, projected on the normal: the analytical
            ! half-cell integral of calc_GH_int_1 is exact for the singular
            ! cell, but the one-point rule across the neighbouring field lines
            ! leaves a first-order error that depends on the lattice of
            ! points; the identity absorbs it into the diagonal, as the row
            ! sum does for H (issue #4, 31 October 2026)

It would become the following, which also corrects what V0-a found (the identities replace the half-cell value; they do not correct it):

            ! G: G_ii is the least-squares fit, row by row, to the identities
            ! H x - G norm_x = -4 pi x for the linear interior harmonics
            ! x, y, z; it replaces the half-cell value of calc_GH_int_1, so
            ! that the diagonal carries the quadrature error of the
            ! off-diagonal row, as the row sum does for H

The history stays in the commit messages and in Documentation/plan_vacuum_bugfix.md. Only comments change, and review/tools/statement_diff.py shows that no statement did.

Recommendation (cleanup): yes. Keep the sentence that says why the code is as it is, and drop the dates, the step numbers and the account of the old error. It is the same rule as your removal of the "moved to X" comments. It takes 1 to 2 h.
V0-f. Four stale comments.
  1. In solve_Phi_BEM, two comments say "solve (H + shift I) Phi = G R", but there has been no shift since f3ebf11 (5 November). The fix is to write "solve H Phi = G R".
  2. The full-stack test greens_identity_indirect (tests/fullstack/test_vac_greens.f90) calls the direct diagonals "the default of this style", but since 49e2441 the indirect ones are the default for both styles. The fix is to drop those words.
  3. calc_GH_int_2 declares and computes n_loc and dn_loc but never uses them, as already at 2.47. The fix is to delete the two declarations and the two assignments.
  4. The header of set_BC_4 says that style 4 differs from style 2 by 0.7 % on cbm18a. Since the edge weight of F5 the difference is 0.19 % (anchors −4.5051e-2 and −4.5136e-2). The fix is to correct the number.
Recommendation: fix them now. They have no effect on results and take a few minutes.

Vacuum verification

Routine by routine, in the order the data flows. From this stage on the page shows dev/vacuum-fixes at b41fd8a, the code after the pull requests #31 to #33 of the V0 decisions, #34 of read_VMEC, your V1 commit 59c6e90 and the pull requests #37 and #38 of 18 November (section D); its GitHub links point there. Each group shows the 2.47 routine against the routine at b41fd8a as one diff, with the commits that touched those lines. Use "hide comment-only diff lines" in the index for a first pass over the code alone: a quarter of the changed lines in vac_ops are comments.

V1

Vacuum plumbing outside the vacuum modules

files driver_eq, driver_sol, driver_POST, sol_ops, input_ops, num_vars, MPI_ops, PB3D_opstime 30 minread
  • Fixed boundary skips the vacuum (ad2313b): store_vac and calc_vac_res are not called for BC_style(2) = 1, and POST does not read a vacuum that is not in the output.
  • The vacuum energy in POST (212e3ec): the term E_pot(7) was switched off at 2.47 (1.eq.2 and a "NO VACUUM" print); it is on whenever vac%res exists.
  • Inputs: alpha_style 1 with a free boundary and VMEC is refused (cc4c96d); a warning when n_alpha and the field period share a factor, because the average over the lines then aliases the field-period harmonic (50c9511); check_vac (6894199) and vac_diag_style (e027949, default 1 since 49e2441), both broadcast in MPI_ops. Since your decision V0-b (bba7922), the comment of vac_diag_style in num_vars calls style 2 a diagnostic, and a free-boundary run with vac_diag_style 2 prints the warning "vac_diag_style 2 is a diagnostic, less accurate than 1: not for production runs".
  • Comments without history (f0273a7, your decision V0-e): the comment of the n_alpha warning in input_ops no longer names issue #4 or a date. It also rewrote the comment on par_lims_found in PB3D_ops, but 59c6e90 removed that line, so nothing of the commit is left in PB3D_ops; its card still links the reconstruct_PB3D_vac block, because git log -L counts the removed line as part of that block.
  • POST plot wiring (a8804ac): the plot is called once for all plotted modes after the mode loop; the plot ranges default to 0, which means "from the boundary". The commit also had reconstruct_PB3D_vac rebuild the parallel angle of the field-line style from two entries it appended to misc_vac.
  • The parallel angle in the output (59c6e90, your V1 change): print_output_vac writes vac%ang for both styles, and reconstruct_PB3D_vac reads it for both, before the style branch, as it reads norm and x_vec. For the field-line style the stored angle has n_par_X × n_alpha entries, one per boundary point. The two limits in misc_vac, the four local variables that rebuilt the angle from them (par_lims, dpar, id, par_lims_found) and the case of an output without the limits are gone, so misc_vac has its six entries of 2.47 again. In reconstruct_PB3D_vac the 2.47 → b41fd8a diff is now the rename of stage 1, the read of ang moved out of the axisymmetric case, and two blank lines that lost their trailing spaces (a8804ac had added lines after them, which 59c6e90 removed). On the VMEC twin (8 field lines, two Richardson levels) and the circular HELENA case the eigenvalues and every POST output file are bit-identical to those of 593020a (its commit message).
How to check it
  1. Read the driver blocks below the cards: the two calls are skipped for BC_style(2) = 1 in driver_eq, driver_sol and driver_POST alike.
  2. Read the sol_ops condition for E_pot(7) and the input guards in input_ops.
  3. Check that the two new inputs are broadcast (MPI_ops) and defaulted (input_ops), and that the warning for vac_diag_style 2 is printed only for a free boundary.
  4. Read reconstruct_PB3D_vac next to print_output_vac (V11): the same six entries of misc_vac on both sides, and ang written and read for both styles under the same name.

commit message
Since 2.44 the vacuum was hard-disabled with 'Vacuum has not been
implemented yet!' errors, which made ALL HELENA runs die in the
equilibrium driver and let VMEC runs compute an (unused, unverified)
3-D vacuum response every Richardson level.

* driver_eq/driver_sol/driver_POST now skip vacuum storage,
  calculation and reconstruction when BC_style(2) = 1 (fixed-boundary
  edge BC), where the vacuum response is genuinely not used. The
  remaining guards for free-boundary styles are untouched.
* Verified: HELENA fixed-boundary runs work again end-to-end (first
  time since 2.44); VMEC fixed-boundary eigenvalue is bit-identical
  with and without the previously wasted vacuum computation.
* vac_ops hygiene: leftover unconditional plot_HDF5('EP',...) in
  calc_vac_res is now behind ldebug/debug_calc_vac_res (it tried to
  write into a nonexistent Data/ directory on every free-boundary
  call); guarded sec_X against double allocation on the reconstruction
  path.

commit message
calc_vac_res now returns the surface-energy Hessian as it enters A: the
Neumann-to-Dirichlet map of the BEM times -2 pi (the sign from the exterior
map being negative definite, the 2 pi from the toroidal integral that A
carries; derivation in the comment), then its Hermitian part (the
discretization left an asymmetry of 1e-5 that SLEPc took for a complex
eigenvalue). set_BC_2, set_BC_4 and POST use res unchanged; POST's vacuum
term is no longer disabled.

The factor was measured before it was written: on the eps = 0.05 circular
external kink, -2 pi reproduces MISHKA without a wall to 0.3-0.8 % at
n = 10, 15, 20, while -1 and -4 pi are 60-80 % off. On cbm18a at psi = 0.75
the ordering no-vacuum <= free <= fixed now holds, and POST's energy
balance closes to 0.07 % with the vacuum term in.

Tests: check_vac_res.py (response Hermitian and positive semi-definite,
run on the free-boundary regression), regression_circ_eps005_free_bnd
(fixed stable, free -0.43034 anchored at 1e-3 and MISHKA's 0.42679 at 2 %),
the cylinder unit-test reference multiplied by the same factor; all
committed *.12.xz fixtures are decompressed at configure time.

commit message
alpha_style 1 (one field line, many turns, Weyl surface sampling) is
not numerically preferable in the current formulation: PB3D only uses
surface-averaged coefficients, for which the explicit field-line grid
of alpha_style 2 converges spectrally while single-line equidistribution
converges at the discrepancy rate, is frozen during Richardson
extrapolation (fixed line length), and would need per-point transverse
spacings (three-distance theorem) for the free-boundary vacuum. It is
kept as a legacy/cross-check mode.

* input_ops: free-boundary 3-D runs (eq_style 1, BC_style(2) /= 1) with
  alpha_style 1 are now rejected at input processing with a clear
  message, instead of failing later in the equilibrium driver.
* vac_ops header, openwiki: the single-line vacuum spacing is
  documented as deliberately not implemented rather than an open item;
  input-and-configuration explains the style choice.

commit message
- calc_GH_1 and calc_vac_res space the field lines by (max_alpha - min_alpha)
  pi / n_alpha, as rich_ops lays them out (end point excluded), instead of
  / (n_alpha - 1); test_vac_3d builds its grid the same way. New full-stack
  test point_source_3d: a point source inside the surface gives an exterior
  harmonic potential with exact normal data, and the style-1 solve returns
  its trace to 2 % at 81 x 80 with first-order convergence, on the circular
  and on a rippled torus. This pins the normal orientation, the alpha
  weights and the exterior solve; the style-1 against style-2 ratios now
  converge to 1 at first order (the old agreement at m = 1 was the
  duplicated line cancelling a near-singular solve).
- calc_GH zeroes G and H before the assembly accumulates into them, so the
  interlaced copy of the previous Richardson level is not counted twice: on
  W7-X the level-2 response equals a fresh run at that resolution bit for
  bit.
- read_input_eq warns when n_alpha and the VMEC field period share a factor
  (the toroidal average then aliases the harmonic LCM(n_alpha, N_fp)).
- check_vac_res.py reads the VMEC vacuum groups (vac_R_<level>) as well.

Review of the cloud commits 429f003 and d6d49e6: every hunk kept. Open:
6e and 6f (VMEC twins), and the W7-X response, which is unconverged at 16
field lines (29 % between 61 and 121 parallel points, not positive definite
at 121).

commit message
The diagonals of the vacuum operators H and G can now be set either from
the identities that the discrete operators must satisfy for known
potentials (indirect, vac_diag_style 1) or from the corner term and the
integral of the kernel over the node's cell (direct, vac_diag_style 2),
for both vacuum styles. Indirect in the field-line style is the existing
row sum for the constant and the identities for the linear interior
harmonics; in the axisymmetric style it is new: a least-squares fit, row
by row, to the identities for R^n, R^n Z (interior, free term -4 pi) and
the n-mode Green's function of a ring source at the centroid (exterior,
free term 0). Direct in the axisymmetric style is the existing chord
angle with the analytical near-singular integrals; in the field-line
style it is new: -2 pi plus the cell integral of calc_diag_direct for H
(the row sum at the end points of the lines, which have no full cell)
and the analytical cell integral of calc_GH_int_1 for G. The default, 0,
keeps each style's previous choice until the benchmark of both settings
is done; solve_Phi_BEM is untouched.

Two new full-stack tests: greens_identity_indirect (axisymmetric, the
three identities with the indirect diagonals hold to 1e-5, by
construction) and point_source_direct_3d (field-line, the point-source
solve with the direct diagonals converges: errors 1.9e-2 -> 6.4e-3 on the
torus at 41 x 40 -> 81 x 80, against 1.0e-2 -> 3.1e-3 with the row sum).
Unit, full-stack and the four regression decks pass unchanged with the
default.

commit message
The benchmark of the two diagonal options (full-stack test
exact_exterior_2d_options, the exact toroidal harmonics of the circular
torus with n = 10, k = 6, 10, 15 through the axisymmetric style) decides
the default: with the indirect diagonals of diag_indirect_2 the solution
errors at 601 boundary points are 4.6e-5, 2.2e-4 and 7.4e-4, against
2.1e-3, 4.6e-3 and 7.7e-3 with the direct ones (the chord angle and the
analytical near-singular integrals), and they fall by a factor 8 per
doubling of the points instead of 1.8. The first-order convergence of
the axisymmetric vacuum in HELENA's poloidal points, measured on 1
November, was the error of its diagonal. On the circular external kinks
at 257 HELENA points the free-boundary eigenvalue moves from -0.42452 to
-0.42562 at epsilon = 0.05 (MISHKA converged: -0.42679) and from
-0.43679 to -0.43802 at epsilon = 0.33 (TERPSICHORE converged:
-0.43848), closer to the references than the direct option at 1025
points. For the field-line style the row sum was already the default
(point-source solve on the torus 3.1e-3 at 81 x 80 against 6.4e-3 with
the direct diagonals). cbm18a free with BC style 2 moves from -4.5046e-2 to -4.5051e-2 (0.01 %: the pedestal mode is only weakly coupled to the vacuum), with style 4 from -4.5130e-2 to -4.5136e-2.

vac_diag_style is 1 (indirect) by default and 2 (direct) on request;
the value 0 is gone. The anchors of the HELENA free-boundary regression
decks are set to the new values; the fixed-boundary and VMEC anchors are
unchanged.

commit message
plot_vac_pot plots the vacuum potential of the computed eigenmodes outside
the plasma for the axisymmetric (vac%style 2) and the field-line (vac%style 1)
vacuum. The stub in driver_POST that switched it off since April 2018 and the
VMEC block in input_ops are gone; a fixed boundary skips it.

- vac_pot_plot rewritten: normal data of calc_vac_res (dphi = -i(nq-m)X along
  -J grad psi, the field-line basis for style 1, exp(-im theta) times
  exp(in zeta_F) for style 2), boundary potential from solve_Phi_BEM, potential
  off the boundary from Green's representation (eval_pot_ext); one solve and
  one set of external rows for all plotted modes; planes in zeta_F as the
  plasma plots; box in metres, by default from the boundary; outputs
  [id]_vac_pot_RE/IM, Data/[id]_vac_bnd.dat, vac_in_plasma.
- Near the boundary: subtraction of the interior harmonic matching the
  nearest boundary value (sub_nearest; to first order through 1, x, y, z for
  style 1, R^|n| for style 2); field-line near-field rule for external points
  only within an interval length of the boundary (its zone edge left a
  second-order error farther out).
- check_vac: exact exterior potentials evaluated off the boundary from exact
  and from solved boundary data (CHECKVAC exterior lines).
- misc_vac holds the parallel limits; POST rebuilds the field-line angles.
- Fixed: out-of-bounds reads of external points in calc_GH_1 and calc_GH_2;
  interlaced_vac_copy writing past vac%ang; the tolerance gather in calc_GH_2
  (the same on all processes) removed.
- Figure Documentation/figures/vacuum_plot/vac_pot_circular.png (circular
  HELENA case and its VMEC twin) and its script.

vac_vars and the distributed-matrix helpers

files vac_vars, vac_utilities (helpers), headers of vac_ops and vac_utilitiestime 30 minread
  • STRUMPACK optional: #ifdef PB3D_WITH_STRUMPACK; without it BLACSCTXTSIZE, numroc and indxl2g are declared locally and the solve uses ScaLAPACK LU.
  • ang, dnorm and h_fac are now allocated for both styles (three style branches gone); h_fac lost its fourth column, which held the 2.47 field-line H diagonal factor.
  • loc_idx replaces about twenty copies of the local-index sum of the block-cyclic layout.
  • New helpers in vac_utilities: n_col1_loc, vec_glob2dis, dis_matvec (a distributed matrix times a global vector, used by the identity diagonals and check_vac) and dis_diag. They were in the test utilities first and moved here (fe305fd).
  • The plot commit a8804ac also fixed interlaced_vac_copy, which wrote past the end of vac%ang.

The commit that introduced loc_idx and removed the style branches of the allocation (028735c, "four mechanical simplifications") claims no change of results. The tool below lists its statement changes without comments and whitespace: the 22 copies of the local-index sum become loc_idx calls, the H sign of calc_GH_int_2 moves from a final H = -H into the three formulas, the style branches of the allocation go, and the field-line style stores its parallel angle. In appendix A the commit leaves all nine eigenvalues the same, bit for bit.

"""What a commit changed in the Fortran statements, ignoring comments,
blank lines, whitespace, and the lines that only restructure code.

For a refactoring commit (code moved into contained procedures, a repeated
expression replaced by a function) the full diff is long while the change of
statements is short. This prints, for the given commit and files, the code
lines that were removed and not added back, and those added and not removed
before (multisets, comments and trailing comments stripped, whitespace
normalised). What remains is what to read.

Run from the repository root:
    python3 review/tools/statement_diff.py 225aa72 Modules/vac_ops.f90
    python3 review/tools/statement_diff.py 028735c Modules/vac_ops.f90 Modules/vac_utilities.f90 Modules/vac_vars.f90
"""
import re
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from collections import Counter


os.chdir(subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], capture_output=True, text=True,
                      check=True, cwd=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))).stdout.strip())


def git(*a):
    return subprocess.run(["git", *a], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout


def code_part(line):
    """The statement part of a Fortran line: trailing comment (outside quotes) removed."""
    out, quote = [], None
    for ch in line.strip():
        if quote:
            out.append(ch)
            if ch == quote:
                quote = None
        elif ch in "'\"":
            quote = ch
            out.append(ch)
        elif ch == "!":
            break
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", "".join(out)).strip()


def statements(diff, sign):
    lines = [l[1:] for l in diff.splitlines() if l.startswith(sign) and not l.startswith(sign * 3)]
    return Counter(c for c in (code_part(l) for l in lines) if c)


def main(sha, files):
    diff = git("show", "--format=", "-U0", sha, "--", *files)
    rem, add = statements(diff, "-"), statements(diff, "+")
    subj = git("show", "-s", "--format=%h %ad %s", "--date=short", sha).strip()
    print(f"== {subj}")
    print(f"   statements removed {sum(rem.values())}, added {sum(add.values())}, "
          f"identical on both sides {sum((rem & add).values())}")
    print("   removed and not added back:")
    for k, v in (rem - add).items():
        print(f"     - {k}" + (f"   (x{v})" if v > 1 else ""))
    print("   added and not there before:")
    for k, v in (add - rem).items():
        print(f"     + {k}" + (f"   (x{v})" if v > 1 else ""))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = sys.argv[1:] or ["225aa72", "Modules/vac_ops.f90"]
    main(args[0], args[1:] or ["Modules/"])
How to check it
  1. Read loc_idx (six lines) against one of the 2.47 index sums in the tool's output.
  2. Read the vac_vars diff: the #ifdef around STRUMPACK, the allocation of ang, dnorm, h_fac for both styles.
  3. Read dis_matvec and dis_diag in the helper group; the identity diagonals (V6) and check_vac use them.

V3

store_vac: geometry and normal

routine store_vactime 30 minread

The field-line branch (store_vac_VMEC) is split into three named steps: restore_previous_level (Richardson: keep, interlace or reconstruct the previous level), store_geometry (points, normal, metric factors of this equilibrium job, on the last process) and broadcast_geometry. The changes inside them:

  • The normal is −J∇ψ (one minus sign, e3b4847). With +J∇ψ the off-diagonal H had the wrong sign, the row sum then set a wrong diagonal, and the response of the circular VMEC twin was 0.27 of the HELENA one. With −J∇ψ: 0.80 at 64 lines, and after the near-field rule (V4) 0.98 to 0.99.
  • h_fac stores gαα, gαθ, gθθ; the 2.47 fourth column (a factor for the old H diagonal) is gone.
  • vac%ang now holds the parallel angle of every point, for the POST plot; since 59c6e90 the output holds it too (V11).
  • The axisymmetric branch (store_vac_HEL) is the 2.47 code; the July commit 3679ee7 only removed its stop.
How to check it
  1. Find the minus sign in norm_com_C in store_geometry and compare with the axisymmetric normal of store_vac_HEL, also −J∇ψ (its comment says "− R (Z_θ ∇R − R_θ ∇Z)").
  2. Read the three named steps against the 2.47 block: the split changed no statement except the step sizes, which now come from vac_steps (V8 has the tool output for that commit).

vac_ops.f90 lines now: 63–504 (store_vac); at 2.47: 52–469 (store_vac). Line numbers in the diff are file line numbers (left: 2.47, right: now).

V4

Field-line kernels and calc_GH_1

routines calc_GH, calc_GH_1, calc_GH_int_1time 1.5 hstudy

calc_GH. G and H are set to zero before both styles accumulate into them. After a Richardson step the field-line arrays still held the interlaced copy of the previous level, so 2.47 counted those contributions twice. Since your decision V0-a (937d6a8), calc_GH also sets the diagonals of the boundary rows for both styles, after the assembly of the style; V6 explains that block.

calc_GH_int_1, the kernels on one interval of a field line, is rewritten:

  • Far from the influence point: the kernel values at the two ends (the trapezoidal rule along the line), with H = n·(xs−x)/r³. 2.47 had (-G)**(-3) = r³ instead of 1/r³.
  • At the singular point: the exact integral of 1/r over the half cell in the metric of the surface (the closed form F(U, V, s) in the comment and in the demo). The 2.47 expression had the same logarithm twice and diverged like 1/s² for perpendicular coordinates. H gets 0 there; calc_GH sets the diagonals afterwards (V6).
  • Near the influence point (within n_near = 4 interval lengths, a parameter): 8-point Gauss–Legendre on each half interval, on the cubic interpolant through a four-point stencil. This is the fix of 31 October for W7-X: at the inboard bean tips neighbouring lines are 0.007 R₀ apart and the points along them 0.06 R₀, so the kernel along the neighbouring line is a peak much narrower than the point spacing. The point rule then gives order-one errors whose sign depends on how the points of neighbouring lines line up; the diagonal of vac%res on W7-X ranged from 44 to 126 depending on the grid (7 000 to 62 000 boundary points), sorted by the fractional part of q Δθ/Δα. With the near-field rule the five grids from 64 × 121 to 144 × 121 and 128 × 141 agree to 1.2 % on the whole diagonal, and the circular twin's free eigenvalue went from −0.5189 to −0.4491 against HELENA's −0.4438. The demo shows the same effect on a straight line.
  • The interval that bridges two field lines is skipped before any evaluation (2.47 evaluated it and dropped it with on_field_line).

calc_GH_1: the contributions get the weight Δp Δα / 2 per half interval, so G and H are true surface operators (consistent with the absolute −4π of the row sum); the α step is 2π/nα (vac_steps; 2.47 used 2π/(nα−1), 50c9511); at least 2 lines and 4 points per line are required. Since V0-a it only assembles the rows: the diagonal block at its end and its contained set_diag are gone, and the diagonals are in V6.

How to check it
  1. Half-cell demo: the closed form against brute-force quadrature for perpendicular, skewed and very anisotropic cells (agreement to 1e-14); then read the singular branch of calc_GH_int_1 against the formula in its comment.
  2. Near-field demo: the point rule's error for the dipole kernel on a neighbouring line at d/h = 0.12 ranges from −89 % to +318 % with the offset of the points; the near-field rule stays below 3e-3. Then read the near branch: stencil parameter s, Lagrange weights l, the factor 0.5 for the half interval.
  3. Tests: GH_int_1_singular (brute force), GH_int_1_near (tolerance 3e-3, the error of the cubic interpolant), GH_int_1_regular, greens_identity_3d, point_source_3d, response_1_vs_2 (field-line style on an axisymmetric torus against the axisymmetric style: ratios 1.006 to 0.996, recorded).

script
"""Area 4c: the singular half-cell integral of the field-line G (vac_utilities.calc_GH_int_1).

Near the influence point the squared distance on the surface is the quadratic
form g_tt dp^2 + 2 g_at dp da + g_aa da^2 (p along the field line, a the line
label). With the metric-normalised half-cell sizes
    U = sqrt(g_tt) dp/2,   V = sqrt(g_aa) da/2,   s = g_at / sqrt(g_aa g_tt),
the code uses the primitive
    F = int_0^U int_-V^V du dv / sqrt(u^2 + 2 s u v + v^2)
      = U ln((V + sU + D+)/(-V + sU + D-)) + V ln((U + sV + D+)/(-U + sV + D-)),
    D+- = sqrt(U^2 +- 2 s U V + V^2).
This script checks the closed form against brute-force quadrature in polar
coordinates around the singular corner (which removes the 1/r singularity),
for perpendicular and strongly skewed cells and very different aspect ratios.

It also evaluates the bracket of the 2.47 expression,
    ln|(d2 + E + s)/(d1 - E + s)| - E/s^2 ln|(d2 + E + s)/(d1 - E + s)|,
with E = V/U (the same logarithm twice), to show that it diverges like 1/s^2
for a cell with perpendicular sides (s -> 0), where the integral is finite.
"""
import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import quad

from _common import BLUE, ORANGE, plt, save


def F_closed(U, V, s):
    Dp = np.sqrt(U**2 + 2 * s * U * V + V**2)
    Dm = np.sqrt(U**2 - 2 * s * U * V + V**2)
    return U * np.log(abs((V + s * U + Dp) / (-V + s * U + Dm))) + \
        V * np.log(abs((U + s * V + Dp) / (-U + s * V + Dm)))


def F_brute(U, V, s):
    """Rectangle [0,U] x [-V,V] split into two triangles-fans from the origin (polar)."""
    def over(phi_a, phi_b, rmax):
        def inner(phi):
            c, d = np.cos(phi), np.sin(phi)
            q = np.sqrt(c * c + 2 * s * c * d + d * d)        # r^2 (c,d) -> distance factor
            return rmax(phi) / q                              # int_0^rmax r dr / (r q) = rmax / q
        return quad(inner, phi_a, phi_b, epsabs=1e-13, epsrel=1e-13, limit=200)[0]
    pc = np.arctan2(V, U)                                     # corner angles
    tot = 0.0
    tot += over(-pc, pc, lambda p: U / np.cos(p))             # right edge u = U
    tot += over(pc, np.pi / 2, lambda p: V / np.sin(p))       # top edge v = V
    tot += over(-np.pi / 2, -pc, lambda p: V / -np.sin(p))    # bottom edge v = -V
    return tot


def old_bracket(U, V, s):
    E = V / U
    d1 = np.sqrt(1 + 2 * E * s + E**2)
    d2 = np.sqrt(1 - 2 * E * s + E**2)
    L = np.log(abs((d2 + E + s) / (d1 - E + s)))
    return L - E / s**2 * L


print(f"{'U':>6} {'V':>6} {'s':>6} {'closed form':>14} {'brute force':>14} {'rel diff':>9}")
for U, V, s in [(1, 1, 0.0), (1, 1, 0.5), (1, 1, -0.9), (0.1, 1, 0.3), (1, 0.05, 0.95), (2.5, 0.4, -0.6)]:
    a, b = F_closed(U, V, s), F_brute(U, V, s)
    print(f"{U:6.2f} {V:6.2f} {s:6.2f} {a:14.10f} {b:14.10f} {abs(a - b) / b:9.1e}")

ss = np.linspace(-0.95, 0.95, 400)
ss = ss[np.abs(ss) > 0.01]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.6, 3.6))
ax.plot(ss, [F_closed(1, 1, s) for s in ss], color=BLUE, label="F, closed form (now)")
ax.plot(ss, [old_bracket(1, 1, s) for s in ss], color=ORANGE, label="2.47 bracket")
ax.set_ylim(-20, 20)
ax.set_xlabel("skew s = g_at / sqrt(g_aa g_tt)")
ax.set_title("half-cell integral for U = V = 1")
ax.legend(fontsize=8)
save(fig, "halfcell_integral.png")

script
"""Area 4c: why the field-line kernels need a near-field rule (commit 0bbda47).

On W7-X the field lines at the inboard bean tips run almost toroidally, so
neighbouring lines lie much closer together (median 0.007 R_0 at 128 lines)
than the points along each line (0.06 R_0). Seen from a point on one line,
the kernel along the neighbouring line is a peak of width ~d (the line
distance) sampled at spacing h >> d.

Model: a straight neighbouring line at distance d from the influence point,
points x_k = (k + f) h, k = -K..K, where f in [0, 1) is the offset of the
points relative to the closest approach (on W7-X, set by frac(q dtheta /
dalpha) of the grid). Integrals over |x| <= L:

    G-like:  int dx / sqrt(d^2 + x^2)          = 2 asinh(L/d)
    H-like:  int d dx / (d^2 + x^2)^(3/2)      = 2 L / (d sqrt(d^2 + L^2))

Rules: (1) the point rule (trapezoidal along the line, as calc_GH_int_1 at
2.47 and now far from the influence point); (2) the near-field rule of
calc_GH_int_1 now: within n_near = 4 interval lengths, 8-point Gauss-Legendre
on each half interval (here on the exact straight line; PB3D uses the cubic
interpolant through four points, exact for a straight line).
The error of the point rule is of order one and its sign depends on f: this
is how every W7-X grid got sorted into too large or plausible responses.
"""
import numpy as np

from _common import BLUE, GREEN, ORANGE, RED, plt, save

xg, wg = np.polynomial.legendre.leggauss(8)
h, K = 1.0, 40
L = K * h


def rules(d, f):
    xk = (np.arange(-K, K + 1) + f) * h
    xk = xk[np.abs(xk) <= L]
    exact_G = 2 * np.arcsinh(L / d)
    exact_H = 2 * L / (d * np.sqrt(d**2 + L**2))
    gk = 1 / np.sqrt(d**2 + xk**2)
    hk = d / (d**2 + xk**2) ** 1.5
    # point rule (trapezoid) on the sampled part + exact tails to |x| = L
    def tails(fun_int):
        return fun_int(L) - fun_int(xk[-1]) + fun_int(-xk[0]) - fun_int(L)
    G_int = lambda x: np.arcsinh(x / d)                     # noqa: E731
    H_int = lambda x: x / (d * np.sqrt(d**2 + x**2))        # noqa: E731
    w = np.full(xk.size, h); w[0] = w[-1] = h / 2
    pt_G = np.sum(w * gk) + (G_int(L) - G_int(xk[-1])) + (G_int(xk[0]) - G_int(-L))
    pt_H = np.sum(w * hk) + (H_int(L) - H_int(xk[-1])) + (H_int(xk[0]) - H_int(-L))
    # near-field rule: Gauss on the intervals within 4 h of the closest approach
    nf_G, nf_H = pt_G, pt_H
    for i in range(xk.size - 1):
        a, b = xk[i], xk[i + 1]
        if min(abs(a), abs(b)) < 4 * h:
            # remove the trapezoid of this interval, add Gauss on its two halves
            nf_G -= h / 2 * (gk[i] + gk[i + 1]); nf_H -= h / 2 * (hk[i] + hk[i + 1])
            for lo, hi in ((a, 0.5 * (a + b)), (0.5 * (a + b), b)):
                x = 0.5 * (hi - lo) * xg + 0.5 * (hi + lo)
                nf_G += 0.5 * (hi - lo) * np.sum(wg / np.sqrt(d**2 + x**2))
                nf_H += 0.5 * (hi - lo) * np.sum(wg * d / (d**2 + x**2) ** 1.5)
    return [(pt_G - exact_G) / exact_G, (pt_H - exact_H) / exact_H,
            (nf_G - exact_G) / exact_G, (nf_H - exact_H) / exact_H]


fs = np.linspace(0, 1, 101)[:-1]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10.5, 3.6), sharex=True)
print(f"{'d/h':>5} {'point rule G: min..max':>24} {'point rule H: min..max':>24} {'near rule H: max':>17}")
for d, c in ((0.12, RED), (0.25, ORANGE), (0.5, GREEN), (1.0, BLUE)):
    e = np.array([rules(d, f) for f in fs])
    axes[0].plot(fs, 100 * e[:, 1], color=c, label=f"d/h = {d}")
    axes[1].semilogy(fs, np.abs(e[:, 3]) + 1e-17, color=c, label=f"d/h = {d}")
    print(f"{d:5.2f} {100*e[:,0].min():10.2f} .. {100*e[:,0].max():6.2f} %   "
          f"{100*e[:,1].min():8.1f} .. {100*e[:,1].max():8.1f} %   {np.abs(e[:,3]).max():14.1e}")
axes[0].set_title("point rule, H-like kernel: error in %")
axes[0].set_xlabel("offset f of the points (fraction of h)")
axes[0].set_ylim(-110, 400)
axes[1].set_title("near-field rule (8-pt Gauss within 4 h): |relative error|")
axes[1].set_xlabel("offset f of the points (fraction of h)")
axes[0].legend(fontsize=8); axes[1].legend(fontsize=8)
save(fig, "near_field_lines.png")
print("W7-X bean tips: d/h ~ 0.007/0.06 = 0.12 (median at 128 lines).")

The α step 2π/nα is guarded by response_1_vs_2: since commit 798fe50 (30 October) it compares the field-line to axisymmetric ratio of res(m, m) with recorded values to 0.5 %, and the old step 2π/(nα−1) moved them by 1.25 % (comment in the test). A mutation test on 30 October, before those recorded values, had not caught it.

Recorded decision (6 November). n_near = 4 stays, with a note to re-evaluate it once you have digested the vacuum work. The comment in calc_GH_int_1 points to issue #9 since V0-e.

471    !> Calculate the matrices \c G and \c H.472    !!473    !! This  is  done  by  iterating  over  the  subintervals,  calculating  the474    !! contributions to the  potential values on the left and  right boundary of475    !! the interval, and adding these to the appropriate values in G and H.476    !!477    !! As each process in  the blacs grid only has access to  its own values, an478    !! extra interval  is is calculated  to the left  and right of  the internal479    !! process grid edges.480    !!481    !! Optionally, this  procedure can be  used to calculate the  coefficients G482    !! and H  with respect  to other  points, outside of  the boundary.  This is483    !! useful when the potential is to be calculated at external points.484    !!485    !! In this case, however, no (near-)  singular points are calculated, and if486    !! they appear any way, perhaps by accident, they will not be accurate.487    !!488    !! \Note Multiple  field lines are  stored sequentially, which  implies that489    !! the integral between the  last point on a field line  and the first point490    !! on the next field lines needs to be left out.491    !!492    !! \todo For  3-D vacuums,  step sizes  are constant. Axisymmetric kernels and calc_GH_2

routines calc_GH_2, calc_GH_int_2time 40 minread

This is the part closest to your 2.47 code.

  • calc_GH_int_2: the three H formulas change sign (normal derivative along the stored −J∇ψ). Since V0-f (ebd972c) the variables n_loc and dn_loc, which 2.47 computed and never used, are removed. Nothing else.
  • calc_GH_2: the corner term is −2β with β the vacuum's internal angle (as at 2.47); the toroidal functions use |n| (Q−ν−1 = Qν for the half-integer degrees), so negative n works; the tolerance on ρ is computed from the boundary points every process holds, without a gather, so that the BLACS processes alone can call it with external points; an external point within the tolerance of a boundary point gets the row 4π φj of that point. Since V0-a its end no longer sets the indirect diagonals; calc_GH does (V6).

The plot commit a8804ac also fixed out-of-bounds reads for external points in calc_GH_1 and calc_GH_2, and removed the gather of the tolerance in calc_GH_2, which is the same on every process.

History, for orientation: 2 November (f407afa) changed the corner term to the plasma's angle 2π − β, because the kernels were then the plasma's; 5 November (f3ebf11) flipped the kernels to the vacuum's and returned to −2β. Net change against 2.47: only the H sign in calc_GH_int_2. In appendix A, f407afa moves the circular ε = 0.05 free eigenvalue by 0.67 % and cbm18a free by 1.4e-4, and f3ebf11 then moves nothing by more than 1e-13: the result changed with the corner term of 2 November, and the flip of 5 November kept it.

How to check it
  1. In calc_GH_int_2, check that the three H expressions changed sign and nothing else (the classifier cannot say this for the vacuum groups; the diff is short).
  2. Read the corner-term block at the end of the row loop of calc_GH_2 against eq. (146).
  3. Read the external-point branch (the 4π row) and the n_abs changes.

Tests: asymptote, G_regular, H_regular_numderiv (H against a numerical derivative of G along the source normal), GH_singular_quadrature, GH_edge_correction, greens_identity, exact_exterior_2d (exact toroidal harmonics of the circular torus; on 2 November, with the direct diagonals of that time, 0.19 to 1.07 % at 301 points).

V6

Diagonals: indirect and direct

routines the diagonal block of calc_GH, diag_indirect, set_pot_2, set_diag_vac; fit_diag, vac_steps, solid_angle_node, H_sing_node, calc_diag_direct, dis_diagtime 1 hstudy

Input vac_diag_style: 1 indirect (default), 2 direct.

  • Field-line, indirect: Hii from the row sum (as 2.47); Gii = the least-squares solution, one per row, of H x − G nx = −4π x for x, y, z. Until V0-a the code wrote it as the analytical half-cell value plus a correction in which the half-cell value cancelled (V0-a); since then it computes the fit in one step. The identities (31 October) put the error of the one-point rule across neighbouring lines into the diagonal.
  • Field-line, direct: Hii = −2π + the integral of the H kernel over the cell (calc_diag_direct, with H_sing_node = the corrected eq. 69 of the manuscript, erratum E22), the row sum at the line ends; Gii from the half cells alone. solid_angle_node computes the faceted solid angle (eq. 45); on the field-aligned mesh it is 16 % of 4π away from 2π (mesh directions 14° apart, erratum E6), so it is printed by check_vac only.
  • Axisymmetric, indirect: per row, least squares for (Hii, Gii) over the identities of Rⁿ, RⁿZ (c = −4π) and the ring-source potential at the centroid (c = 0). It made the axisymmetric style converge like 1/N³ in the poloidal points instead of 1/N: exact harmonics k = 6/10/15 at 601 points 4.6e-5/2.2e-4/7.4e-4 against 2.1e-3/4.6e-3/7.7e-3 with the direct diagonals. The convergence like 1/N of style 2 in HELENA's poloidal points, found on 1 November, came from this diagonal.

How the code does it since V0-a (937d6a8, pull request #31). One routine does the fit for both styles, and one routine chooses the potentials:

  • fit_diag in vac_utilities solves, for each boundary row i and in the least-squares sense over a list of potentials k with known boundary values φ and normal data φ′, the identity \[ h\,\phi_{k,i} - g\,\phi'_{k,i} = c_k\phi_{k,i} - \sum_{j\ne i} H_{ij}\phi_{k,j} + \sum_{j\ne i} G_{ij}\phi'_{k,j} \] for h = Hii, for g = Gii, or for both. It takes the off-diagonal sums as the products with the full matrices minus their current diagonals, so the matrices are not changed. An entry that is not fitted is passed in as known, and its term moves to the right-hand side. For both entries it solves the 2 × 2 normal equations by Cramer's rule, as diag_indirect_2 did; for one entry it divides once.
  • diag_indirect in vac_ops passes each style's potentials. For the field-line style it calls fit_diag twice: first for Hii from the constant, which gives the row sum, then for Gii from x, y and z with that Hii. For the axisymmetric style it calls it once, for both entries from the three potentials of set_pot_2, each scaled to unit maximum.
  • calc_GH, after the assembly, sets the indirect diagonals with vac_diag_style 1. With vac_diag_style 2 the axisymmetric style keeps the diagonals of its assembly (corner term and analytical integrals), and the field-line style gets the direct Hii where a node has a full cell, the row sum at the ends of the lines, and keeps the half-cell Gii.
  • Both check_vac styles call diag_indirect to compare the assembled diagonals with the indirect ones (V9).

The numbers moved only at rounding level. On the Mac, with both trees built without STRUMPACK (whose solver gives eigenvalues up to 1e-7 apart from one run to the next), cbm18a free boundary with both values of vac_diag_style and the field-line style with vac_diag_style 2 are bit-identical, and the field-line style with the indirect diagonals moves the twin's eigenvalue by 1.05e-13 at 16 lines and 1.08e-13 at 64. Issue #29 (other test potentials for the axisymmetric style) would only change the list in diag_indirect.

On the torus of the full-stack tests the field-line point-source solve gives 1.0e-2 → 3.1e-3 with the indirect diagonals and 1.9e-2 → 6.4e-3 with the direct ones, from 41 × 40 to 81 × 80 (commit e027949).

Why the indirect ones won (6 November, W7-X check_vac on nine grids, Snellius, commit 43a74ed): at 128 lines × 121 points the identity residual for x is 1.2e-3 indirect against 4.1e-2 direct, and the axis-ring solve 5.9e-3 against 5.2e-2. On the circular twin the direct diagonals moved the eigenvalue from −0.43914 to −0.48650. Report: Documentation/w7x_check_vac_diag.md.

How to check it
  1. The torus toy in V0: in its figure the blue curve (row sum plus the identities of x, y, z) falls like 1/N³, the orange one (corner term −2π alone) like 1/N.
  2. Read the diagonal block of calc_GH (in its group in V4), then diag_indirect and fit_diag: the right-hand side rr, how a known entry moves into it, and the normal equations (both entries: the 2 × 2 system; one entry: one division).
  3. Tests: greens_identity_indirect, exact_exterior_2d_options, solid_angle_node, H_sing_node (1e-5 against brute force), diag_direct_3d, point_source_direct_3d.
Recorded decisions (6 November). Indirect diagonals are the default for both styles; the direct ones serve as the check_vac diagnostic. The work-bucket item on the quadrature of H_sing_node on very skewed cells is parked; after the W7-X result it would only sharpen the diagnostic. Decided on 17 November (V0): V0-a, one routine for the indirect diagonals, is done (#31); V0-b keeps vac_diag_style as an input, documented as a diagnostic, with a warning for style 2 (#31, see V1).

solve_Phi_BEM

routine solve_Phi_BEMtime 20 minread
  • Solves H Φ = G R for both styles (no shift; since f3ebf11).
  • With STRUMPACK: the compressed (HSS) solve runs on a copy of H; the residual is then checked against the uncompressed H, and if it is above 1e-6 relative the solve falls back to ScaLAPACK LU. On W7-X the HSS solve failed every time (27 October) and the fallback took over; the sampling parameters are hard-coded (unchanged from 2.47).
  • Without STRUMPACK: pdgetrf + pdgetrs on a copy of H. With check_vac the condition number in the 1-norm is estimated (pdgecon) and printed: 3.5 to 3.8 on every W7-X grid.
How to check it
  1. Read the STRUMPACK block only if you build with it (PB3D_WITH_STRUMPACK); the residual check after it and the fallback are the new parts.
  2. Read the ScaLAPACK branch: pdgetrf/pdgetrs on the copy H_ext, and pdgecon under check_vac.
  3. The two comments that said "(H + shift I)" say "solve H Phi = G R" since V0-f (ebd972c).

Test: solve_Phi_BEM_roundtrip.

3335    !> \public Calculates potential  \c Phi on boundary of BEM  in terms of some3336    !! right-hand side .3337    !!3338    !! This is done by solving the system of equations3339    !!  \f$\overline{\text{H}}\overline{\Phi} =3340    !!  \overline{\text{G}}\overline{\text{R}}\f$,3341    !! where \f$\overline{\text{R}}\f$ is the right-hand side, for example equal3342    !! to \f$\overline{\text{E}}\overline{\text{P}}\f$  to solve in  function of3343    !! the individual Fourier modes.3344    !!3345    !! Both vacuum styles assemble  \f$\overline{\text{H}}\f$ in the vacuum-side3346    !! convention: the  kernels take  the normal derivative  along the  stored3347    !! normal  \f$-\mathcal{J}\nabla\psi\f$, out  of  the vacuum,  and the  diagonal3348    !! carries  \f$-2\beta\f$ with  \f$\beta\f$ the  vacuum's internal  angle (the3349    !! row-sum identity for the field-line style). Potentials that are harmonic3350    !! in the  vacuum and  decay at infinity  then satisfy3351    !! \f$\overline{\text{H}}\overline{\phi} =3352    !! \overline{\text{G}}\overline{\text{D}\phi}\f$, and potentials that are3353    !! harmonic inside the boundary satisfy3354    !! \f$\overline{\text{H}}\overline{\phi} - \overline{\text{G}}\overline{\text{D}\phi}3355    !! = -4\pi\overline{\phi}\f$ (both verified in the full-stack tests). The3356    !! corner  term  also  makes  the  system  nonsingular  when  the  first  and3357    !! last points of a closed boundary coincide, as they do for HELENA: the two3358    !! rows differ only in the column of that term.3359    !!3360    !! calc_vac_res: data, projection, factor

routine calc_vac_res (set_up_data, solve_potential, project_response, finish_response)time 1 hstudy

The routine is split into four named internal steps that share the host's variables (225aa72). That commit says no statement changed; the tool below lists what did change besides the structure. Two things: the step sizes now come from vac_steps, which gives the same Δp and Δα as the replaced lines for every case that runs (they differ only for nα = 1, which calc_GH_1 refuses), and the CHECKVAC report of the diagonals names vac_diag_style and says "assembled" instead of "rowsum". So the split is a restructure; in appendix A it moves the nine eigenvalues by at most 1.4e-13. What changed inside the steps, against 2.47:

"""What a commit changed in the Fortran statements, ignoring comments,
blank lines, whitespace, and the lines that only restructure code.

For a refactoring commit (code moved into contained procedures, a repeated
expression replaced by a function) the full diff is long while the change of
statements is short. This prints, for the given commit and files, the code
lines that were removed and not added back, and those added and not removed
before (multisets, comments and trailing comments stripped, whitespace
normalised). What remains is what to read.

Run from the repository root:
    python3 review/tools/statement_diff.py 225aa72 Modules/vac_ops.f90
    python3 review/tools/statement_diff.py 028735c Modules/vac_ops.f90 Modules/vac_utilities.f90 Modules/vac_vars.f90
"""
import re
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from collections import Counter


os.chdir(subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], capture_output=True, text=True,
                      check=True, cwd=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))).stdout.strip())


def git(*a):
    return subprocess.run(["git", *a], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout


def code_part(line):
    """The statement part of a Fortran line: trailing comment (outside quotes) removed."""
    out, quote = [], None
    for ch in line.strip():
        if quote:
            out.append(ch)
            if ch == quote:
                quote = None
        elif ch in "'\"":
            quote = ch
            out.append(ch)
        elif ch == "!":
            break
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", "".join(out)).strip()


def statements(diff, sign):
    lines = [l[1:] for l in diff.splitlines() if l.startswith(sign) and not l.startswith(sign * 3)]
    return Counter(c for c in (code_part(l) for l in lines) if c)


def main(sha, files):
    diff = git("show", "--format=", "-U0", sha, "--", *files)
    rem, add = statements(diff, "-"), statements(diff, "+")
    subj = git("show", "-s", "--format=%h %ad %s", "--date=short", sha).strip()
    print(f"== {subj}")
    print(f"   statements removed {sum(rem.values())}, added {sum(add.values())}, "
          f"identical on both sides {sum((rem & add).values())}")
    print("   removed and not added back:")
    for k, v in (rem - add).items():
        print(f"     - {k}" + (f"   (x{v})" if v > 1 else ""))
    print("   added and not there before:")
    for k, v in (add - rem).items():
        print(f"     + {k}" + (f"   (x{v})" if v > 1 else ""))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = sys.argv[1:] or ["225aa72", "Modules/vac_ops.f90"]
    main(args[0], args[1:] or ["Modules/"])
  • set_up_data: EP = −(nq − m) times cos and sin of the phase, the normal data along −J∇ψ (2.47: +). The phase is nα + (nq − m)p on the field lines and −mθ for the axisymmetric style.
  • project_response: for the field-line style the weight is Δp / nα (halved at the line ends): the projection averages over the lines, which matches the per-toroidal-mode normalisation of the axisymmetric style. 2.47 used Δp Δα.
  • finish_response: res = (2π/μ₀) times the complex combination of the four real blocks, then its Hermitian part. The 2π: A holds 2δW with the toroidal integral included, and res up to there is per unit toroidal angle. The Hermitian part: the discretisation leaves an asymmetry of about 1e-5, which made SLEPc reject converged eigenvalues as complex.

How the factor was found. Commit 212e3ec (27 October) measured it before writing it: on the circular ε = 0.05 external kink a factor of magnitude 2π reproduced MISHKA-1 without a wall to 0.3 to 0.8 % at n = 10, 15 and 20, while 1 and 4π were 60 to 80 % off; then it was derived (the comment in finish_response). The sign was −2π then, with the data sign of that time; since f3ebf11 the data are −(nq − m) and the factor is +2π, with the same response.

Check of the factor: in the large-aspect-ratio cylinder the vacuum energy of an edge displacement equals the field-line bending energy of a plasma layer of thickness a/|m| at the edge, 4π²(nq − m)²|Xe|²/(μ₀R₀|m|) in A. The full-stack test vac_response_cylinder checks res(m, m) against it (1 to 2 % for m = 1 … 5). The external kink against MISHKA-1 and TERPSICHORE is the end-to-end check of the sign and the factor: circular ε = 0.33, n = 10, free boundary: PB3D's field-line style at 128 lines × 400 points −0.438488, TERPSICHORE −0.438480 (with its kinetic-energy parity error corrected), MISHKA-1 −0.43377 (1.1 % less unstable, probably its parallel inertia; not verified).

How to check it
  1. In set_up_data: the sign of EP, and the phase for each style.
  2. In project_response: the weight Δp/nα with the halved line ends, and the axisymmetric weight (θi+1 − θi−1)/2.
  3. In finish_response: the combination of the four real blocks into the complex res (the sign comment for the lower rows is from 2.47), then /μ₀, ×2π, Hermitian part.

1444    !> Calculates the vacuum response.1445    !!1446    !! First  \c G and \c  H are completed if  this is not the  first Richardson1447    !! level.1448    !! 1449    !! Then the vacuum contribution is calculated using the two-fold strategy of1450    !! first solving 1451    !!  \f$\overline{\text{H}}\overline{\Phi} =1452    !!  \overline{\text{G}}\overline{\text{E}} \overline{\text{P}}\f$,1453    !! followed by left-multiplication of \f$\overline{\Phi}\f$ by1454    !!  \f$\overline{\text{P}}\overline{\text{E}}^\dagger\f$.1455    !!1456    !! The  non-square matrix  \f$\overline{\text{E}}\f$ contains  the exponents1457    !! for different  mode numbers and  different poloidal grid  points, whereas1458    !! \f$\overline{\text{P}}\f$ are diagonal matrices  that contain the factors1459    !! \f$(nq-m)\f$.1460    !!1461    !! In practice, the complex matrix \f$\overline{\text{E}}\f$ is split in the1462    !! two components of a real matrix twice the width.1463    !!1464    !! For vacuum style  1, the poloidal grid points correspond  to the paralell1465    !! grid points and have to be provied by a \c grid variable.1466    !!1467    !! If \c  jump_to_sol is used for  the current Richardson level,  the vacuum1468    !! quantities are not calculated, but just restored.1469    !!1470    !! V9

check_vac diagnostics

routines check_vac_exact, check_vac_exact_1, check_vac_exact_2, write_points_vactime 30 minskim

Off by default (check_vac = .false.). With it, PB3D tests its own operators on the real equilibrium surface with potentials whose boundary data are exact, and prints lines that start with CHECKVAC. Field-line style: identity residuals for 1, x, y, z and x² − y² (interior) and for a point source on the axis and two rings of sources along the axis, with unit weights and with weights cos(nζ) (exterior), each for c = −4π, −2π, 0, 2π, 4π; exterior solves for the point source and the rings; per-point files of residuals and errors. Axisymmetric style: the potentials of set_pot_2, the ring solve, and the assembled diagonals against the alternative ones. Since V0-a the field-line style also compares the assembled diagonal of G with the indirect one (the line CHECKVAC diagonal max|G_assembled-G_indirect|/max|G| and the file check_vac_diag_diff_G.dat): on the twin at 16 lines × 100 points it reads 2.2e-13 with vac_diag_style 1, as it must, and 0.59 with vac_diag_style 2, where the half-cell Gii differs from the indirect one by up to 0.59 of the largest |Gii|. The CHECKVAC lines are split so that writo, which cuts lines at about 100 characters, prints them whole. scripts/snellius/checkvac_table.py and diag_table.py collect them.

Reviewing these matters less than the core: they do not change the response. They do matter as evidence, since the W7-X conclusions rest on them.

How to check it: check that every call in check_vac is read-only for vac (it builds its own right-hand sides and solves into its own arrays), then read the free terms c of the identities (−4π for interior, 0 for exterior potentials) and how the exact normal data are formed.

V10

POST vacuum potential plot

routines vac_pot_plot, eval_pot_ext, glob2dis_cols, sub_nearest, grad_bnd_1, check_vac_extcommit a8804ac (Opus side session, 6 November)time 30 minskim

At 2.47 the plot existed for the axisymmetric style only and was switched off. Now it works for both: the potential off the boundary from the Green representation (eval_pot_ext, which calls calc_GH with external points), with a correction for points close to the boundary (sub_nearest, grad_bnd_1), all plotted modes in one pass. check_vac_ext compares with exact exterior potentials: axisymmetric at the 1e-7 level from 4 spacings out; field lines on the twin at 64 × 100: 2e-8 to 2e-6 at 0.5a to 1a from the boundary, 1e-4 to 7e-4 within 0.2a, except the cos 10ζ ring (1e-2). Figure: Documentation/figures/vacuum_plot/vac_pot_circular.png.

The same commit fixed three things in the core routines: out-of-bounds reads of external points in calc_GH_1 and calc_GH_2, interlaced_vac_copy writing past vac%ang, and an unneeded gather of the tolerance in calc_GH_2. The stub that had switched the plot off dated from April 2018.

For the field-line style the plot takes the grid of the parallel angle (min_par_X, max_par_X, n_par_X) from vac%ang. Since 59c6e90 that angle comes from the output as PB3D stored it, and the stop "No parallel angle in the vacuum output" is gone: POST refuses every output below version 2.49, and every 2.49 output holds the angle.

A finding of that work, recorded in calc_GH_int_1: for points off the boundary the near-field rule only helps within one interval length, because the edge of its zone leaves an error that falls like Δp², while the plain trapezoidal errors at the line ends cancel between interleaved lines. The on-boundary rows have the same zone edge; whether that limits the 3-D operators is not tested.

How to check it: skim vac_pot_plot for its flow (normal data as in calc_vac_res, one solve, external rows from eval_pot_ext), then read eval_pot_ext and sub_nearest, the two places with numerics of their own.

vac_ops.f90 lines now: 2516–2635 (eval_pot_ext), 2637–2663 (glob2dis_cols), 2665–2718 (sub_nearest), 2720–2777 (grad_bnd_1), 2779–2913 (check_vac_ext), 2915–3333 (vac_pot_plot); at 2.47: 1829–2150 (vac_pot_plot). Line numbers in the diff are file line numbers (left: 2.47, right: now).

The matrices \f$\overline{\text{H}}\f$1837-    !! and \f$\overline{\text{G}}\f$ have to be calculated in advance.2519+    !! The kernels are taken along  the stored normal \f$-\mathcal{J}\nabla\psi\f$,2520+    !! which points out  of the vacuum. Green's second identity  then gives, at a2521+    !! point \f$\vec{x}\f$ off the boundary,2522+    !!  \f[ \sum_j \left( H(\vec{x},\vec{x}_j)\phi_j -2523+    !!  G(\vec{x},\vec{x}_j)\,\text{d}\phi_j \right) = \left\{2524+    !!  \begin{array}{ll}2525+    !!  4\pi\phi(\vec{x}) & \text{in the vacuum,} \\2526+    !!  0 & \text{in the plasma}2527+    !!  \end{array} \right. \f]2528+    !! for a potential \f$\phi\f$ that is  harmonic in the vacuum and decays at2529+    !! infinity, and \f$0\f$ in the  vacuum and \f$-4\pi\phi(\vec{x})\f$ in the2530+    !! plasma for a potential  harmonic inside the boundary (the constant for the2531+    !! field-line style, \f$R^{|n|}\f$ for the axisymmetric one). 2516    !> \public Potential at points off the boundary, from its values and its2517    !! normal data on the boundary.2518    !!2519    !! The kernels are taken along  the stored normal \f$-\mathcal{J}\nabla\psi\f$,2520    !! which points out  of the vacuum. Green's second identity  then gives, at a2521    !! point \f$\vec{x}\f$ off the boundary,2522    !!  \f[ \sum_j \left( H(\vec{x},\vec{x}_j)\phi_j -2523    !!  G(\vec{x},\vec{x}_j)\,\text{d}\phi_j \right) = \left\{2524    !!  \begin{array}{ll}2525    !!  4\pi\phi(\vec{x}) & \text{in the vacuum,} \\2526    !!  0 & \text{in the plasma}2527    !!  \end{array} \right. \f]2528    !! for a potential \f$\phi\f$ that is  harmonic in the vacuum and decays at2529    !! infinity, and \f$0\f$ in the  vacuum and \f$-4\pi\phi(\vec{x})\f$ in the2530    !! plasma for a potential  harmonic inside the boundary (the constant for the2531    !! field-line style, \f$R^{|n|}\f$ for the axisymmetric one).  On the boundary2532    !! the same sum, with the diagonal  that calc_GH() adds there, is the identity2533    !! \f$\overline{\text{H}}\phi - \overline{\text{G}}\,\text{d}\phi = c\phi\f$2534    !! of solve_Phi_BEM(), \f$c = 0\f$ and \f$-4\pi\f$ for the two kinds.2535    !!2536    !! This routine returns the sum divided by \f$4\pi\f$ for every column of2537    !! \c Phi_s and \c D_s. The rows  of G and H are assembled by calc_GH() for2538    !! the external points  (no diagonal; the trapezoidal rule with the near-field2539    !! rule along the field lines for the field-line style, the toroidal-function2540    !! kernels for the axisymmetric style), in chunks that bound the memory.2541    !! Within a few grid spacings of the boundary the quadrature does not2542    !! resolve the kernels.2543    !!2544    !! Every process of the BLACS grid of the vacuum has to call it.2545    !!2546    !! \return ierr2547    integer function eval_pot_ext(vac,x_ext,Phi_s,D_s,desc_s,pot) result(ierr)2548        use vac_vars, only: in_context, set_loc_lims2549        use vac_utilities, only: mat_dis2loc2550 2551        character(*), parameter :: rout_name = 'eval_pot_ext'2552 2553        !
