local columns of the result2585        n_col_loc = 02586        if (in_context(vac%ctxt_HG)) n_col_loc = &2587            &numroc(n_col,vac%bs,vac%ind_p(2),0,vac%n_p(2))2588        call set_loc_lims(n_col_loc,vac%bs,vac%ind_p(2),vac%n_p(2),lims_c_loc)2589 2590        ! chunks of points2591        i_1 = 12592        do while (i_1.le.n_ext)2593            i_2 = min(n_ext,i_1+n_ch-1)2594            n_r = i_2-i_1+12595            n_row_loc = 02596            if (in_context(vac%ctxt_HG)) n_row_loc = &2597                &numroc(n_r,vac%bs,vac%ind_p(1),0,vac%n_p(1))2598            call set_loc_lims(n_row_loc,vac%bs,vac%ind_p(1),vac%n_p(1),&2599                &lims_r_loc)2600 2601            ! external rows of G and H2602            allocate(G_loc(max(1,n_row_loc),max(1,vac%n_loc(2))))2603            allocate(H_loc(max(1,n_row_loc),max(1,vac%n_loc(2))))2604            G_loc = 0._dp2605            H_loc = 0._dp2606            ierr = calc_GH(vac,n_r_in=n_r,lims_r_in=lims_r_loc,&2607                &x_vec_in=x_ext(i_1:i_2,:),G_in=G_loc,H_in=H_loc)2608            CHCKERR('')2609 2610            ! (H Phi - G D) / 4 pi, gathered2611            if (in_context(vac%ctxt_HG)) then2612                call descinit(desc_GH,n_r,vac%n_bnd,vac%bs,vac%bs,0,0,&2613                    &vac%ctxt_HG,max(1,n_row_loc),ierr)2614                CHCKERR('descinit failed for GH')2615                call descinit(desc_P,n_r,n_col,vac%bs,vac%bs,0,0,&2616                    &vac%ctxt_HG,max(1,n_row_loc),ierr)2617                CHCKERR('descinit failed for P')2618                allocate(P_loc(max(1,n_row_loc),max(1,n_col_loc)))2619                P_loc = 0._dp2620                call pdgemm('N','N',n_r,n_col,vac%n_bnd,1._dp/(4*pi),H_loc,&2621                    &1,1,desc_GH,Phi_s,1,1,desc_s,0._dp,P_loc,1,1,desc_P)2622                call pdgemm('N','N',n_r,n_col,vac%n_bnd,-1._dp/(4*pi),G_loc,&2623                    &1,1,desc_GH,D_s,1,1,desc_s,1._dp,P_loc,1,1,desc_P)2624                allocate(P_ser(n_r,n_col))2625                ierr = mat_dis2loc(vac%ctxt_HG,P_loc(1:n_row_loc,1:n_col_loc),&2626                    &lims_r_loc,lims_c_loc,P_ser)2627                CHCKERR('')2628                pot(i_1:i_2,:) = P_ser2629                deallocate(P_loc,P_ser)2630            end if2631 2632            deallocate(G_loc,H_loc,lims_r_loc)2633            i_1 = i_2+12634        end do2635    end function eval_pot_ext 2637    !> Copies columns  with the boundary points  as rows, the same  on every2638    !! process, into their local block-cyclic part.2639    subroutine glob2dis_cols(vac,A_glob,lims_c_loc,A_dis)2640        use vac_vars, only: in_context, loc_idx2641 2642        ! input / output2643        type(vac_type), intent(in) :: vac                                       !< vacuum variables2644        real(dp), intent(in) :: A_glob(:,:)                                     !< global columns, n_bnd by n_col2645        integer, intent(in) :: lims_c_loc(:,:)                                  !< local column limits2646        real(dp), intent(inout) :: A_dis(:,:)                                   !< local part2647 2648        ! local variables2649        integer :: i_rd, i_cd                                                   ! index of subrow and subcolumn2650        integer :: rd, cd                                                       ! global row and column2651 2652        if (.not.in_context(vac%ctxt_HG)) return2653        do i_cd = 1,size(lims_c_loc,2)2654            do cd = lims_c_loc(1,i_cd),lims_c_loc(2,i_cd)2655                do i_rd = 1,size(vac%lims_r,2)2656                    do rd = vac%lims_r(1,i_rd),vac%lims_r(2,i_rd)2657                        A_dis(loc_idx(vac%lims_r,i_rd,rd),&2658                            &loc_idx(lims_c_loc,i_cd,cd)) = A_glob(rd,cd)2659                    end do2660                end do2661            end do2662        end do2663    end subroutine glob2dis_cols 2665    !> Subtracts from the potential off the boundary the representation of2666    !! the interior harmonic that equals it at the nearest boundary point.2667    !!2668    !! In the vacuum the representation of a potential that is harmonic inside2669    !! the boundary is zero (eval_pot_ext()), so the subtraction changes2670    !! nothing exactly. In the quadrature it removes the error that the double2671    !! layer makes with the potential at the nearest boundary point, the part2672    !! that grows without bound as the point approaches the boundary; what2673    !! remains comes from the variation of the potential along the boundary and2674    !! from the single layer. With \c psi_bnd the boundary values of the2675    !! interior harmonic (the constant for the field-line style, \f$R^{|n|}\f$2676    !! for the axisymmetric one) and \c pot_psi its representation, every2677    !! column \f$c\f$ becomes \f$\phi(\vec{x},c) -2678    !! \Phi_j^c/\psi_j\,\phi_\psi(\vec{x})\f$, \f$j\f$ the boundary point2679    !! nearest to \f$\vec{x}\f$. For points in the vacuum only: inside the2680    !! plasma the result is the potential of the nearest boundary point2681    !! instead of zero.2682    !!2683    !! For the field-line style, with the gradient \c grad of the columns at2684    !! the boundary points (grad_bnd_1()) and the representations \c pot_x of2685    !! the coordinates x, y and z, the subtracted harmonic is the linear2686    !! function \f$\Phi_j + \vec{g}_j\cdot(\vec{x}-\vec{x}_j)\f$, which2687    !! matches the potential to first order at the nearest boundary point and2688    !! removes the error of the potential's variation along the boundary as2689    !! well. The constant alone leaves that error where the nearest boundary2690    !! point lies on a neighbouring field line, a large part of a wavelength2691    !! away in a mode of high toroidal mode number.2692    subroutine sub_nearest(vac,x_ext,Phi_glob,psi_bnd,pot_psi,pot,grad,pot_x)2693        ! input / output2694        type(vac_type), intent(in) :: vac                                       !< vacuum variables2695        real(dp), intent(in) :: x_ext(:,:)                                      !< points2696        real(dp), intent(in) :: Phi_glob(:,:)                                   !< boundary values of the columns, n_bnd by n_c2697        real(dp), intent(in) :: psi_bnd(:)                                      !< boundary values of the interior harmonic2698        real(dp), intent(in) :: pot_psi(:)                                      !< its representation at the points2699        real(dp), intent(inout) :: pot(:,:)                                     !< representation of the columns at the points, n_ext by n_c2700        real(dp), intent(in), optional :: grad(:,:,:)                           !< gradient of the columns at the boundary points, n_bnd by 3 by n_c (field-line style)2701        real(dp), intent(in), optional :: pot_x(:,:)                            !< representation of x, y and z at the points, n_ext by 32702        2703        ! local variables2704        integer :: id, kd                                                       ! counters2705        integer :: j_min                                                        ! nearest boundary point2706        2707        do id = 1,size(x_ext,1)2708            j_min = minloc(sum((vac%x_vec-spread(x_ext(id,:),1,vac%n_bnd))**2,&2709                &2),1)2710            pot(id,:) = pot(id,:) - Phi_glob(j_min,:)/psi_bnd(j_min)*pot_psi(id)2711            if (present(grad) .and. present(pot_x)) then2712                do kd = 1,32713                    pot(id,:) = pot(id,:) - grad(j_min,kd,:)*&2714                        &(pot_x(id,kd)-vac%x_vec(j_min,kd)*pot_psi(id))2715                end do2716            end if2717        end do2718    end subroutine sub_nearest 2720    !> Gradient of columns of boundary values at the boundary points of the2721    !! field-line style.2722    !!2723    !! At every point the gradient \f$\vec{g}\f$ of a potential follows from2724    !! \f$\vec{g}\cdot\Delta\vec{x}_p = \Delta\Phi_p\f$, \f$\vec{g}\cdot2725    !! \Delta\vec{x}_\alpha = \Delta\Phi_\alpha\f$ and \f$\vec{g}\cdot2726    !! \vec{n} = \text{d}\phi\f$: central differences of the position and of2727    !! the boundary values along the field line (one-sided at its ends) and2728    !! across the field lines at the same parallel point (periodic in the2729    !! field-line label when the lines cover a full turn, \c alpha_periodic,2730    !! one-sided otherwise), and the normal data along the stored normal.2731    subroutine grad_bnd_1(vac,Phi_glob,D_glob,alpha_periodic,grad)2732        ! input / output2733        type(vac_type), intent(in) :: vac                                       !< vacuum variables2734        real(dp), intent(in) :: Phi_glob(:,:)                                   !< boundary values, n_bnd by n_c2735        real(dp), intent(in) :: D_glob(:,:)                                     !< normal data, n_bnd by n_c2736        logical, intent(in) :: alpha_periodic                                   !< the field lines cover a full turn in alpha2737        real(dp), intent(out) :: grad(:,:,:)                                    !< gradient, n_bnd by 3 by n_c2738        2739        ! local variables2740        integer :: rd                                                           ! boundary point2741        integer :: par_id, alpha_id                                             ! its parallel index and field line2742        integer :: n_par, n_al                                                  ! points per line and lines2743        integer :: jp(2), ja(2)                                                 ! neighbours along and across the lines2744        integer :: ipiv(3), info                                                ! pivots and status of the solve2745        real(dp) :: A(3,3)                                                      ! system2746        real(dp), allocatable :: b(:,:)                                         ! right-hand sides and solution2747        2748        n_par = vac%n_ang(1)2749        n_al = vac%n_ang(2)2750        allocate(b(3,size(Phi_glob,2)))2751        do rd = 1,vac%n_bnd2752            par_id = mod(rd-1,n_par)+12753            alpha_id = (rd-1)/n_par+12754            jp = [rd-1,rd+1]2755            if (par_id.eq.1) jp(1) = rd2756            if (par_id.eq.n_par) jp(2) = rd2757            ja = [rd-n_par,rd+n_par]2758            if (alpha_id.eq.1) then2759                ja(1) = rd2760                if (alpha_periodic) ja(1) = rd+(n_al-1)*n_par2761            end if2762            if (alpha_id.eq.n_al) then2763                ja(2) = rd2764                if (alpha_periodic) ja(2) = rd-(n_al-1)*n_par2765            end if2766            if (ja(1).eq.ja(2)) ja(1) = rd                                      ! two lines2767            A(1,:) = vac%x_vec(jp(2),:)-vac%x_vec(jp(1),:)2768            A(2,:) = vac%x_vec(ja(2),:)-vac%x_vec(ja(1),:)2769            A(3,:) = vac%norm(rd,:)2770            b(1,:) = Phi_glob(jp(2),:)-Phi_glob(jp(1),:)2771            b(2,:) = Phi_glob(ja(2),:)-Phi_glob(ja(1),:)2772            b(3,:) = D_glob(rd,:)2773            call dgesv(3,size(b,2),A,3,ipiv,b,3,info)2774            if (info.ne.0) b = 0._dp                                            ! degenerate: no first-order term2775            grad(rd,:,:) = b2776        end do2777    end subroutine grad_bnd_1 2779    !> Checks the potential that eval_pot_ext() gives off the boundary against2780    !! exact values, for check_vac_exact().2781    !!2782    !! Every column holds a potential's values \c Phi_glob and normal data \c2783    !! D_glob on the boundary and its exact values \c val_ex at the points \c2784    !! x_ext. The points lie on the normals of some boundary points, at the2785    !! distance \c f_d times half the larger width of the boundary in R and Z,2786    !! outward for positive \c f_d and inward for negative. For each column and2787    !! distance the largest error over the points, divided by \c scale, is2788    !! printed on a line starting with CHECKVAC exterior; for the points in the2789    !! vacuum also the error after sub_nearest() with the interior harmonic2790    !! of column \c col_psi (sub=). input / output2802        type(vac_type), intent(inout) :: vac                                    !< vacuum variables2803        real(dp), intent(in) :: f_d(:)                                          !< distance of each point from the boundary, in units of half the larger width2804        real(dp), intent(in) :: x_ext(:,:)                                      !< points2805        real(dp), intent(in) :: Phi_glob(:,:)                                   !< boundary values, n_bnd by n_col2806        real(dp), intent(in) :: D_glob(:,:)                                     !< normal data, n_bnd by n_col2807        real(dp), intent(in) :: val_ex(:,:)                                     !< exact values at the points, n_ext by n_col2808        character(len=*), intent(in) :: col_names(:)                            !< names of the columns2809        real(dp), intent(in) :: scale(:)                                        !< scale of the errors, per column2810        integer, intent(in) :: col_psi                                          !< column of the interior harmonic2811        integer, intent(in), optional :: cols_x(3)                              !< columns of x, y and z (field-line style): first-order subtraction as well2812 2813        ! local variables2814        integer :: id, jd                                                       ! counters2815        integer :: n_col, n_col_loc                                             ! number of columns and local number2816        integer :: file_i                                                       ! file unit2817        integer :: desc_s(BLACSCTXTSIZE)                                        ! descriptor of the boundary columns2818        integer, allocatable :: lims_c_loc(:,:)                                 ! local column limits2819        real(dp), allocatable :: Phi_s(:,:), D_s(:,:)                           ! local boundary columns2820        real(dp), allocatable :: pot(:,:)                                       ! potential at the points2821        real(dp), allocatable :: pot_sub(:,:)                                   ! the same after sub_nearest2822        real(dp), allocatable :: pot_sub1(:,:)                                  ! the same after the first-order sub_nearest2823        real(dp), allocatable :: grad(:,:,:)                                    ! gradient of the columns on the boundary2824character(len=max_str_ln) :: sub_str                                    ! error after sub_nearest as string2825        logical, allocatable :: done(:)                                         ! distance already printed2826        logical, allocatable :: same_d(:)                                       ! points at the distance being printed2827        logical :: rank_o                                                       ! output rank2828 2829        ! initialize ierr2830        ierr = 02831 2832        rank_o = rank.eq.n_procs-12833        n_col = size(Phi_glob,2)2834 2835        ! boundary columns2836        n_col_loc = 02837        if (in_context(vac%ctxt_HG)) n_col_loc = &2838            &numroc(n_col,vac%bs,vac%ind_p(2),0,vac%n_p(2))2839        call set_loc_lims(n_col_loc,vac%bs,vac%ind_p(2),vac%n_p(2),lims_c_loc)2840        allocate(Phi_s(max(1,vac%n_loc(1)),max(1,n_col_loc)))2841        allocate(D_s(max(1,vac%n_loc(1)),max(1,n_col_loc)))2842        Phi_s = 0._dp2843        D_s = 0._dp2844        desc_s = 02845        call glob2dis_cols(vac,Phi_glob,lims_c_loc,Phi_s)2846        call glob2dis_cols(vac,D_glob,lims_c_loc,D_s)2847        if (in_context(vac%ctxt_HG)) then2848            call descinit(desc_s,vac%n_bnd,n_col,vac%bs,vac%bs,0,0,&2849                &vac%ctxt_HG,max(1,vac%n_loc(1)),ierr)2850            CHCKERR('descinit failed')2851        end if2852 2853        ! potential at the points, and after subtraction of the interior2854        ! harmonic matching the nearest boundary value2855        allocate(pot(size(x_ext,1),n_col))2856        ierr = eval_pot_ext(vac,x_ext,Phi_s,D_s,desc_s,pot)2857        CHCKERR('')2858        pot_sub = pot2859        call sub_nearest(vac,x_ext,Phi_glob,Phi_glob(:,col_psi),&2860            &pot(:,col_psi),pot_sub)2861        if (present(cols_x)) then2862            allocate(grad(vac%n_bnd,3,n_col))2863            call grad_bnd_1(vac,Phi_glob,D_glob,&2864                &abs(max_alpha-min_alpha-2._dp).lt.1.E-8_dp,grad)2865            pot_sub1 = pot2866            call sub_nearest(vac,x_ext,Phi_glob,Phi_glob(:,col_psi),&2867                &pot(:,col_psi),pot_sub1,grad=grad,pot_x=pot(:,cols_x))2868        end if2869 2870        ! largest error per column and distance (one line each: writo cuts2871        ! long lines)2872        allocate(done(size(f_d)),same_d(size(f_d)))2873        done = .false.2874        do id = 1,size(f_d)2875            if (done(id)) cycle2876            same_d = abs(f_d-f_d(id)).lt.1.E-12_dp2877            done = done .or. same_d2878            do jd = 1,n_col2879                sub_str = ''2880                if (f_d(id).gt.0._dp .and. jd.ne.col_psi) sub_str = ' sub='//&2881                    &trim(r2strt(maxval(abs(pot_sub(:,jd)-val_ex(:,jd)),&2882                    &mask=same_d)/scale(jd)))2883                call writo('CHECKVAC exterior '//trim(col_names(jd))//&2884                    &' n_bnd='//trim(i2str(vac%n_bnd))//' d/a='//&2885                    &trim(r2strt(f_d(id)))//' err='//trim(r2strt(&2886                    &maxval(abs(pot(:,jd)-val_ex(:,jd)),mask=same_d)/&2887                    &scale(jd)))//trim(sub_str),persistent=rank_o)2888                if (present(cols_x)) then                                       ! For every  eigenmode of \c X_ids  the normal data of  the vacuum2919    !! potential on the boundary are those of calc_vac_res(): along the stored2920    !! normal \f$-\mathcal{J}\nabla\psi\f$, out of the vacuum, \f$\text{d}\phi =2921    !! -\mathcal{J}\vec{B}\cdot\nabla X = -i(nq-m)X\f$, summed over the modes of2922    !! the solution at the plasma edge with the basis \f$e^{i(n\alpha +2923    !! (nq-m)\theta)} = e^{i(n\zeta_\text{F} - m\theta)}\f$ of the field-line2924    !! style, or \f$e^{-im\theta}\f$ for the axisymmetric style, which splits2925    !! off \f$e^{in\zeta_\text{F}}\f$. These data are \f$-\mathcal{J}Q_n\f$, with2926    !! \f$Q_n\f$ the normal component of the magnetic perturbation that POST2927    !! plots: the normal component of the perturbed field is continuous across2928    !! the boundary. The boundary potential follows from the exterior system of2929    !! solve_Phi_BEM(), the potential in the vacuum from Green's representation2930    !! (eval_pot_ext()): for the field-line style the complex potential at the2931    !! 3-D points, for the axisymmetric style \f$\hat{\phi}(R,Z)\f$ times2932    !! \f$e^{in\zeta_\text{F}}\f$.2933    !!2934    !! The points lie in the planes of constant \f$\zeta_\text{F}\f$ of the2935    !! plasma plots, \c n_zeta_plot values from \c min_zeta_plot to \c2936    !! max_zeta_plot in units of \f$\pi\f$ (the geometrical angle is2937    !! \f$-\zeta_\text{F}\f$ for VMEC and HELENA), on a grid of \c n_vac_plot2938    !! points in \f$R\f$ and \f$Z\f$ from \c min_Rvac_plot to \c max_Rvac_plot2939    !! and from \c min_Zvac_plot to \c max_Zvac_plot, in metres. Where a maximum2940    !! does not exceed its minimum (the default), the range is that of the2941    !! boundary points widened on both sides by half the larger of their widths2942    !! in \f$R\f$ and \f$Z\f$.2943    !!2944    !! boundary columns: real and imaginary part per eigenmode (and the constant)2984        integer :: n_col_loc                                                    ! local number of columns2985        integer :: n_RZ                                                         ! boundary point2988        integer :: par_id, alpha_id                                             ! parallel index and field line of a boundary point2989        integer :: file_i                                                       ! file unit2990        integer :: desc_s(BLACSCTXTSIZE)                                        ! descriptor of the boundary columns2991        integer, allocatable :: lims_c_loc(:,:)                                 ! V11

print_output_vac

routine print_output_vactime 10 minskim

Two changes against 2.47. The parallel angle ang is written for both styles, after x_vec and before the style branch; at 2.47 only the axisymmetric style wrote it (your commit 59c6e90; before it, a8804ac had written the two limits of the angle as entries 7 and 8 of misc_vac, and POST rebuilt the angle from them). h_fac is written with 3 columns. misc_vac has its six entries of 2.47.

How to check it: compare the names written here with the names reconstruct_PB3D_vac in PB3D_ops reads (V1, commit 59c6e90): misc_vac with six entries; sec_X, norm, x_vec and ang for both styles; h_fac or dnorm by style; RE_res and IM_res. The HDF5 reads go by name, so the order does not matter. The list of written variables in the doc comment above the routine names ang as well.

vac_ops.f90 lines now: 3610–3793 (print_output_vac); at 2.47: 2320–2502 (print_output_vac). Line numbers in the diff are file line numbers (left: 2.47, right: now).

Stage 6

The free edge again; inputs, defaults and output format

D

The free edge again: end weights, no central differences, no style 4

files SLEPC_ops, num_utilities, input_ops, PB3D_ops, num_vars, SLEPC_utilitiestime 45 minstudy

Three commits of 17 and 18 November, merged on 18 November through the pull requests #37 and #38, change the code of F5 and F6. Those two sections stay as you reviewed them, at 9e9aba5; this one shows the result, 2.47 against b41fd8a. With the default input (left differences of order p = 3, BC_style 1 2) only the first commit moves eigenvalues, and only those of a free boundary.

The weights of the last points (cba0762, #37)

F5 gave the edge point half a weight, as the trapezoidal rule does. With left differences that left a part of the error proportional to 1/N, where N is n_r_sol. The difference at point i uses the points i − p to i. The points beyond the edge do not exist, so XN enters one difference, XN−1 two, and only XN−p and the points before it enter all p + 1. The rows of the last points are then not consistent equations. On the circular ε = 0.33 kink the steps between 200, 400, 800, 1600 and 3200 points shrank by 2.7, 2.5 and 2.3 per doubling, where a second-order method gives 4.

The new function calc_end_weights in num_utilities gives the last points the weights wi, in units of the step h, for which the weighted sum of the left differences of any X that is zero at the first p points equals X at the edge:

h Σi wi (DX)i = XN,    with    (DX)i = (1/h) Σm = 0 … p cm Xi−m.

This is the discrete form of ∫ X′ dψ = X(edge), which the integration by parts of the energy uses. Collecting the terms in XN−k gives the weights from the edge inwards:

c0 wN = 1,    Σm = 0 … min(p, k) cm wN−k+m = 0   for k ≥ 1.

For p = 3 they are 6/11, 108/121, 1.0143, 1.0286, 1.0156 and so on, tending to 1. Their sum is half a step less than that of unit weights, as for the trapezoidal rule. fill_mat uses them for a free edge with p = 2 or 3. For p = 1 the weights that satisfy the equation are all 1, which would not take the half step off, so the edge point keeps half a weight. A fixed edge keeps weight 1 at every point: with the end weights the circular fixed-boundary eigenvalue converged more slowly, and cbm18a fixed barely moved.

PB3D, n = 10, free edge, BC_style 1 2, p = 3, from the commit message:

case, weights of the last points20040080016003200 points
circular ε = 0.33, wN = 1/2 (F5)−0.438020−0.437937−0.437906−0.437893−0.437888
circular ε = 0.33, end weights−0.437887−0.437883−0.437883−0.437883−0.437883
circular ε = 0.05, wN = 1/2 (F5)−0.425616−0.425556−0.425526−0.425514−0.425509
circular ε = 0.05, end weights−0.425513−0.425519−0.425508−0.425505−0.425505

At 200 points the ε = 0.33 value is now 9e-6 from the limit (relative), against 3e-4 before. With p = 2 the steps fall by 4 per doubling instead of 2. cbm18a moves by 3e-6; according to the commit message its first-order convergence does not come from the edge (see "What nobody has checked yet" in Q). Two anchors moved, ε = 0.05 free to −4.2551e-1 and the twin's free run to −4.3901e-1 (T), and circ_eps005_free_bnd.sh now requires its 200- and 400-point values to agree to 5e-5: they agree to 1.3e-5, against 1.4e-4 with wN = 1/2. The new unit test end_weights is in test_num_utilities.

The demo below copies the assembly of fill_mat, set_BC_1 and set_BC_2 for one mode of a model problem whose mode lies against the edge. It computes the weights with the same recurrence and checks the first equation above to 1e-12. The error of its lowest eigenvalue is proportional to 1/N with wN = 1 (2.47) and with wN = 1/2 (F5, 370 times smaller), and to 1/N3 with the end weights for p = 3. Its part 3 belongs to the list "What nobody has checked yet" in Q.

figure: review/figures/end_weights_1d.png
script
"""Area D: the weights of the last points of a free edge (num_utilities.calc_end_weights,
used by SLEPC_ops.fill_mat since cba0762).

PB3D sums the energy over the radial points i = 0 ... N with weights h w_i, and
takes the radial derivative at point i as a left finite difference over p + 1
points (p = norm_disc_prec_sol):

    (D X)_i = (1/h) sum_{m=0}^{p} c_m X_{i-m}.

Part 1 computes the end weights with the recurrence of calc_end_weights,

    c_0 w_N = 1,   sum_{m=0}^{min(p,k)} c_m w_{N-k+m} = 0  for k >= 1,

and checks the property they are made for: h sum_i w_i (D X)_i = X_N for any
grid function X that vanishes at the first p points (the discrete form of the
integral of X' over the plasma).

Part 2 is a one-mode copy of the assembly of fill_mat, set_BC_1 and set_BC_2
for the model problem

    -X'' + V X = lambda X  on 0 < r < 1,   X(0) = 0,   X'(1) + kappa X(1) = 0,

which is PB3D's Euler equation and natural boundary condition with P2 = 1,
P0 = V, K0 = 1, P1 = K1 = K2 = 0 and vac%res = kappa. V = 4000 (1 - r)^6 puts
the mode against the edge, so that the edge alone sets the error. It compares
three choices for the weights of the last points, all others being 1:

    'h'    w_N = 1                       (2.47)
    'h/2'  w_N = 1/2                     (4915d4b, F5)
    'end'  the weights of part 1         (cba0762, for p = 2 and 3)

The reference eigenvalue comes from Chebyshev collocation on 200 points.

Part 3 repeats the end weights with V = 0, so that the mode also reaches the
inner end, where set_BC_1 sets the first p points to zero.
"""
import numpy as np
import scipy.sparse as sp
from scipy.linalg import eig
from scipy.sparse.linalg import eigsh

from _common import BLUE, GREEN, ORANGE, plt, save

KAPPA = 1.0
EV_BC = 1.0e6                                  # artificial eigenvalue of the inner boundary rows


def V(r):
    return 4000 * (1 - r) ** 6


def fd(offsets):
    """Coefficients of the first derivative at offset 0 from the given offsets (step 1)."""
    o = np.asarray(offsets, float)
    rhs = np.zeros(len(o))
    rhs[1] = 1.0
    return np.linalg.solve(np.vander(o, len(o), increasing=True).T, rhs)


def end_weights(p, tol=1e-12):
    """The recurrence of calc_end_weights: w[0] is the last point, w[1] the one before it, ..."""
    c = fd(np.arange(0, -p - 1, -1))           # c[m] multiplies X_{i-m}
    w = [1 / c[0]]
    while True:
        k = len(w)
        w.append(-sum(c[m] * w[k - m] for m in range(1, min(p, k) + 1)) / c[0])
        if k + 1 > p and max(abs(np.array(w[-p:]) - 1)) < tol:
            return np.array(w[:-p])


def weights(N, p, kind):
    w = np.ones(N + 1)
    tail = {"h": [1.0], "h/2": [0.5], "end": end_weights(p)}[kind]
    for m, wm in enumerate(tail):
        w[N - m] = wm
    return w


def assemble(N, p, kind, V=V):
    h = 1.0 / N
    r = np.arange(N + 1) * h
    w = weights(N, p, kind) * h
    c = fd(np.arange(0, -p - 1, -1)) / h
    A = sp.lil_matrix((N + 1, N + 1))
    B = sp.lil_matrix((N + 1, N + 1))
    for i in range(p, N + 1):                  # fill_mat: rows from ndps+1 (1-based) to the edge
        st = i - np.arange(p + 1)
        A[i, i] += w[i] * V(r[i])
        B[i, i] += w[i]
        for a, ca in zip(st, c):
            for b, cb in zip(st, c):
                A[a, b] += w[i] * ca * cb
    for k in range(p):                         # set_BC_1 at the inner end
        for d in range(1, p + 1):
            A[k, k + d] = A[k + d, k] = B[k, k + d] = B[k + d, k] = 0.0
        A[k, k] = EV_BC
        B[k, k] = 1.0
    A[N, N] += KAPPA                           # set_BC_2: vac%res on the edge diagonal
    return A.tocsc(), B.tocsc()


def reference(n=200, V=V):
    x = np.cos(np.pi * np.arange(n + 1) / n)
    cc = np.r_[2, np.ones(n - 1), 2] * (-1) ** np.arange(n + 1)
    xx = np.tile(x, (n + 1, 1)).T
    D = np.outer(cc, 1 / cc) / (xx - xx.T + np.eye(n + 1))
    D -= np.diag(D.sum(axis=1))
    r = (x + 1) / 2
    D = 2 * D                                  # r = 1 is index 0, r = 0 is index n
    L = -D @ D + np.diag(V(r))
    M = np.eye(n + 1)
    L[n] = 0; L[n, n] = 1; M[n] = 0            # X(0) = 0
    L[0] = D[0]; L[0, 0] += KAPPA; M[0] = 0    # X'(1) + kappa X(1) = 0
    ev = eig(L, M, right=False)
    ev = ev[np.isfinite(ev) & (ev.real > 0)].real
    return ev.min()


def lowest(N, p, kind, near, V=V):
    A, B = assemble(N, p, kind, V)
    return eigsh(A, k=1, M=B, sigma=near, which="LM", return_eigenvectors=False)[0]


# part 1: the weights and the property they are made for
print("part 1: end weights of calc_end_weights, last point first")
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
for p in (1, 2, 3):
    w = end_weights(p)
    if np.allclose(w, 1.0):
        print(f"  p = {p}: all weights are 1 (PB3D does not use them: it keeps 1/2 at the edge point)")
    else:
        print(f"  p = {p}: {len(w)} weights differ from 1 by more than 1e-12: "
              + ", ".join(f"{x:.4f}" for x in w[:6]) + " ...")
    print(f"         sum of (w - 1) = {np.sum(w - 1):+.6f}   (the trapezoidal rule: -0.5)")
    N = 50
    h = 1.0 / N
    X = rng.standard_normal(N + 1)
    X[:p] = 0.0
    c = fd(np.arange(0, -p - 1, -1)) / h
    DX = np.array([sum(c[m] * X[i - m] for m in range(p + 1)) for i in range(p, N + 1)])
    for kind in ("h/2", "end"):
        lhs = h * np.sum(weights(N, p, kind)[p:] * DX)
        print(f"         {kind:>3} weights: h sum w (DX) - X_N = {lhs - X[N]:+.2e}")
print("  (p = 3: 6/11 = %.4f, 108/121 = %.4f)" % (6 / 11, 108 / 121))

# part 2: the lowest eigenvalue of the model
lam = reference()
Ns = np.array([100, 200, 400, 800, 1600, 3200])
print(f"\npart 2: model eigenvalue, reference {lam:.9f} (Chebyshev, 200 points)")
print("  error of the lowest eigenvalue; error*N constant means first order")
res = {}
for p, kind in ((3, "h"), (3, "h/2"), (3, "end"), (2, "h/2"), (2, "end")):
    err = np.array([lowest(N, p, kind, lam) - lam for N in Ns])
    res[(p, kind)] = err
    if len(set(np.sign(err[-3:]))) == 1:
        order = -np.polyfit(np.log(Ns[-3:]), np.log(np.abs(err[-3:])), 1)[0]
        tail = f"   order from the last three: {order:.1f}"
    else:
        tail = "   (changes sign)"
    print(f"  p = {p}, weights {kind:>3}: error " + " ".join(f"{e:+9.2e}" for e in err) + tail)
    print(f"  {'':22} error*N " + " ".join(f"{e * N:+9.3f}" for e, N in zip(err, Ns)))

# part 3: the inner end
lam0 = reference(V=lambda r: 0 * r)
err0 = np.array([lowest(N, 3, "end", lam0, V=lambda r: 0 * r) - lam0 for N in Ns])
print(f"\npart 3: V = 0, reference {lam0:.9f}: the mode reaches the inner end")
print(f"  p = 3, weights end: error " + " ".join(f"{e:+9.2e}" for e in err0))
print(f"  {'':22} error*N " + " ".join(f"{e * N:+9.3f}" for e, N in zip(err0, Ns)))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.6, 3.8))
ax.loglog(Ns, np.abs(res[(3, "h")]), "o-", color=ORANGE, label="p = 3, w_N = 1 (2.47)")
ax.loglog(Ns, np.abs(res[(3, "h/2")]), "s-", color=BLUE, label="p = 3, w_N = 1/2 (F5)")
ax.loglog(Ns, np.abs(res[(3, "end")]), "^-", color=GREEN, label="p = 3, end weights (cba0762)")
ax.set_xlabel("number of radial intervals N")
ax.set_ylabel("|error| of the lowest eigenvalue")
ax.set_title("one-mode copy of fill_mat at a free edge")
ax.legend(fontsize=8)
save(fig, "end_weights_1d.png")

Central differences and boundary style 4 removed (9b36fa6, #38, issue #36)

Your decision of 18 November, for these reasons (from the issue):

  • Central differences (norm_disc_style_sol = 1). Every central first difference is exactly zero for a mode that changes sign from one radial point to the next, so the energy terms with the radial derivative (PV_2, KV_2) did not see such a mode. Near a free edge the stencils were shifted inwards, so the formula was not central there, and no end weights exist for it. No test or example used it; the default has been left differences since July 2017. The runs of the 2017 paper stay reproducible from the tag Weyens2017PB3D.
  • Boundary style 4. It replaced the last row of the matrices by the natural boundary condition, so A and B were not Hermitian. With the end weights it converges to the eigenvalue of style 2, but only at first order: −0.43266, −0.43531, −0.43661 and −0.43725 at 200 to 1600 points on the circular ε = 0.33 kink, against −0.437883 for style 2.

What the code does now:

  • The radial derivative is always a left difference over p + 1 points. fill_mat computes its coefficients once, before the loop over the rows; set_nonzeros uses the half stencil [p, 0]; set_BC_1 zeroes the couplings to the p neighbours.
  • set_BC_4 is gone, and set_BC sets the edge condition at the last point only; the loop over n_max points is gone with n_max.
  • adapt_run_PB3D stops with a message when BC_style(1) is not 1 or BC_style(2) is not 1 or 2. An input file that still sets norm_disc_style_sol stops at the namelist read: PB3D prints "Cannot read user-provided file" and the compiler's message, which for gfortran is "Cannot match namelist object name norm_disc_style_sol" (I checked this with a small program).
  • The output array misc_sol has 7 entries instead of 8: min_r_sol, max_r_sol, norm_disc_prec_sol, BC_style(1), BC_style(2), EV_style, EV_BC. The header of print_output_in listed EV_BC twice and now names EV_style.
  • The cbm18a free-boundary deck uses style 2, and its script checks that value only; the numbers of the earlier comparison with style 4 are kept in Documentation/testing.md. With left differences and style 1 or 2, the eight regression eigenvalues are identical in all 17 printed digits before and after the commit (macOS, one process).

No check on the length of misc_sol (35a40e8)

9b36fa6 made reconstruct_PB3D_in stop when misc_sol did not have 7 entries. 35a40e8 removed that check again: the minimum version check is the guard against older output, and output of an earlier 2.49 build has to be generated again.

Found while preparing this section. Files from before and after 18 November both carry version 2.49, so the version check (min_PB3D_version = 2.49) lets an older file through. reconstruct_PB3D_in then reads its entries shifted by one: entry 4, the old norm_disc_style_sol = 2, becomes BC_style(1), and entry 5, the old BC_style(1) = 1, becomes BC_style(2). POST then handles a free-boundary run as a fixed-boundary one: driver_POST does not read the vacuum, the energy decomposition in sol_ops leaves out the vacuum term because vac%res is not allocated, and the vacuum plot is skipped. No message says so. A fixed-boundary file is read with the right BC_style(2) by chance. Raising prog_version and min_PB3D_version to 2.50 would make the version check refuse such files (a question in Q).
How to check it
  1. Read calc_end_weights against the recurrence above. coeff(ord+1-m) multiplies Xi−m, so coeff(ord+1) is c0 and w_loc(1) = 1/c0. The loop stops when ord successive weights are within 1e-12 of 1 and returns the ones before them. The function end_weights of the demo is the same loop in Python.
  2. In fill_mat, w_end is set before the row loop: from calc_end_weights for BC_style(2) = 2 and p ≥ 2, 1/2 for p = 1, and 1 for a fixed edge. w_q = w_end(n_r-kd) gives the last row (kd = n_r − 1, counted from 0) the weight w_end(1).
  3. In set_BC, the edge condition is set at the last point only; the inner end still sets the first p points.
  4. Compare print_output_in with reconstruct_PB3D_in: the same seven entries of misc_sol, in the same order.

commit message
With left finite differences the stencils of the points beyond the edge do
not exist, so the last norm_disc_prec_sol + 1 unknowns appear in fewer
stencils than the others. With the trapezoidal weight h/2 at the edge point
(4915d4b) the rows of the last points are then not consistent equations,
and the free-boundary eigenvalue keeps an error of first order in n_r_sol:
on the circular eps = 0.33 case the steps between 200, 400, 800, 1600 and
3200 points shrink by 2.7, 2.5 and 2.3, not by 4.

fill_mat now gives the last points of a free edge the weights of the new
num_utilities::calc_end_weights, for left differences of order 2 or 3:
6/11, 108/121, 1.0143, 1.0286, ... times h for order 3. They are the
weights for which the sum over the points of the finite difference of X is
X at the edge, as the integral of X' is, and they follow from the stencil
by a recurrence from the edge inwards. Their sum is that of the
trapezoidal rule.

PB3D, n = 10, free edge, style 2, at 200, 400, 800, 1600, 3200 points:
  circular eps = 0.33  before  -0.438020 -0.437937 -0.437906 -0.437893 -0.437888
                       now     -0.437887 -0.437883 -0.437883 -0.437883 -0.437883
  circular eps = 0.05  before  -0.425616 -0.425556 -0.425526 -0.425514 -0.425509
                       now     -0.425513 -0.425519 -0.425508 -0.425505 -0.425505
The 200-point value of the eps = 0.33 case is 9e-6 from the limit instead
of 3e-4. With order 2 the steps fall by 4 per doubling instead of 2.
cbm18a moves by 3e-6: its first-order convergence is not from the edge.

Boundary style 4 now converges to the value of style 2, at first order
(circular case -0.43266, -0.43531, -0.43661, -0.43725 at 200 to 1600
points); with the trapezoidal weight it converged to -0.469, 7 % off. The
comments on style 4 say so.

Not changed: central differences and order 1 keep the trapezoidal weight.
A fixed edge keeps the full weight: with the same weights the circular
fixed-boundary eigenvalue converged slower (its mode is a spike on the
last five grid points, so that case does not settle it) and cbm18a fixed
barely moved.

Anchors: cbm18a free style 4 -4.5088e-2 (0.1 %), eps = 0.05 free
-4.2551e-1, twin free -4.3901e-1. circ_eps005_free_bnd.sh requires the
200- and 400-point values to agree to 5e-5 (1.3e-5 now, 1.4e-4 with the
trapezoidal weight). New unit test end_weights. macOS, one process: 20 of
24 tests pass; the four mpirun tests segfault here with and without this
change.

commit message
The radial derivative of the solution is now always a left finite
difference over norm_disc_prec_sol + 1 points, and a free boundary is
always BC_style(2) = 2: the vacuum energy is added to the edge block and
the matrices stay Hermitian.

Central differences (input norm_disc_style_sol):
- Every central first difference gives exactly zero for a mode that
  changes sign from one radial point to the next, so the PV_2 and KV_2
  terms did not see such a mode.
- Near a free edge the stencils were shifted inwards, so the formula was
  not central there, and no end weights existed for it.
- No test and no example deck used it.
The input, the variable and the branches on it are gone. fill_mat computes
the difference coefficients once, before the loop over the rows.

Boundary style 4:
- It replaced the last row of the style-2 matrices by the natural boundary
  condition, which made them non-Hermitian. With the end weights it
  converges to the value of style 2 with an error proportional to
  1/n_r_sol; style 2 is far more accurate at every n_r_sol.
- set_BC_4 is gone. set_BC sets the edge condition at the last point only.
- adapt_run_PB3D stops with a message when BC_style(1) is not 1 or
  BC_style(2) is not 1 or 2.

Output: misc_sol has seven entries instead of eight (no difference style).
reconstruct_PB3D_in stops with a message when it finds another number.

Tests: the cbm18a free-boundary deck uses style 2 and the script checks
that value only. The numbers of the earlier cross-check with style 4 are
kept in Documentation/testing.md.

With the default settings no eigenvalue changes: the eight regression
eigenvalues with left differences and style 1 or 2 are identical in all 17
printed digits before and after this commit (macOS, one process,
build without STRUMPACK).

Stage 7

Tests

T

The test layers and what they guard

files tests/unit (8 files), tests/fullstack (8 files), tests/regression, tests/referencetime 1.5 hread

2.47 had no tests that ran. Now ctest has four layers: unit (no PSPLINE, HDF5 or PETSc; 7 suites), full-stack (links all of PB3D; 6 suites, the vacuum ones also with 2 and 4 MPI processes), regression (whole PB3D runs on committed fixtures, against recorded eigenvalues) and smoke tests. CI (GitHub Actions) also runs a sanitizer build of the unit layer, the fortitude lint gate and ratchets on the compiler- and Doxygen-warning counts.

Gaps. (1) No VMEC fixture with ntor > 0 in the repository, so nothing in CI runs the 3-D vacuum on a non-axisymmetric surface or the Nyquist path. A small rippled twin (64 lines, ntor 6) would cover both; its wout would need to be committed. (2) The multi-process regression rows do not run in CI. (3) The implicit-SAVE fix of M1 has no test.

Eigenvalues are ω²/ωA² in PB3D's MISHKA normalisation (norm_style 1); the field-line anchors are reproducibility anchors at a fixed grid, not converged values.

Test sources

All new; the vendored test-drive framework (tests/vendor/test-drive/testdrive.F90) is left out. The sources are shown at b41fd8a: since V0-e (f0273a7) and V0-f (ebd972c) their comments carry no dates or step numbers, and the measured values in the comment of test_exact_exterior_2d are said to be those of the direct diagonals. test_num_utilities holds the unit test end_weights of D (cba0762).

function values, reference299 300        do kd = 1,2301            call circ(t_s_in(kd),x_s(kd,:),norm=norm_s(kd,:))302        end do303        call circ(t_i,x_in,norm=norm_in)304        do kd = 1,2305            call q_pair(gam_arg(x_s(kd,:),x_in),n,ql(kd,:),ierr)306            call check(error, ierr, 0, 'dtorh1 failed')307            if (allocated(error)) return308            Aij(kd) = aij_reg(x_s(kd,:),norm_s(kd,:),x_in,n)309        end do310 311        G = 0._dp312        H = 0._dp313        call calc_GH_int_2(G,H,t_s_in,t_i,x_s,x_in,norm_s,norm_in,Aij,ql,&314            &1.e-30_dp,[b_of(n-1),b_of(n)],n)315 316        do kd = 1,2317            x_pert = x_s(kd,:) + eps*norm_s(kd,:)318            call q_pair(gam_arg(x_pert,x_in),n,q,ierr)319            call check(error, ierr, 0, 'dtorh1 failed')320            if (allocated(error)) return321            fp = q(2)/sqrt(x_in(1)*x_pert(1))322            x_pert = x_s(kd,:) - eps*norm_s(kd,:)323            call q_pair(gam_arg(x_pert,x_in),n,q,ierr)324            fm = q(2)/sqrt(x_in(1)*x_pert(1))325            H_ref = -(t_s_in(2)-t_s_in(1))*(fp-fm)/(2._dp*eps)                 ! vacuum-side sign326            call check(error, H(kd), H_ref, thr=1.e-6_dp, rel=.true., &327                &message='H('//trim(i2str(kd))//') vs numerical derivative: '&328                &//trim(r2str(H(kd)))//' vs '//trim(r2str(H_ref)))329            if (allocated(error)) return330        end do331    end subroutine test_H_regular_numderiv332 333    !> Brute-force reference for the integrals over a subinterval with the334    !! influence point at the left end (t_in = t_s(1)):335    !!   I(kd) = int hat_kd(t) k(t) dt,336    !! by subtracting the exactly integrable logarithmic model337    !!   s_kd(t) = c hat_kd(t) (ln(a_r (t-t_1)) + b-type constants)338    !! and integrating the smooth remainder with panel-refined Gauss rules.339    !!340    !! Shared by the singular and edge-correction tests.341    subroutine brute_force_GH_sing(t_s_in,n,I_G,I_H,ierr)342        real(dp), intent(in) :: t_s_in(2)                                       ! source interval343        integer, intent(in) :: n                                                ! toroidal mode number344        real(dp), intent(out) :: I_G(2), I_H(2)                                 ! integrals345        integer, intent(out) :: ierr                                            ! error status346 347        integer :: kd, id, jd                                                   ! counters348        real(dp) :: x_in(2), norm_in(2), dnorm_in(2)                            ! influence geometry (= left end)349        real(dp) :: x_s2(2)                                                     ! right-end position350        real(dp) :: delta                                                       ! interval length351        real(dp) :: a_r                                                         ! chord coefficient in the log model352        real(dp) :: c_G, c_H_log, c_H_const                                     ! model coefficients353        real(dp) :: I_ln(2)                                                     ! int hat_kd ln(u) du354        real(dp) :: I_hat                                                       ! int hat_kd du355        real(dp) :: u_lo                                                        ! truncation of the remainder integral356        real(dp) :: p_lo, p_hi                                                  ! panel ends357        real(dp) :: t_q, u_q, w_q                                               ! quadrature node in t and u, weight358        real(dp) :: kv, sv(2)                                                   ! kernel and model values359        real(dp) :: aij0                                                        ! Aij at the singular point360        integer, parameter :: n_pan = 60                                        ! quadrature panels361        real(dp), parameter :: pan_fac = 0.7_dp                                 ! geometric panel refinement362 363        ierr = 0364        delta = t_s_in(2)-t_s_in(1)365        call circ(t_s_in(1),x_in,norm=norm_in,dnorm=dnorm_in)366        call circ(t_s_in(2),x_s2)367        aij0 = aij_sing(x_in,norm_in,dnorm_in,n)368 369        ! log model: Q_{n-1/2}(gam(t)) ~ -ln(a_r (t-t_1)) - b_n with370        ! a_r = |x'(t_1)|/(8 R_in) (from the asymptote Q = -1/2 ln(x/32) - b_n371        ! with x = gam-1 ~ (|x'| u)^2/(2 R_in^2))372        a_r = a_min/(8._dp*x_in(1))373 374        ! exact log moments: int_0^delta hat_kd(u) ln(u) du375        I_ln(1) = delta*(0.5_dp*log(delta)-0.75_dp)376        I_ln(2) = delta*(0.5_dp*log(delta)-0.25_dp)377        I_hat = 0.5_dp*delta378 379        ! G model: k_G ~ c_G (-ln(a_r u) - b_n), c_G = -2/sqrt(R_in R_1)380        c_G = -2._dp/x_in(1)                                                    ! R_1 = R_in381        ! H model: k_H ~ c_H_log (-ln(a_r u) - b_n) + c_H_const with382        ! c_H_log = -norm_R(t_1)/R_1 / R_in and the finite part of the383        ! -Aij (gam Q_{n-1/2} - Q_{n-3/2}) term: (gam Q - Q') -> -2/(2n-1)384        c_H_log = norm_in(1)/(x_in(1)**2)                                       ! vacuum-side sign (as k_H)385        c_H_const = -2._dp/x_in(1)*aij0*2._dp/(2._dp*n-1._dp)386 387        do kd = 1,2388            I_G(kd) = c_G*(-I_ln(kd)-(log(a_r)+b_of(n))*I_hat)389            I_H(kd) = c_H_log*(-I_ln(kd)-(log(a_r)+b_of(n))*I_hat) + &390                &c_H_const*I_hat391        end do392 393        ! truncation: gamma-1 >= ~3e-10 for dtorh reliability394        u_lo = sqrt(3.e-10_dp*2._dp*x_in(1)*x_s2(1))/a_min395 396        ! panel-refined quadrature of the smooth remainders on [u_lo,delta]397        p_hi = delta398        do id = 1,n_pan399            p_lo = max(u_lo,p_hi*pan_fac)400            if (id.eq.n_pan) p_lo = u_lo401            do jd = 1,16402                u_q = 0.5_dp*(p_lo+p_hi) + 0.5_dp*(p_hi-p_lo)*gl_x(jd)403                w_q = 0.5_dp*(p_hi-p_lo)*gl_w(jd)404                t_q = t_s_in(1) + u_q405                ! model values406                sv(1) = c_G*(-log(a_r*u_q)-b_of(n))407                sv(2) = c_H_log*(-log(a_r*u_q)-b_of(n)) + c_H_const408                ! true kernels minus models, weighted by the hat functions409                call k_G(t_q,x_in,n,kv,ierr)410                if (ierr.ne.0) return411                I_G(1) = I_G(1) + w_q*(1._dp-u_q/delta)*(kv-sv(1))412                I_G(2) = I_G(2) + w_q*(u_q/delta)*(kv-sv(1))413                call k_H(t_q,x_in,n,kv,ierr)414                if (ierr.ne.0) return415                I_H(1) = I_H(1) + w_q*(1._dp-u_q/delta)*(kv-sv(2))416                I_H(2) = I_H(2) + w_q*(u_q/delta)*(kv-sv(2))417            end do418            p_hi = p_lo419            if (p_hi.le.u_lo) exit420        end do421    end subroutine brute_force_GH_sing422 423    !> Singular subinterval (influence point = left end, both ends within the424    !! analytical-approximation region): the analytical integrals of425    !! calc_GH_int_2 against brute-force quadrature, at two interval sizes to426    !! also confirm convergence of the approximation.427    subroutine test_GH_singular_quadrature(error)428        type(error_type), allocatable, intent(out) :: error429 430        integer, parameter :: n = 2                                             ! toroidal mode number431        real(dp), parameter :: t_1 = 0.4_dp                                     ! left end = influence point432        real(dp), parameter :: deltas(2) = [5.e-3_dp,5.e-4_dp]                  ! interval sizes433        real(dp), parameter :: tols(2) = [2.e-2_dp,2.e-3_dp]                    ! relative tolerances434 435        integer :: id, kd, ierr                                                 ! counters, error status436        real(dp) :: t_s_in(2)                                                   ! source interval437        real(dp) :: G(2), H(2)                                                  ! kernel results438        real(dp) :: x_s(2,2), norm_s(2,2)                                       ! source geometry439        real(dp) :: x_in(2), norm_in(2), dnorm_in(2)                            ! influence geometry440        real(dp) :: Aij(2), ql(2,2)                                             ! helpers441        real(dp) :: rho2_2                                                      ! squared distance to right end442        real(dp) :: I_G(2), I_H(2)                                              ! brute-force references443 444        do id = 1,size(deltas)445            t_s_in = [t_1,t_1+deltas(id)]446            do kd = 1,2447                call circ(t_s_in(kd),x_s(kd,:),norm=norm_s(kd,:))448            end do449            call circ(t_1,x_in,norm=norm_in,dnorm=dnorm_in)450            rho2_2 = sum((x_s(2,:)-x_in)**2)451 452            ! at singular points the caller supplies the limit form of Aij453            ! and does not evaluate the toroidal harmonics454            Aij = aij_sing(x_in,norm_in,dnorm_in,n)455            ql = 0._dp456 457            G = 0._dp458            H = 0._dp459            call calc_GH_int_2(G,H,t_s_in,t_1,x_s,x_in,norm_s,norm_in,Aij,ql,&460                &4._dp*rho2_2,[b_of(n-1),b_of(n)],n)                            ! tol > rho2_2: both ends in analytical region461 462            call brute_force_GH_sing(t_s_in,n,I_G,I_H,ierr)463            call check(error, ierr, 0, 'brute-force quadrature failed')464            if (allocated(error)) return465 466            do kd = 1,2467                call check(error, G(kd), I_G(kd), &468                    &thr=tols(id)*abs(I_G(kd)), &469                    &message='singular G('//trim(i2str(kd))//'), delta = '//&470                    &trim(r2str(deltas(id)))//': '//trim(r2str(G(kd)))//&471                    &' vs '//trim(r2str(I_G(kd))))472                if (allocated(error)) return473                call check(error, H(kd), I_H(kd), &474                    &thr=tols(id)*abs(I_H(kd)), &475                    &message='singular H('//trim(i2str(kd))//'), delta = '//&476                    &trim(r2str(deltas(id)))//': '//trim(r2str(H(kd)))//&477                    &' vs '//trim(r2str(I_H(kd))))478                if (allocated(error)) return479            end do480        end do481    end subroutine test_GH_singular_quadrature482 483    !> Near-singular subinterval with only the left end inside the484    !! analytical-approximation region (tol between the two rho^2): the485    !! implementation adds a trapezoidal correction for the difference486    !! between the true toroidal function and its approximation at the far487    !! end, which needs the toroidal harmonics there.488    subroutine test_GH_edge_correction(error)489        type(error_type), allocatable, intent(out) :: error490 491        integer, parameter :: n = 2                                             ! toroidal mode number492        real(dp), parameter :: t_1 = 0.4_dp                                     ! left end = influence point493        real(dp), parameter :: delta = 5.e-3_dp                                 ! interval size494        real(dp), parameter :: tol_rel = 2.e-2_dp                               ! relative tolerance495 496        integer :: kd, ierr                                                     ! counter, error status497        real(dp) :: t_s_in(2)                                                   ! source interval498        real(dp) :: G(2), H(2)                                                  ! kernel results499        real(dp) :: x_s(2,2), norm_s(2,2)                                       ! source geometry500        real(dp) :: x_in(2), norm_in(2), dnorm_in(2)                            ! influence geometry501        real(dp) :: Aij(2), ql(2,2)                                             ! helpers502        real(dp) :: rho2_2                                                      ! squared distance to right end503        real(dp) :: I_G(2), I_H(2)                                              ! brute-force references504 505        t_s_in = [t_1,t_1+delta]506        do kd = 1,2507            call circ(t_s_in(kd),x_s(kd,:),norm=norm_s(kd,:))508        end do509        call circ(t_1,x_in,norm=norm_in,dnorm=dnorm_in)510        rho2_2 = sum((x_s(2,:)-x_in)**2)511 512        ! left end singular: limit Aij; right end regular: caller supplies513        ! the toroidal harmonics and the regular Aij there514        Aij(1) = aij_sing(x_in,norm_in,dnorm_in,n)515        Aij(2) = aij_reg(x_s(2,:),norm_s(2,:),x_in,n)516        ql = 0._dp517        call q_pair(gam_arg(x_s(2,:),x_in),n,ql(2,:),ierr)518        call check(error, ierr, 0, 'dtorh1 failed')519        if (allocated(error)) return520 521        G = 0._dp522        H = 0._dp523        call calc_GH_int_2(G,H,t_s_in,t_1,x_s,x_in,norm_s,norm_in,Aij,ql,&524            &0.25_dp*rho2_2,[b_of(n-1),b_of(n)],n)                              ! tol < rho2_2: right end outside analytical region525 526        call brute_force_GH_sing(t_s_in,n,I_G,I_H,ierr)527        call check(error, ierr, 0, 'brute-force quadrature failed')528        if (allocated(error)) return529 530        do kd = 1,2531            call check(error, G(kd), I_G(kd), thr=tol_rel*abs(I_G(kd)), &532                &message='edge-corrected G('//trim(i2str(kd))//'): '//&533                &trim(r2str(G(kd)))//' vs '//trim(r2str(I_G(kd))))534            if (allocated(error)) return535            call check(error, H(kd), I_H(kd), thr=tol_rel*abs(I_H(kd)), &536                &message='edge-corrected H('//trim(i2str(kd))//'): '//&537                &trim(r2str(H(kd)))//' vs '//trim(r2str(I_H(kd))))538            if (allocated(error)) return539        end do540    end subroutine test_GH_edge_correction541 542    !> Regular subinterval of the 3-D (field-line aligned) kernels: G is the543    !! free-space Green's function -1/|x_s - x_in| and H its directional544    !! derivative along the source normal, checked against a central545    !! difference.546    subroutine test_GH_int_1_regular(error)547        type(error_type), allocatable, intent(out) :: error548 549        real(dp), parameter :: eps = 1.e-7_dp                                   ! step for central difference550 551        integer :: id, kd                                                       ! counters552        real(dp) :: G(2), H(2)                                                  ! kernel results553        real(dp) :: x_s(4,3), norm_s(4,3)                                       ! source geometry (four-point stencil)554        real(dp) :: x_in(3)                                                     ! influence point555        real(dp) :: x_pert(3)                                                   ! perturbed point556        real(dp) :: fp, fm, r, H_ref                                            ! function values, distance, reference557 558        ! straight stencil, the interval between points 2 and 3; the influence559        ! point is far (26 interval lengths), so the endpoint values are used560        do id = 1,4561            x_s(id,:) = [2.9_dp,0.1_dp,0.2_dp] + &562                &(id-2)*[-0.05_dp,0.05_dp,0.05_dp]563            norm_s(id,:) = [0.9_dp,0.1_dp,0.3_dp] + (id-2)*[-0.1_dp,0.1_dp,0.1_dp]564        end do565        x_in = [1.5_dp,-1.0_dp,0.5_dp]566 567        G = 0._dp568        H = 0._dp569        call calc_GH_int_1(G,H,x_s,x_in,norm_s,[1._dp,0.1_dp,1._dp,0.5_dp],&570            &[0.1_dp,0.1_dp],1.e-30_dp,2)571 572        do kd = 1,2573            r = sqrt(sum((x_s(kd+1,:)-x_in)**2))574            call check(error, G(kd), -1._dp/r, thr=1.e-14_dp, rel=.true., &575                &message='G('//trim(i2str(kd))//') mismatch')576            if (allocated(error)) return577 578            ! H = norm . grad_s (-1/r), via central difference579            x_pert = x_s(kd+1,:) + eps*norm_s(kd+1,:)580            fp = -1._dp/sqrt(sum((x_pert-x_in)**2))581            x_pert = x_s(kd+1,:) - eps*norm_s(kd+1,:)582            fm = -1._dp/sqrt(sum((x_pert-x_in)**2))583            H_ref = (fp-fm)/(2._dp*eps)584            call check(error, H(kd), H_ref, thr=1.e-6_dp, rel=.true., &585                &message='H('//trim(i2str(kd))//') vs numerical derivative: '&586                &//trim(r2str(H(kd)))//' vs '//trim(r2str(H_ref)))587            if (allocated(error)) return588        end do589    end subroutine test_GH_int_1_regular590end module test_vac_kernels
