1!------------------------------------------------------------------------------!2!> Golden-file test of the HELENA equilibrium parser (HELENA_ops.read_HEL)3!! on the committed cbm18a_extended_vac fixture (the same file the physics4!! regression layer runs the full code on).5!!6!! read_HEL is deterministic given the file, so the parsed and derived7!! quantities (grid sizes, profiles, MISHKA-normalization factors, geometry)8!! are pinned against golden values recorded from the current9!! implementation; internal-consistency relations that must hold exactly by10!! construction (rot_t = 1/q, flux_t' = q flux_p', flux_p' = 2 pi) and an11!! implementation-independent trapezoidal cross-check of the toroidal flux12!! integral guard against parsing- and normalization regressions with13!! independent references.14!!15!! The fixture directory is passed through the environment variable16!! PB3D_FIXTURE_DIR (set by CTest; the test is only registered when the17!! fixture is available).18!------------------------------------------------------------------------------!19module test_read_HEL20    use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: error_unit21    use testdrive, only: new_unittest, unittest_type, error_type, check22    use num_vars, only: dp, pi23    use str_utilities, only: r2str, i2str24 25    implicit none26    private27    public collect_read_HEL28 29contains30    !> Collect the tests.31    subroutine collect_read_HEL(testsuite)32        type(unittest_type), allocatable, intent(out) :: testsuite(:)33 34        testsuite = [ &35            &new_unittest("cbm18a_golden", test_cbm18a_golden) &36            &]37    end subroutine collect_read_HEL38 39    !> Parse the fixture and pin everything.40    subroutine test_cbm18a_golden(error)41        use num_vars, only: eq_i, eq_name42        use HELENA_ops, only: read_HEL43        use HELENA_vars, only: pres_H, q_saf_H, rot_t_H, flux_p_H, flux_t_H, &44            &nchi, chi_H, ias, RBphi_H, R_H, Z_H, RMtoG_H, BMtoG_H45 46        type(error_type), allocatable, intent(out) :: error47 48        integer :: ierr, kd                                                     ! error status, counter49        integer :: n_r_in                                                       ! number of normal points50        integer :: istat                                                        ! status51        logical :: use_pol_flux_H                                               ! whether HELENA uses poloidal flux52        character(len=1024) :: fix_dir                                          ! fixture directory53        real(dp) :: flux_t_trap                                                 ! trapezoidal toroidal flux54        real(dp) :: ellip                                                       ! ellipticity55 56        ! open the fixture on the equilibrium unit57        call get_environment_variable('PB3D_FIXTURE_DIR',fix_dir,&58            &status=istat)59        call check(error, istat, 0, 'PB3D_FIXTURE_DIR not set')60        if (allocated(error)) return61        eq_name = trim(fix_dir)//'/cbm18a_extended_vac.12'62        open(unit=eq_i,file=trim(eq_name),status='old',action='read',&63            &iostat=istat)64        call check(error, istat, 0, 'could not open '//trim(eq_name))65        if (allocated(error)) return66 67        ierr = read_HEL(n_r_in,use_pol_flux_H)68        close(eq_i)69        call check(error, ierr, 0, 'read_HEL failed')70        if (allocated(error)) return71 72        write(error_unit,'(A,I5,A,I5,A,I2)') '   [read_HEL] n_r_in = ',&73            &n_r_in,', nchi = ',nchi,', ias = ',ias74        write(error_unit,'(A,2ES23.15)') '   [read_HEL] q axis/edge:    ',&75            &q_saf_H(1,0),q_saf_H(n_r_in,0)76        write(error_unit,'(A,2ES23.15)') '   [read_HEL] pres axis/edge: ',&77            &pres_H(1,0),pres_H(n_r_in,0)78        write(error_unit,'(A,2ES23.15)') '   [read_HEL] F axis/edge:    ',&79            &RBphi_H(1,0),RBphi_H(n_r_in,0)80        write(error_unit,'(A,2ES23.15)') '   [read_HEL] flux_p/t edge:  ',&81            &flux_p_H(n_r_in,0),flux_t_H(n_r_in,0)82        write(error_unit,'(A,2ES23.15)') '   [read_HEL] RMtoG, BMtoG:   ',&83            &RMtoG_H,BMtoG_H84        write(error_unit,'(A,3ES23.15)') '   [read_HEL] R lims, max Z:  ',&85            &minval(R_H),maxval(R_H),maxval(Z_H)86 87        ! grid and symmetry metadata (from the file header)88        call check(error, ias, 0, 'cbm18a is up-down symmetric')89        if (allocated(error)) return90        call check(error, n_r_in, 801, 'n_r_in golden')91        if (allocated(error)) return92        call check(error, nchi, 401, 'nchi golden')93        if (allocated(error)) return94        call check(error, use_pol_flux_H, 'HELENA uses poloidal flux')95        if (allocated(error)) return96 97        ! symmetric equilibria are given on the half poloidal circumference98        ! (the file stores the angles with 8 significant digits)99        call check(error, abs(chi_H(1)).lt.1.e-12_dp .and. &100            &abs(chi_H(nchi)-pi).lt.1.e-6_dp, &101            &'chi grid spans [0, pi] for ias = 0')102        if (allocated(error)) return103 104        ! exact-by-construction consistency relations105        call check(error, maxval(abs(flux_p_H(:,1)-2._dp*pi)).lt.1.e-12_dp, &106            &'flux_p_H'' = 2 pi (MISHKA normalization)')107        if (allocated(error)) return108        call check(error, maxval(abs(flux_t_H(:,1)-&109            &q_saf_H(:,0)*2._dp*pi)).lt.1.e-10_dp, &110            &'flux_t'' = q flux_p''')111        if (allocated(error)) return112        call check(error, maxval(abs(rot_t_H(:,0)*q_saf_H(:,0)-1._dp)).lt.&113            &1.e-12_dp, 'rot_t = 1/q')114        if (allocated(error)) return115 116        ! monotonicity of the fluxes117        do kd = 2,n_r_in118            call check(error, flux_p_H(kd,0).gt.flux_p_H(kd-1,0) .and. &119                &flux_t_H(kd,0).gt.flux_t_H(kd-1,0), &120                &'fluxes increase monotonically')121            if (allocated(error)) return122        end do123 124        ! implementation-independent cross-check: the toroidal flux is the125        ! integral of q over the poloidal flux (trapezoid, so only accurate126        ! to the grid resolution)127        flux_t_trap = 0._dp128        do kd = 2,n_r_in129            flux_t_trap = flux_t_trap + &130                &0.5_dp*(q_saf_H(kd,0)+q_saf_H(kd-1,0))*&131                &(flux_p_H(kd,0)-flux_p_H(kd-1,0))132        end do133        call check(error, abs(flux_t_H(n_r_in,0)-flux_t_trap).lt.&134            &1.e-3_dp*abs(flux_t_trap), &135            &'flux_t edge vs trapezoidal integral of q dpsi: '//&136            &trim(r2str(flux_t_H(n_r_in,0)))//' vs '//&137            &trim(r2str(flux_t_trap)))138        if (allocated(error)) return139 140        ! geometry: degenerate first normal point on the magnetic axis141        call check(error, maxval(abs(R_H(:,1)-R_H(1,1))).lt.1.e-12_dp .and. &142            &maxval(abs(Z_H(:,1))).lt.1.e-12_dp, &143            &'first normal point degenerates to the magnetic axis')144        if (allocated(error)) return145 146        ! golden profile and normalization values (recorded from the147        ! implementation; if these move, the parser or the MISHKA148        ! normalization changed)149        call check(error, q_saf_H(1,0), 1.0521365_dp, thr=1.e-10_dp, &150            &rel=.true., message='q on axis golden')151        if (allocated(error)) return152        call check(error, q_saf_H(n_r_in,0), 25.031802_dp, thr=1.e-10_dp, &153            &rel=.true., message='q at edge golden')154        if (allocated(error)) return155        call check(error, pres_H(1,0), 1.2251493e-2_dp, thr=1.e-10_dp, &156            &rel=.true., message='pressure on axis golden')157        if (allocated(error)) return158        call check(error, flux_p_H(n_r_in,0), &159            &3.767600982734008e-1_dp, thr=1.e-10_dp, rel=.true., &160            &message='poloidal flux at edge golden')161        if (allocated(error)) return162        call check(error, RMtoG_H, 8.319203019203020e-1_dp, thr=1.e-10_dp, &163            &rel=.true., message='RMtoG golden')164        if (allocated(error)) return165        call check(error, BMtoG_H, 1.1634848_dp, thr=1.e-10_dp, rel=.true., &166            &message='BMtoG golden')167        if (allocated(error)) return168 169        ! ellipticity from the parsed flux surfaces (ias = 0: top half)170        ellip = 2._dp*maxval(Z_H)/(maxval(R_H)-minval(R_H))171        call check(error, ellip, 9.9995911e-1_dp, thr=1.e-8_dp, rel=.true., &172            &message='ellipticity golden')173        if (allocated(error)) return174    end subroutine test_cbm18a_golden175end module test_read_HEL

1!------------------------------------------------------------------------------!2!> Rank-agnostic helpers for the full-stack tests.3!!4!! The vacuum matrices G and H live in the 2-D block-cyclic ScaLAPACK5!! distribution described in vac_vars.init_vac and the response vac%res only6!! on the last process, so the tests never index them as if they were7!! global: they assert on quantities evaluated identically on every process,8!! through vac_utilities (n_col1_loc, vec_glob2dis, dis_matvec) and9!! gather_res below. Because every process asserts on the same numbers,10!! test-drive's control flow cannot diverge between ranks, which would11!! otherwise deadlock collective calls in subsequent tests.12!------------------------------------------------------------------------------!13module fullstack_utils14    use num_vars, only: dp15    use vac_vars, only: vac_type16    implicit none17    private18    public gather_res19 20contains21    !> Broadcast the vacuum response from the last process (the only one22    !! where calc_vac_res leaves it) to all.23    integer function gather_res(vac,res) result(ierr)24        use MPI25        use num_vars, only: rank, n_procs26 27        type(vac_type), intent(in) :: vac                                       !< vacuum variables28        complex(dp), intent(inout) :: res(:,:)                                  !< global response on all processes29 30        ierr = 031        if (rank.eq.n_procs-1) res = vac%res32        call MPI_Bcast(res,size(res),MPI_DOUBLE_COMPLEX,n_procs-1,&33            &MPI_COMM_WORLD,ierr)34    end function gather_res35end module fullstack_utils

1!------------------------------------------------------------------------------!2!> Driver for the PB3D full-stack tests, built on the test-drive framework.3!!4!! In contrast to the unit tests (tests/unit), these tests link against the5!! complete pb3d_modules library, and therefore require the full dependency6!! stack (MPI, ScaLAPACK, STRUMPACK, ...). The executable initializes MPI7!! itself, so it can be run directly (MPI singleton mode) or under8!! mpirun -n <N>; the test suites are rank-agnostic (they assert on globally9!! gathered quantities, see fullstack_utils), so multi-process runs exercise10!! the block-cyclic distribution paths with identical assertions.11!!12!! Every rank runs every test. Rank 0 reports to stderr; the other ranks13!! write to pb3d_fullstack_tests_rank<r>.log in the working directory, so14!! rank-specific failures remain inspectable without interleaving output.15!! The failure count is combined over all ranks at the end.16!!17!! Usage:18!!  - no arguments:         run all test suites19!!  - one argument:         run only that suite (e.g. "vac_kernels")20!!  - two arguments:        run one test of one suite21!------------------------------------------------------------------------------!22program pb3d_fullstack_tester23    use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: error_unit24    use MPI25    use testdrive, only: run_testsuite, new_testsuite, testsuite_type, &26        &select_suite, run_selected, get_argument27    use test_vac_kernels, only: collect_vac_kernels28    use test_vac_greens, only: collect_vac_greens29    use test_vac_3d, only: collect_vac_3d30    use test_splines, only: collect_splines31    use test_calc_int_vol, only: collect_calc_int_vol32    use test_read_HEL, only: collect_read_HEL33    use num_vars, only: dp, rank, n_procs, prog_name, max_it_zero, tol_zero, &34        &max_nr_backtracks_HH, rich_restart_lvl35    use rich_vars, only: rich_lvl36    use X_vars, only: n_mod_X37    use str_utilities, only: i2str38    use messages, only: init_output39 40    implicit none41 42    ! local variables43    integer :: stat                                                             ! cumulative failure count44    integer :: stat_glob                                                        ! failure count over all ranks45    integer :: is                                                               ! suite index46    integer :: ierr                                                             ! error variable47    integer :: out_unit                                                         ! unit for test output (error_unit on rank 0)48    character(len=:), allocatable :: suite_name, test_name                      ! command-line selection49    type(testsuite_type), allocatable :: testsuites(:)                          ! all test suites50    character(len=*), parameter :: fmt = '("#", *(1x, a))'                      ! output format51 52    ! minimal PB3D global state so that library routines (messages, BLACS53    ! grids, ...) work outside the full PB3D/POST startup sequence54    call MPI_init(ierr)55    if (ierr.ne.0) error stop 'MPI_init failed'56    call MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_Comm_world,rank,ierr)57    call MPI_Comm_size(MPI_Comm_world,n_procs,ierr)58    prog_name = 'TEST'59    n_mod_X = 1                                                                 ! vac%res is allocated with this size; overridden by the response test60    max_it_zero = 100                                                           ! zero-finder settings, normally set during input61    tol_zero = 1.e-10_dp                                                        ! processing (see input_ops); calc_GH_2 needs them62    max_nr_backtracks_HH = 20                                                   ! for its singularity tolerance63    rich_lvl = 1                                                                ! no Richardson extrapolation in the tests64    rich_restart_lvl = 165    call init_output()66 67    ! rank 0 reports to stderr, other ranks to per-rank log files68    if (rank.eq.0) then69        out_unit = error_unit70    else71        open(newunit=out_unit,file='pb3d_fullstack_tests_rank'//&72            &trim(i2str(rank))//'.log',status='replace',action='write')73    end if74 75    stat = 076 77    testsuites = [ &78        &new_testsuite("vac_kernels", collect_vac_kernels), &79        &new_testsuite("vac_greens", collect_vac_greens), &80        &new_testsuite("vac_3d", collect_vac_3d), &81        &new_testsuite("splines", collect_splines), &82        &new_testsuite("calc_int_vol", collect_calc_int_vol), &83        &new_testsuite("read_HEL", collect_read_HEL) &84        &]85 86    call get_argument(1, suite_name)87    call get_argument(2, test_name)88 89    if (allocated(suite_name)) then90        is = select_suite(testsuites, suite_name)91        if (is.gt.0 .and. is.le.size(testsuites)) then92            if (allocated(test_name)) then93                write(out_unit, fmt) "Suite:", testsuites(is)%name94                call run_selected(testsuites(is)%collect, test_name, &95                    &out_unit, stat)96                if (stat.lt.0) error stop 197            else98                write(out_unit, fmt) "Testing:", testsuites(is)%name99                call run_testsuite(testsuites(is)%collect, out_unit, stat)100            end if101        else102            write(out_unit, fmt) "Available testsuites"103            do is = 1, size(testsuites)104                write(out_unit, fmt) "-", testsuites(is)%name105            end do106            error stop 1107        end if108    else109        do is = 1, size(testsuites)110            write(out_unit, fmt) "Testing:", testsuites(is)%name111            call run_testsuite(testsuites(is)%collect, out_unit, stat)112        end do113    end if114 115    ! combine the failure count over all ranks, so a rank-local failure116    ! cannot be masked by a clean rank 0117    stat_glob = stat118    call MPI_Allreduce(stat,stat_glob,1,MPI_INTEGER,MPI_SUM,MPI_Comm_world,&119        &ierr)120    if (ierr.ne.0) stat_glob = max(1,stat_glob)121 122    call MPI_finalize(ierr)123 124    if (stat_glob.gt.0) then125        write(out_unit, '(i0, 1x, a)') stat_glob, &126            &"test failure(s) over all ranks!"127        error stop 1128    end if129end program pb3d_fullstack_tester

The par_lim window and the13!! par_id_mem memory indices are checked against the same formulas.14!------------------------------------------------------------------------------!15module test_PB3D_utilities16    use testdrive, only: new_unittest, unittest_type, error_type, check17    use num_vars, only: dp18    use str_utilities, only: i2str19    use grid_vars, only: grid_type20    use flat_vars, only: var_flat_type21    use PB3D_utilities, only: setup_rich_id, setup_par_id, conv_flat2ND22 23    implicit none24    private25    public collect_PB3D_utilities26 27contains28    !> Collect the tests.29    subroutine collect_PB3D_utilities(testsuite)30        type(unittest_type), allocatable, intent(out) :: testsuite(:)31 32        testsuite = [ &33            &new_unittest("setup_rich_id", test_setup_rich_id), &34            &new_unittest("par_id_partition", test_par_id_partition), &35            &new_unittest("par_id_window_and_memory", test_par_id_window), &36            &new_unittest("conv_flat2ND", test_conv_flat2ND) &37            &]38    end subroutine collect_PB3D_utilities39 40    !> Richardson level range: only the last level, or all levels when41    !! I63        integer, parameter :: n_par = 17                                        ! 1 + 4 k with k = 464 65        type(grid_type) :: grid                                                 ! grid (only n(1) is used)66        integer :: lvl, id                                                      ! counters67        integer :: par_id(3)                                                    ! parallel id68        integer :: count_vis(17)                                                ! how often each point is visited69 70        grid%n = [n_par,1,1]71 72        ! without combination: the whole grid at once73        par_id = setup_par_id(grid,rich_lvl_max,rich_lvl_max)74        call check(error, all(par_id.eq.[1,n_par,1]), &75            &'no tot_rich: whole grid with stride 1')76        if (allocated(error)) return77 78        ! with combination: partition over the levels79        count_vis = 080        do lvl = 1,rich_lvl_max81            par_id = setup_par_id(grid,rich_lvl_max,lvl,tot_rich=.true.)82            call check(error, par_id(1).ge.1 .and. par_id(2).le.n_par .and. &83                &par_id(3).ge.1, 'valid range for level '//trim(i2str(lvl)))84            if (allocated(error)) return85            do id = par_id(1),par_id(2),par_id(3)86                count_vis(id) = count_vis(id) + 187            end do88        end do89        call check(error, all(count_vis.eq.1), &90            &'levels partition the grid (every point exactly once)')91        if (allocated(error)) return92 93        ! the explicit expected ids (s and p from the docstring)94        call check(error, all(setup_par_id(grid,3,1,tot_rich=.true.).eq.&95            &[1,17,4]), 'level 1: s = 4, p = 1')96        if (allocated(error)) return97        call check(error, all(setup_par_id(grid,3,2,tot_rich=.true.).eq.&98            &[3,15,4]), 'level 2: s = 4, p = 3')99        if (allocated(error)) return100        call check(error, all(setup_par_id(grid,3,3,tot_rich=.true.).eq.&101            &[2,16,2]), 'level 3: s = 2, p = 2')102        if (allocated(error)) return103    end subroutine test_par_id_partition104 105    !> A par_lim window returns exactly the full-range points that fall106    !! expected number of points120        logical :: glob_set(17)                                                 ! full-range index set of this level121 122        grid%n = [n_par,1,1]123 124        do lvl = 1,rich_lvl_max125            ! full-range set of this level126            par_id = setup_par_id(grid,rich_lvl_max,lvl,tot_rich=.true.)127            glob_set = .false.128            do id = par_id(1),par_id(2),par_id(3)129                glob_set(id) = .true.130            end do131 132            ! memory indices: contiguous, starting at the position of the155            ! first windowed point in the per-level storage156            call check(error, par_id_mem(2)-par_id_mem(1)+1, n_exp, &157                &'memory range size, level '//trim(i2str(lvl)))158            if (allocated(error)) return159        end do160 161        ! documented explicit case: level 1, window [5,13]: global points162        ! 5, 9, 13 are the 2nd..4th stored level-1 points163        par_id_win = setup_par_id(grid,rich_lvl_max,1,tot_rich=.true.,&164            &par_lim=par_lim,par_id_mem=par_id_mem)165        call check(error, all(par_id_win.eq.[1,9,4]) .and. &166            &all(par_id_mem.eq.[2,4]), 'level-1 window: ids [1,9,4], mem [2,4]')167        if (allocated(error)) return168    end subroutine test_par_id_window169 170    !> 1-D to n-D conversion restores shape, bounds and values.171    subroutine test_conv_flat2ND(error)172        type(error_type), allocatable, intent(out) :: error173 174        type(var_flat_type) :: var                                              ! counters177        integer :: ld                                                           ! linear counter178 179        ! 2-D with non-unit lower bounds: (0:2, 3:4)180        var%tot_i_min = [0,3]181        var%tot_i_max = [2,4]182        var%p = [(1._dp*ld, ld = 1,6)]183        call conv_flat2ND(var,var_2D)184        call check(error, lbound(var_2D,1).eq.0 .and. ubound(var_2D,1).eq.2 &185            &.and. lbound(var_2D,2).eq.3 .and. ubound(var_2D,2).eq.4, &186            &'2-D bounds')187        if (allocated(error)) return188        ld = 0189        do jd = 3,4190            do id = 0,2191                ld = ld + 1192                call check(error, var_2D(id,jd), 1._dp*ld, &193                    &thr=0._dp, message='2-D column-major order')194                if (allocated(error)) return195            end do196        end do197 198        ! 1!------------------------------------------------------------------------------!2!> Unit tests of the zero finders in num_ops (Householder with backtracking,3!! Zhang bracketing) on functions with known roots.4!------------------------------------------------------------------------------!5module test_num_ops6    use testdrive, only: new_unittest, unittest_type, error_type, check7    use num_vars, only: dp, pi8    use str_utilities, only: r2str9    use num_ops, only: calc_zero_HH, calc_zero_Zhang10 11    implicit none12    private13    public collect_num_ops14 15contains16    !> Collect the tests.17    subroutine collect_num_ops(testsuite)18        type(unittest_type), allocatable, intent(out) :: testsuite(:)19 20        testsuite = [ &21            &new_unittest("zero_HH", test_zero_HH), &22            &new_unittest("zero_Zhang", test_zero_Zhang) &23            &]24    end subroutine collect_num_ops25 26    !> Householder zero finder on f = x^2 - 2 (root sqrt(2)), orders 1-3.27    subroutine test_zero_HH(error)28        type(error_type), allocatable, intent(out) :: error29 30        integer :: ord                                                          ! Householder order31        real(dp) :: zero                                                        ! found zero32        character(len=:), allocatable :: msg                                    ! error message33 34        do ord = 1,335            zero = 0._dp36            msg = trim(calc_zero_HH(zero,f_sq2,ord,1.0_dp))37            call check(error, len_trim(msg), 0, 'calc_zero_HH returned: '//msg)38            if (allocated(error)) return39            call check(error, zero, sqrt(2._dp), thr=1.e-8_dp, rel=.true., &40                &message='HH order '//trim(r2str(real(ord,dp)))//' zero: '//&41                &trim(r2str(zero)))42            if (allocated(error)) return43        end do44    end subroutine test_zero_HH45 46    !> Zhang bracketing zero finder on f = cos (root pi/2).47    subroutine test_zero_Zhang(error)48        type(error_type), allocatable, intent(out) :: error49 50        real(dp) :: zero                                                        ! found zero51        character(len=:), allocatable :: msg                                    ! error message52 53        zero = 0._dp54        msg = trim(calc_zero_Zhang(zero,f_cos,[1.0_dp,2.0_dp]))55        call check(error, len_trim(msg), 0, 'calc_zero_Zhang returned: '//msg)56        if (allocated(error)) return57        call check(error, zero, pi/2._dp, thr=1.e-8_dp, rel=.true., &58            &message='Zhang zero: '//trim(r2str(zero)))59        if (allocated(error)) return60    end subroutine test_zero_Zhang61 62    !> f = x^2 - 2 and derivatives, in the calc_zero_HH callback form.63    function f_sq2(x,ord)64        real(dp), intent(in) :: x65        integer, intent(in) :: ord66        real(dp) :: f_sq267 68        select case (ord)69            case (0)70                f_sq2 = x**2 - 2._dp71            case (1)72                f_sq2 = 2._dp*x73            case (2)74                f_sq2 = 2._dp75            case default76                f_sq2 = 0._dp77        end select78    end function f_sq279 80    !> f = cos, in the calc_zero_Zhang callback form.81    function f_cos(x)82        real(dp), intent(in) :: x83        real(dp) :: f_cos84 85        f_cos = cos(x)86    end function f_cos87end module test_num_ops

Stage 9

Afterwards: a cheaper vacuum

E

Reading guide to the wave report

file Documentation/vacuum_wave_report/report.pdf on branch exp/vacuum-wave-prototype (worktree .claude/worktrees/vacuum-wave-prototype), 7 pages, 4 Novembertime 1 to 2 hstudy

Where the cost is now. The field-line vacuum solves for the potential at every boundary point, with two dense N × N matrices G and H and a dense LU (memory N², work N³). A Richardson level doubles the points per line, so N doubles and the matrices grow fourfold. At 128 lines × 400 points (N = 51 200, the grid that matches TERPSICHORE on the circular twin to 2e-5) one matrix takes 21 GB and the run was given 220 GB.

What the report proposes (your idea, prototyped in Python on 3 November): write the potential as a sum of M′ waves ei(nφ − mkθ) and require the error of the boundary equation to have no component along any of those waves (Galerkin). Then the unknowns are M′ amplitudes, the system is M′ × M′, and its entries are sums over pairs of points. Under Richardson those sums carry over: a pair of old points enters with ¼ of its previous value, and only pairs with a new point are computed. No N × N matrix is ever stored.

Read in this order:

  1. Abstract and §I (1 page): the problem and the claim.
  2. §II, eqs. (1)–(5): the point-value form, which is what calc_GH_1 does now. Careful with signs: the report was written on 3 and 4 November, before the one convention of 5 November. Its n points out of the plasma, its Hij = −wjK, and its self term Hii = 2π − ci. The code now takes the normal into the plasma (V0), which flips the signs of H and of the data together. The method does not depend on the choice.
  3. Fig. 2 and §III.A: why waves in the geometric angle need sidebands. Each exact harmonic of the torus is spread over a band of m (3 to 10 for m = 6, 9 to 24 for m = 15), because the geometric and the toroidal-coordinate poloidal angles differ by up to 0.345 rad at aspect ratio 3.
  4. §III.B–C, eqs. (6)–(11), and Fig. 3: the wave form; A is nearly tridiagonal (first neighbours 0.17 of the diagonal, a/(2R₀) = 1/6).
  5. §IV, eqs. (12)–(15), and Fig. 4: the Richardson step. Compare with §VI of your 2019 manuscript: option B there (reuse of the LU of H) is wrong as written (erratum E12); the wave form is a fourth option, closest to option C.
  6. Table I and §V: the four criteria fixed before the runs, all met: carried-over sums equal sums from scratch to 9e-16; the energy error equals the point-value form's to 3 digits; 34 waves for a 10-mode window; 51 264 points in 1.9 GB.
  7. §VI: what is not tested. This list decides whether the method can enter PB3D: the near-field rule (near pairs change when points are added), a stellarator (waves n ± Nfp, …), PB3D's own data (single waves, the case of Fig. 5(c)-like data: 3 to 4 sidebands would do), the straight-field-line angle, Fortran and MPI.

Where it meets the code. The rows are those of calc_GH_1 without the near-field rule; the data b correspond to EP of set_up_data; the energy (eq. 11) to project_response. Your 2018 \todo in the header of calc_GH (reuse of the contributions of inherited points, scaled by ½) and interlaced_vac_copy are the point-value precursor of eq. (14).

The other options, all exploration only and nothing decided (overview, section 7): a doubly periodic (θ, ζ) vacuum grid separate from the field-line grid; locally corrected trapezoidal quadrature on such a grid (Wu–Martinsson, Alpert, Duan–Rokhlin, Malhotra); a Fourier-basis vacuum as in CAS3D/NESTOR; a fast solver (GMRES with FMM or H-matrix products, or a HODLR direct solve; the condition number is only 3.5 to 3.8). The gate for any of them: the check_vac exact potentials on the circular twin and on W7-X 128 × 121 must improve and the twin eigenvalue must stay within its regression tolerance. The parked next step for the wave form (issue #4 comment of 3 November): W7-X from ~/Code/desc-vs-vmec/overnight/inputs/w7x_2015/wout_w7x.03.00llfix_99.nc, port the near-field rule, reproduce check_vac at 128 × 121, then compare wave form and point values, then the carry-over.

Appendices

Optional table and ledger

A

Eigenvalue at every commit

optionalrun Snellius, 14 November 2026

Not part of the review. For each commit that changed the compiled code, this shows whether any of nine eigenvalues changed. Use it to look up a commit, or to check a claim in the sections above that a commit "changed no number".

Open the table

What was run. Every commit from 2.47 to 9e9aba5 that changes a file compiled into PB3D (Modules/, PB3D.f90, CMakeLists.txt, cmake/, include/): 48 commits, plus tag 2.47 itself. Each was built in Release on Snellius (foss/2025a, PETSc 3.25.3, SLEPc 3.25.1) and run on the nine decks below, one process per deck, all nine at once in one 16-core job. The decks use only input variables that exist at every commit, so the same files ran unchanged on all of them. A default that changed between commits (the boundary-condition style, the diagonal style, the field-line spacing) is part of what the table shows. All decks use the poloidal flux and prim_X = 10, so the toroidal mode number is n = 10.

The number in each cell is line 1 of PB3D_out_EV_R_1.txt: the real part of the first eigenvalue, normalised to the squared Alfvén frequency, so a negative value is unstable. These are the regression decks, not converged runs. The W7-X deck has 16 field lines of 61 points each, far too coarse for a W7-X answer, but enough to show whether a commit changes the 3-D path.

Rows that are not plain builds. Tag 2.47 and a8c07b6 do not compile against PETSc 3.25: they use the PETSc 3.9 Fortran interface. So the table starts at the port, 775219a, and cannot say whether the port changed a number with respect to 2.47. Rows 775219a to 1862df0 are built with STRUMPACK-Dense 1.1.1, because the vacuum module needed it to compile until 429f003 made it optional. 429f003 has two rows: with STRUMPACK, then without it, so the vacuum system is solved by ScaLAPACK LU (pdgesv), as in every later row. The two 429f003 rows differ only in that solver.

What it shows. Between consecutive builds there are 47 steps.

  • 30 steps change none of the nine eigenvalues, bit for bit. These include every mechanical commit after the port (d4812f7, 1862df0, the module splits 8ac37d7 and 17b712c, the warning cleanup 6ce5029, the lint 17716c4), the setup_modes fix e4e3fdd (as F2 says, no fixture moves the mode window down), the consolidation fe305fd, the step-9 follow-up 329b7a4, the direct diagonal and the input vac_diag_style (e07f0fc, e027949, whose default kept the old behaviour), the four simplifications 028735c, and the switch from STRUMPACK to ScaLAPACK at 429f003. That last one shows nothing about the two solvers: at 429f003 no deck had a working vacuum yet.
  • 4 steps change numbers at rounding level only, by at most 4.5e-13 (relative): 3b99109 (step 9, the Fourier basis; the twin by 4.5e-13), 1a53f50 (the angle version of fourier2real delegates to the table version; W7-X by 4e-14), f3ebf11 (one sign convention for both vacuum styles; the twin free by 1e-13) and 225aa72 (calc_vac_res in named steps; the twin free by 1.4e-13). Hover the ≈ cells for the values.
  • 13 steps move a number, listed below the deck table. Each is a commit that the sections above describe as a change of result, and the sizes agree with them: the shear fix (F1), the factor −2π (V8), the style-4 double insertion (F6), the field-line spacing, the inward normal, B0 (F4), the near-field rule, the free-edge weight (F5), the corner term and the indirect diagonals by default. The relative change in the table is |new − old| / |old|. On that scale the shear fix moved cbm18a fixed by 7.0 %; the 6.5 % in F1 is the same change relative to the corrected value. 0d49f19 changes the Nyquist modes and B0 together. On W7-X only the B0 part acts, because that file has the same main and Nyquist mode lists (288 each): its 6.4 % is the rescaling by 1.064 of F4. On the twin (ntor 0) the old labelling was already right, so its 1.6 % is the B0 change of F4 as well. None of the nine decks shows the Nyquist fix itself.

What else the table tells you.

  • At the port every HELENA run, fixed boundary included, stops in store_vac_HEL with "Vacuum has not been implemented yet!". The vacuum had been switched off this way since 2.44 (commit 53c1c58, 18 November 2020; the message of ad2313b says the same). So the first HELENA eigenvalue in the table is at ad2313b, which skips the vacuum when the boundary is fixed.
  • Between 1d74b8f (style 2 implemented) and 212e3ec, the circular deck with a free boundary gave the fixed-boundary value to 8e-8 (+7.76499e-2, a stable mode), with the factor that the vacuum response then had. 212e3ec set the factor to −2π (its message gives the derivation and the MISHKA check), and the same deck went to −0.430.
  • The VMEC twin with a free boundary changed at six commits: −0.630 at 1d74b8f, −0.0660 after the factor (212e3ec), −0.0833 after the field-line spacing (50c9511), −0.527 after the inward normal (e3b4847), −0.519 after B0 (0d49f19), −0.449 after the near-field rule and the G diagonal (0bbda47), and −0.439 after the edge weight (4915d4b). The axisymmetric (style 2) vacuum gives −0.43679 for the HELENA version of the same equilibrium (comment of the twin regression test).

What the table cannot see. (1) Whether the port changed a number, because 2.47 does not build against PETSc 3.25. (2) The MPI fix 798fe50 (F3), because every run uses one process; F3's evidence is the comparison of 1, 2 and 4 processes. (3) The vacuum commits before style 2 worked (429f003, d6d49e6): no BC-2 deck gave an eigenvalue then, and the BC-4 deck uses only the axisymmetric vacuum. (4) Much of the 3-D vacuum on W7-X: at 16 field lines and n = 10, the W7-X mode hardly feels the vacuum. At the tip, free and fixed boundary differ by 1.8e-4, and no vacuum commit moves the free value by more than 1.2e-4. So the W7-X columns check the VMEC path with ntor > 0 more than the vacuum, and not even the Nyquist matching, because this file's two mode lists coincide (the 6.4 % at 0d49f19 is B0). A rippled twin with ntor 6 would be the deck that shows the Nyquist fix.

To run it again (from the worktree root on the Mac, with an SSH control connection open, which the scripts reuse: ssh -M -S $TMPDIR/pb3d-ssh-ctl -o ControlPersist=6h -fN tweyens@snellius.surf.nl): bash review/fingerprint/make_decks.sh <W7-X deck> writes the decks; bash review/fingerprint/submit.sh unpacks every commit on Snellius and submits review/fingerprint/fp.sbatch as one job array; bash review/fingerprint/fetch.sh copies the results back; python3 review/build_report.py rebuilds this table. The run of 14 November took 50 jobs of 16 cores for about 4 minutes each: 75 s to build, then up to 130 s for the slowest deck (the twin with 64 field lines). The binaries stay in ~/pb3d/fp/bin on Snellius, one per row, so any row can be run on another deck; rm -rf ~/pb3d/fp removes all of it.
